"""Choose the punch timeout: type it in, punch, and watch where each punch starts and ends.

  python punch_tune.py              real glove (UDP port 5005) and the webcam, full screen
  python punch_tune.py --windowed   in a normal window instead
  python punch_tune.py --simulate   a fake glove that throws punches by itself (no hardware)

Type in THIS TERMINAL, then press Enter (F11 leaves full screen so you can see the terminal):
  350               set the timeout to 350 ms (a punch ends at the timeout, or earlier if it stops)
  start_g 3         change any other punch setting the same way (show lists them)
  show              print the current settings
  save              save them to punch_config.json, which capture, training and live play all use
  test 10 60 jab    set up a timed test: 10 jabs in 60 seconds (any number, time and punch; the punch
                    is optional). It waits until you have calibrated (C) and you press "." to start.
                    Afterwards it says how many punches it found with the current timeout and, once a
                    model is trained, how many it classified as jabs, and compares other timeouts.
  q                 quit
Keys that work in any window, no Enter needed:
  .                 start the timed test, and pause or resume it at any time
  F11               full screen on or off
The camera window shows the glove's acceleration, a green line where each punch started, and a blue
(stopped) or orange (timed out) line where it ended. Hold still for a moment first, so gravity is known.

Change the timeout BEFORE recording training data, or retrain afterwards, because the model learns from
punches cut at this timeout.
"""
import argparse
import threading
import time

import punch_segment
import punch_session as ps

GREEN, BLUE, ORANGE, RED, GREY, YELLOW = (0, 220, 0), (255, 170, 0), (0, 150, 255), (0, 0, 255), (180, 180, 180), (0, 255, 255)
COUNTDOWN_S = 3.0
GRACE_S = 0.7   # after the time runs out, wait this long so a punch in progress can finish
COMPARE_TIMEOUTS_MS = (250, 300, 350, 400, 450, 500, 600)
KINDS = {"jab": "JAB", "jabs": "JAB", "hook": "HOOK", "hooks": "HOOK", "uppercut": "UPPERCUT", "uppercuts": "UPPERCUT"}


def score_test(imu, pose, intervals, settings, classifier=None, kind=None, timeouts_ms=COMPARE_TIMEOUTS_MS):
    """Cut a recorded test at each timeout, counting punches that started inside the active intervals
    (the test minus any pauses). Returns [(timeout_ms, found, Counter of labels, unsure)]."""
    from collections import Counter
    rows = []
    for ms in sorted(set(list(timeouts_ms) + [round(1000 * settings.timeout_s)])):
        s = punch_segment.SegmentSettings.from_dict({**settings.to_dict(), "timeout_s": ms / 1000})
        segs = [g for g in punch_segment.find_segments(imu["t"], imu["accel"], imu["gyro"], s)
                if g.reason != "gap" and any(a <= g.start_t <= b for a, b in intervals)]
        labels, unsure = Counter(), 0
        if classifier is not None:
            for g in segs:
                label, conf = classifier.classify(imu, pose, g, s.pre_s)
                if label is None or conf < classifier.min_confidence:
                    unsure += 1
                else:
                    labels[label] += 1
        rows.append((ms, len(segs), labels, unsure))
    return rows


class Tuner:
    def __init__(self, sensors, config):
        self.sensors, self.config = sensors, config
        self.marks = []          # (t, colour) for the trace
        self.active = None       # Segment in progress
        self.last = None         # last finished Segment
        self.count = 0
        self.quit = False
        self.calibrated = False  # set when pose_tracker calibrates (C, then a 5 s countdown)
        self.message, self.message_t = "", 0.0
        self.test = None         # the timed test, if one is set up
        self.report, self.report_t = [], 0.0
        self.classifier = ps.Classifier() if ps.Classifier.exists() else None

    # --- typed commands ---
    def command(self, line):
        line = line.strip().lstrip("﻿").replace(".", " ").strip() if line.strip(" .") else line.strip()
        if line in (".", ""):
            if line == ".":
                self.toggle_test()  # "." then Enter also works, for terminals where the key is not seen
            return
        settings = self.sensors.settings.to_dict()
        word, *rest = line.replace("=", " ").split()
        try:
            if word in ("q", "quit", "exit"):
                self.quit = True
            elif word == "show":
                for k, v in settings.items():
                    print(f"  {k} = {v:g}")
            elif word == "save":
                ps.save_config(self.config)
                self.say(f"saved to {ps.CONFIG_PATH}")
            elif word == "test":
                self.set_up_test(rest)
            elif word in settings and rest:
                settings[word] = float(rest[0])
                self.apply(settings, f"{word} = {float(rest[0]):g}")
            else:
                value = float(word)
                ms = value if value > 10 else value * 1000  # "350" or "0.35"
                settings["timeout_s"] = ms / 1000
                self.apply(settings, f"timeout = {ms:.0f} ms")
        except ValueError:
            self.say(f"did not understand {line!r}; type a timeout in ms, a setting name and value, show, save or q")

    # --- timed test ---
    def set_up_test(self, words):
        """test [punches] [seconds] [jab|hook|uppercut]"""
        numbers = [float(w) for w in words if w.replace(".", "", 1).isdigit()]
        kind = next((KINDS[w.lower()] for w in words if w.lower() in KINDS), None)
        n = int(numbers[0]) if numbers else 10
        seconds = numbers[1] if len(numbers) > 1 else 60.0
        if seconds > 120:
            raise ValueError("a test can be at most 120 s")
        what = f"{n} {kind + 'S' if kind else 'punches'}"
        # state: waiting -> countdown -> running <-> paused (-> countdown) ... -> finishing
        self.test = {"n": n, "seconds": seconds, "left": seconds, "kind": kind, "what": what, "state": "waiting",
                     "intervals": [], "seen": 0}
        self.say(f"TEST SET UP: {what} in {seconds:g} s. Calibrate with C if you have not, then press . to start.")

    def not_ready_reason(self):
        if not self.sensors.glove_ok():
            return "no glove data"
        if not self.sensors.segmenter.ready:
            return "hold the glove still for a moment"
        if not self.calibrated:
            return "press C to calibrate first (stand in guard)"
        return None

    def toggle_test(self):
        test, now = self.test, time.time()
        if test is None:
            self.say("no test set up: type e.g. test 10 60 jab in the terminal first")
        elif test["state"] in ("waiting", "paused"):
            reason = self.not_ready_reason()
            if reason:
                self.say(f"cannot start yet: {reason}")
                return
            test["state"], test["go_wall"] = "countdown", now + COUNTDOWN_S
        elif test["state"] == "countdown":
            test["state"] = "paused" if test["intervals"] else "waiting"
            self.say("countdown cancelled")
        elif test["state"] == "running":
            test["intervals"].append((test["run_t"], self.sensors.latest_imu_t() or test["run_t"]))
            test["left"] -= now - test["run_wall"]
            test["state"] = "paused"
            self.say(f"PAUSED with {test['left']:.0f} s left. Punches now do not count. Press . to resume.")

    def update_test(self):
        test, now = self.test, time.time()
        if test is None:
            return
        if test["state"] == "countdown" and now >= test["go_wall"]:
            test["state"], test["run_wall"] = "running", now
            test["run_t"] = self.sensors.latest_imu_t() or 0.0
            self.say("GO!")
        elif test["state"] == "running" and now - test["run_wall"] >= test["left"]:
            test["intervals"].append((test["run_t"], self.sensors.latest_imu_t() or test["run_t"]))
            test["state"], test["finish_wall"] = "finishing", now + GRACE_S
        elif test["state"] == "finishing" and now >= test["finish_wall"]:
            self.test = None
            threading.Thread(target=self.finish_test, args=(test,), daemon=True).start()

    def counts_for_test(self, start_t):
        test = self.test
        if not test:
            return False
        if test["state"] == "running" and start_t >= test["run_t"]:
            return True
        return any(a <= start_t <= b for a, b in test["intervals"])

    def finish_test(self, test):
        settings = self.sensors.settings
        intervals = test["intervals"]
        imu, pose = self.sensors.window(intervals[0][0] - 1.0, intervals[-1][1] + GRACE_S)
        clf = self.classifier
        rows = score_test(imu, pose, intervals, settings, clf, test["kind"])
        current = round(1000 * settings.timeout_s)
        lines = [f"TEST RESULT: asked for {test['what']} in {test['seconds']:g} s"]
        if clf is None:
            lines.append("(no trained model yet, so punches are counted but not classified)")
        elif round(1000 * clf.segment.timeout_s) != current:
            lines.append(f"(the model was trained at {1000 * clf.segment.timeout_s:.0f} ms; other timeouts are"
                         " only a rough guide until you retrain)")
        best, best_score = None, -1
        for ms, found, labels, unsure in rows:
            text = f"{ms:4d} ms: found {found}/{test['n']}"
            score = found
            if clf is not None:
                if test["kind"]:
                    score = labels.get(test["kind"], 0)
                    text += f", classified as {test['kind']}: {score}/{test['n']}"
                others = ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in sorted(labels.items()) if k != test["kind"])
                text += (f" | other: {others}" if others else "") + (f" | unsure {unsure}" if unsure else "")
            if ms == current:
                text += " <- current"
            if score > best_score:  # the shortest timeout with the best score, as rows go up in time
                best, best_score = text, score
            lines.append(text)
        for line in lines:
            print(line)
        # the camera window has room for a short version; the full table is in the terminal
        current_line = next(l for l in lines if "<- current" in l)
        short = [lines[0], "now:  " + current_line.strip()]
        if best != current_line:
            short.append("best: " + best.strip())
        short.append("(full table in the terminal)")
        self.report, self.report_t = short, time.time()

    def apply(self, settings, what):
        new = punch_segment.SegmentSettings.from_dict(settings)
        self.config["segment"] = new
        self.sensors.set_settings(new)
        self.say(what + "  (type save to keep it)")

    def say(self, text):
        print(text)
        self.message, self.message_t = text, time.time()

    def read_terminal(self):
        while not self.quit:
            try:
                self.command(input())
            except EOFError:
                return

    # --- camera loop callbacks ---
    def on_calibrated(self):
        self.calibrated = True
        if self.test and self.test["state"] == "waiting":
            self.say("calibrated. Press . to start the test")

    def on_frame(self, keys=None):
        while not self.sensors.events.empty():
            kind, value = self.sensors.events.get()
            if kind == "start":
                self.active = value
                self.marks.append((value.start_t, GREEN))
            elif kind == "end":
                self.active, self.last = None, value
                self.count += 1
                self.marks.append((value.end_t, BLUE if value.reason == "decel" else ORANGE))
                if self.counts_for_test(value.start_t):
                    self.test["seen"] += 1
                print(f"punch {self.count}: {1000 * value.duration:.0f} ms, ended by "
                      f"{'stopping' if value.reason == 'decel' else value.reason}, peak {value.peak_g:.1f} g")
        self.marks = self.marks[-40:]
        if keys is not None:
            if keys.period():
                self.toggle_test()
            keys.poll_fullscreen()
        self.update_test()
        return self.quit

    def on_draw(self, frame):
        h, w = frame.shape[:2]
        s = self.sensors.settings
        now_t, now = self.sensors.latest_imu_t() or 0.0, time.time()
        top = 150
        if not self.sensors.glove_ok():
            ps.put(frame, "NO GLOVE DATA (is it on, and on the same WiFi?)", top, RED, 0.7)
        elif not self.sensors.segmenter.ready:
            ps.put(frame, "hold the glove still for a moment...", top, ORANGE, 0.7)
        elif self.active is not None:
            ps.put(frame, f"PUNCH STARTED  {1000 * (now_t - self.active.start_t):.0f} ms", top, GREEN, 1.0, thick=3)
        elif self.last is not None:
            how = "STOPPED" if self.last.reason == "decel" else "TIMED OUT" if self.last.reason == "timeout" else "DATA GAP"
            ps.put(frame, f"PUNCH ENDED: {how} after {1000 * self.last.duration:.0f} ms",
                   top, BLUE if self.last.reason == "decel" else ORANGE, 0.8)
        ps.put(frame, f"timeout {1000 * s.timeout_s:.0f} ms | start {s.start_g:g} g | brake {s.decel_g:g} g | punches {self.count}",
               top + 28, GREY, 0.55)
        if now - self.message_t < 3:
            ps.put(frame, self.message[:75], top + 52, YELLOW, 0.5)

        test, row = self.test, top + 85
        if test:
            state = test["state"]
            if state == "waiting":
                reason = self.not_ready_reason()
                text, colour = f"TEST {test['what']}: " + (reason if reason else "press . to start"), (ORANGE if reason else YELLOW)
            elif state == "countdown":
                text, colour = f"TEST {test['what']}: starting in {max(0.0, test['go_wall'] - now):.0f}", YELLOW
            elif state == "running":
                left = max(0.0, test["left"] - (now - test["run_wall"]))
                text, colour = f"TEST {test['what']}: {left:.0f} s left  seen {test['seen']}  (. pauses)", GREEN
            elif state == "paused":
                text, colour = f"TEST PAUSED: {test['left']:.0f} s left  seen {test['seen']}  (. resumes)", ORANGE
            else:
                text, colour = "TEST: finishing...", YELLOW
            ps.put(frame, text, row, colour, 0.75, thick=2)
        elif self.report and now - self.report_t < 30:
            for i, line in enumerate(self.report):
                ps.put(frame, line[:80], row + 20 * i, YELLOW if line.startswith(("now", "best")) else GREY, 0.45, thick=1)

        # The trace sits above the bottom strip, where pose_tracker shows calibration messages.
        trace_bottom = h - ps.TEXT_BOTTOM - 22
        ps.put(frame, "terminal: type a timeout in ms + Enter  |  . test start/pause  |  F11 full screen",
               h - ps.TEXT_BOTTOM, GREY, 0.45, thick=1)
        times, values = self.sensors.recent_linear_g(3.0)
        ps.draw_trace(frame, times, values, now_t, 3.0, 12.0, self.marks,
                      origin=(10, trace_bottom - 90), size=(w - 20, 90), threshold_g=s.start_g)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use a fake glove (no hardware)")
    parser.add_argument("--windowed", action="store_true", help="start in a normal window, not full screen")
    parser.add_argument("--camera", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=5005, help="UDP port the glove sends to")
    parser.add_argument("--max-seconds", type=float, help="stop by itself (for testing)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    config = ps.load_config()
    sensors = ps.LiveSensors(config["segment"], seconds=150, simulate=args.simulate, port=args.port)  # room for a 2-minute test
    tuner = Tuner(sensors, config)
    if tuner.classifier:
        print(f"Model loaded (trained {tuner.classifier.info['trained_at']}), so timed tests classify punches.")
    threading.Thread(target=tuner.read_terminal, daemon=True).start()
    print(__doc__.split("Type in")[1].split("Change the")[0].strip())
    keys = ps.ToolKeys(fullscreen=not args.windowed)
    started = time.time()

    def on_frame():
        return tuner.on_frame(keys) or bool(args.max_seconds and time.time() - started > args.max_seconds)

    import pose_tracker
    try:
        pose_tracker.main(on_frame=on_frame, on_draw=tuner.on_draw, on_calibrated=tuner.on_calibrated,
                          camera_index=args.camera, fullscreen=not args.windowed, **sensors.pose_callbacks())
    finally:
        sensors.close()
    print(f"{tuner.count} punches seen. Settings are only kept if you typed save.")
    return tuner


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use a fake glove (no hardware)")
    parser.add_argument("--windowed", action="store_true", help="start in a normal window, not full screen")
    parser.add_argument("--camera", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=5005, help="UDP port the glove sends to")
    parser.add_argument("--max-seconds", type=float, help="stop by itself (for testing)")

    from collections import Counter

"""Choose the punch timeout: type it in, punch, and watch where each punch starts and ends.

  python punch_tune.py              real glove (UDP port 5005) and the webcam, full screen
  python punch_tune.py --windowed   in a normal window instead
  python punch_tune.py --simulate   a fake glove that throws punches by itself (no hardware)

Type in THIS TERMINAL, then press Enter (F11 leaves full screen so you can see the terminal):
  350               set the timeout to 350 ms (a punch ends at the timeout, or earlier if it stops)
  start_g 3         change any other punch setting the same way (show lists them)
  show              print the current settings
  save              save them to punch_config.json, which capture, training and live play all use
  test 10 60 jab    set up a timed test: 10 jabs in 60 seconds (any number, time and punch; the punch
                    is optional). It waits until you have calibrated (C) and you press "." to start.
                    Afterwards it says how many punches it found with the current timeout and, once a
                    model is trained, how many it classified as jabs, and compares other timeouts.
  q                 quit
Keys that work in any window, no Enter needed:
  .                 start the timed test, and pause or resume it at any time
  F11               full screen on or off
The camera window shows the glove's acceleration, a green line where each punch started, and a blue
(stopped) or orange (timed out) line where it ended. Hold still for a moment first, so gravity is known.

Change the timeout BEFORE recording training data, or retrain afterwards, because the model learns from
punches cut at this timeout.
"""
import argparse
import threading
import time

import punch_segment
import punch_session as ps

GREEN, BLUE, ORANGE, RED, GREY, YELLOW = (0, 220, 0), (255, 170, 0), (0, 150, 255), (0, 0, 255), (180, 180, 180), (0, 255, 255)
COUNTDOWN_S = 3.0
GRACE_S = 0.7   # after the time runs out, wait this long so a punch in progress can finish
COMPARE_TIMEOUTS_MS = (250, 300, 350, 400, 450, 500, 600)
KINDS = {"jab": "JAB", "jabs": "JAB", "hook": "HOOK", "hooks": "HOOK", "uppercut": "UPPERCUT", "uppercuts": "UPPERCUT"}


def score_test(imu, pose, intervals, settings, classifier=None, kind=None, timeouts_ms=COMPARE_TIMEOUTS_MS):
    """Cut a recorded test at each timeout, counting punches that started inside the active intervals
    (the test minus any pauses). Returns [(timeout_ms, found, Counter of labels, unsure)]."""
    from collections import Counter
    rows = []
    for ms in sorted(set(list(timeouts_ms) + [round(1000 * settings.timeout_s)])):
        s = punch_segment.SegmentSettings.from_dict({**settings.to_dict(), "timeout_s": ms / 1000})
        segs = [g for g in punch_segment.find_segments(imu["t"], imu["accel"], imu["gyro"], s)
                if g.reason != "gap" and any(a <= g.start_t <= b for a, b in intervals)]
        labels, unsure = Counter(), 0
        if classifier is not None:
            for g in segs:
                label, conf = classifier.classify(imu, pose, g, s.pre_s)
                if label is None or conf < classifier.min_confidence:
                    unsure += 1
                else:
                    labels[label] += 1
        rows.append((ms, len(segs), labels, unsure))
    return rows


class Tuner:
    def __init__(self, sensors, config):
        self.sensors, self.config = sensors, config
        self.marks = []          # (t, colour) for the trace
        self.active = None       # Segment in progress
        self.last = None         # last finished Segment
        self.count = 0
        self.quit = False
        self.calibrated = False  # set when pose_tracker calibrates (C, then a 5 s countdown)
        self.message, self.message_t = "", 0.0
        self.test = None         # the timed test, if one is set up
        self.report, self.report_t = [], 0.0
        self.classifier = ps.Classifier() if ps.Classifier.exists() else None

    # --- typed commands ---
    def command(self, line):
        line = line.strip().lstrip("\ufeff").replace(".", " ").strip() if line.strip(" .") else line.strip()
        if line in (".", ""):
            if line == ".":
                self.toggle_test()  # "." then Enter also works, for terminals where the key is not seen
            return
        settings = self.sensors.settings.to_dict()
        word, *rest = line.replace("=", " ").split()
        try:
            if word in ("q", "quit", "exit"):
                self.quit = True
            elif word == "show":
                for k, v in settings.items():
                    print(f"  {k} = {v:g}")
            elif word == "save":
                ps.save_config(self.config)
                self.say(f"saved to {ps.CONFIG_PATH}")
            elif word == "test":
                self.set_up_test(rest)
            elif word in settings and rest:
                settings[word] = float(rest[0])
                self.apply(settings, f"{word} = {float(rest[0]):g}")
            else:
                value = float(word)
                ms = value if value > 10 else value * 1000  # "350" or "0.35"
                settings["timeout_s"] = ms / 1000
                self.apply(settings, f"timeout = {ms:.0f} ms")
        except ValueError:
            self.say(f"did not understand {line!r}; type a timeout in ms, a setting name and value, show, save or q")

    # --- timed test ---
    def set_up_test(self, words):
        """test [punches] [seconds] [jab|hook|uppercut]"""
        numbers = [float(w) for w in words if w.replace(".", "", 1).isdigit()]
        kind = next((KINDS[w.lower()] for w in words if w.lower() in KINDS), None)
        n = int(numbers[0]) if numbers else 10
        seconds = numbers[1] if len(numbers) > 1 else 60.0
        if seconds > 120:
            raise ValueError("a test can be at most 120 s")
        what = f"{n} {kind + 'S' if kind else 'punches'}"
        # state: waiting -> countdown -> running <-> paused (-> countdown) ... -> finishing
        self.test = {"n": n, "seconds": seconds, "left": seconds, "kind": kind, "what": what, "state": "waiting",
                     "intervals": [], "seen": 0}
        self.say(f"TEST SET UP: {what} in {seconds:g} s. Calibrate with C if you have not, then press . to start.")

    def not_ready_reason(self):
        if not self.sensors.glove_ok():
            return "no glove data"
        if not self.sensors.segmenter.ready:
            return "hold the glove still for a moment"
        if not self.calibrated:
            return "press C to calibrate first (stand in guard)"
        return None

    def toggle_test(self):
        test, now = self.test, time.time()
        if test is None:
            self.say("no test set up: type e.g. test 10 60 jab in the terminal first")
        elif test["state"] in ("waiting", "paused"):
            reason = self.not_ready_reason()
            if reason:
                self.say(f"cannot start yet: {reason}")
                return
            test["state"], test["go_wall"] = "countdown", now + COUNTDOWN_S
        elif test["state"] == "countdown":
            test["state"] = "paused" if test["intervals"] else "waiting"
            self.say("countdown cancelled")
        elif test["state"] == "running":
            test["intervals"].append((test["run_t"], self.sensors.latest_imu_t() or test["run_t"]))
            test["left"] -= now - test["run_wall"]
            test["state"] = "paused"
            self.say(f"PAUSED with {test['left']:.0f} s left. Punches now do not count. Press . to resume.")

    def update_test(self):
        test, now = self.test, time.time()
        if test is None:
            return
        if test["state"] == "countdown" and now >= test["go_wall"]:
            test["state"], test["run_wall"] = "running", now
            test["run_t"] = self.sensors.latest_imu_t() or 0.0
            self.say("GO!")
        elif test["state"] == "running" and now - test["run_wall"] >= test["left"]:
            test["intervals"].append((test["run_t"], self.sensors.latest_imu_t() or test["run_t"]))
            test["state"], test["finish_wall"] = "finishing", now + GRACE_S
        elif test["state"] == "finishing" and now >= test["finish_wall"]:
            self.test = None
            threading.Thread(target=self.finish_test, args=(test,), daemon=True).start()

    def counts_for_test(self, start_t):
        test = self.test
        if not test:
            return False
        if test["state"] == "running" and start_t >= test["run_t"]:
            return True
        return any(a <= start_t <= b for a, b in test["intervals"])

    def finish_test(self, test):
        settings = self.sensors.settings
        intervals = test["intervals"]
        imu, pose = self.sensors.window(intervals[0][0] - 1.0, intervals[-1][1] + GRACE_S)
        clf = self.classifier
        rows = score_test(imu, pose, intervals, settings, clf, test["kind"])
        current = round(1000 * settings.timeout_s)
        lines = [f"TEST RESULT: asked for {test['what']} in {test['seconds']:g} s"]
        if clf is None:
            lines.append("(no trained model yet, so punches are counted but not classified)")
        elif round(1000 * clf.segment.timeout_s) != current:
            lines.append(f"(the model was trained at {1000 * clf.segment.timeout_s:.0f} ms; other timeouts are"
                         " only a rough guide until you retrain)")
        best, best_score = None, -1
        for ms, found, labels, unsure in rows:
            text = f"{ms:4d} ms: found {found}/{test['n']}"
            score = found
            if clf is not None:
                if test["kind"]:
                    score = labels.get(test["kind"], 0)
                    text += f", classified as {test['kind']}: {score}/{test['n']}"
                others = ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in sorted(labels.items()) if k != test["kind"])
                text += (f" | other: {others}" if others else "") + (f" | unsure {unsure}" if unsure else "")
            if ms == current:
                text += " <- current"
            if score > best_score:  # the shortest timeout with the best score, as rows go up in time
                best, best_score = text, score
            lines.append(text)
        for line in lines:
            print(line)
        # the camera window has room for a short version; the full table is in the terminal
        current_line = next(l for l in lines if "<- current" in l)
        short = [lines[0], "now:  " + current_line.strip()]
        if best != current_line:
            short.append("best: " + best.strip())
        short.append("(full table in the terminal)")
        self.report, self.report_t = short, time.time()

    def apply(self, settings, what):
        new = punch_segment.SegmentSettings.from_dict(settings)
        self.config["segment"] = new
        self.sensors.set_settings(new)
        self.say(what + "  (type save to keep it)")

    def say(self, text):
        print(text)
        self.message, self.message_t = text, time.time()

    def read_terminal(self):
        while not self.quit:
            try:
                self.command(input())
            except EOFError:
                return

    # --- camera loop callbacks ---
    def on_calibrated(self):
        self.calibrated = True
        if self.test and self.test["state"] == "waiting":
            self.say("calibrated. Press . to start the test")

    def on_frame(self, keys=None):
        while not self.sensors.events.empty():
            kind, value = self.sensors.events.get()
            if kind == "start":
                self.active = value
                self.marks.append((value.start_t, GREEN))
            elif kind == "end":
                self.active, self.last = None, value
                self.count += 1
                self.marks.append((value.end_t, BLUE if value.reason == "decel" else ORANGE))
                if self.counts_for_test(value.start_t):
                    self.test["seen"] += 1
                print(f"punch {self.count}: {1000 * value.duration:.0f} ms, ended by "
                      f"{'stopping' if value.reason == 'decel' else value.reason}, peak {value.peak_g:.1f} g")
        self.marks = self.marks[-40:]
        if keys is not None:
            if keys.period():
                self.toggle_test()
            keys.poll_fullscreen()
        self.update_test()
        return self.quit

    def on_draw(self, frame):
        h, w = frame.shape[:2]
        s = self.sensors.settings
        now_t, now = self.sensors.latest_imu_t() or 0.0, time.time()
        top = 150
        if not self.sensors.glove_ok():
            ps.put(frame, "NO GLOVE DATA (is it on, and on the same WiFi?)", top, RED, 0.7)
        elif not self.sensors.segmenter.ready:
            ps.put(frame, "hold the glove still for a moment...", top, ORANGE, 0.7)
        elif self.active is not None:
            ps.put(frame, f"PUNCH STARTED  {1000 * (now_t - self.active.start_t):.0f} ms", top, GREEN, 1.0, thick=3)
        elif self.last is not None:
            how = "STOPPED" if self.last.reason == "decel" else "TIMED OUT" if self.last.reason == "timeout" else "DATA GAP"
            ps.put(frame, f"PUNCH ENDED: {how} after {1000 * self.last.duration:.0f} ms",
                   top, BLUE if self.last.reason == "decel" else ORANGE, 0.8)
        ps.put(frame, f"timeout {1000 * s.timeout_s:.0f} ms | start {s.start_g:g} g | brake {s.decel_g:g} g | punches {self.count}",
               top + 28, GREY, 0.55)
        if now - self.message_t < 3:
            ps.put(frame, self.message[:75], top + 52, YELLOW, 0.5)

        test, row = self.test, top + 85
        if test:
            state = test["state"]
            if state == "waiting":
                reason = self.not_ready_reason()
                text, colour = f"TEST {test['what']}: " + (reason if reason else "press . to start"), (ORANGE if reason else YELLOW)
            elif state == "countdown":
                text, colour = f"TEST {test['what']}: starting in {max(0.0, test['go_wall'] - now):.0f}", YELLOW
            elif state == "running":
                left = max(0.0, test["left"] - (now - test["run_wall"]))
                text, colour = f"TEST {test['what']}: {left:.0f} s left  seen {test['seen']}  (. pauses)", GREEN
            elif state == "paused":
                text, colour = f"TEST PAUSED: {test['left']:.0f} s left  seen {test['seen']}  (. resumes)", ORANGE
            else:
                text, colour = "TEST: finishing...", YELLOW
            ps.put(frame, text, row, colour, 0.75, thick=2)
        elif self.report and now - self.report_t < 30:
            for i, line in enumerate(self.report):
                ps.put(frame, line[:80], row + 20 * i, YELLOW if line.startswith(("now", "best")) else GREY, 0.45, thick=1)

        # The trace sits above the bottom strip, where pose_tracker shows calibration messages.
        trace_bottom = h - ps.TEXT_BOTTOM - 22
        ps.put(frame, "terminal: type a timeout in ms + Enter  |  . test start/pause  |  F11 full screen",
               h - ps.TEXT_BOTTOM, GREY, 0.45, thick=1)
        times, values = self.sensors.recent_linear_g(3.0)
        ps.draw_trace(frame, times, values, now_t, 3.0, 12.0, self.marks,
                      origin=(10, trace_bottom - 90), size=(w - 20, 90), threshold_g=s.start_g)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use a fake glove (no hardware)")
    parser.add_argument("--windowed", action="store_true", help="start in a normal window, not full screen")
    parser.add_argument("--camera", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=5005, help="UDP port the glove sends to")
    parser.add_argument("--max-seconds", type=float, help="stop by itself (for testing)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    config = ps.load_config()
    sensors = ps.LiveSensors(config["segment"], seconds=150, simulate=args.simulate, port=args.port)  # room for a 2-minute test
    tuner = Tuner(sensors, config)
    if tuner.classifier:
        print(f"Model loaded (trained {tuner.classifier.info['trained_at']}), so timed tests classify punches.")
    threading.Thread(target=tuner.read_terminal, daemon=True).start()
    print(__doc__.split("Type in")[1].split("Change the")[0].strip())
    keys = ps.ToolKeys(fullscreen=not args.windowed)
    started = time.time()

    def on_frame():
        return tuner.on_frame(keys) or bool(args.max_seconds and time.time() - started > args.max_seconds)

    import pose_tracker
    try:
        pose_tracker.main(on_frame=on_frame, on_draw=tuner.on_draw, on_calibrated=tuner.on_calibrated,
                          camera_index=args.camera, fullscreen=not args.windowed, **sensors.pose_callbacks())
    finally:

195	    def __init__(self, *args):
196	        super().__init__(*args)
197	        self.phase, self.phase_end, self.prompt = "announce", time.time() + ANNOUNCE_S, None
198	        self.prompts_done, self.paused = 0, False
199	        self.windows = []        # (label, start, end) of every punch prompt, to tell punches from NONE
200	        self.pending = []        # (label, start, end) prompts waiting for their data
201	        self.free = []           # (start, end) of MOVE, DON'T PUNCH rounds
202	        self.none_pending = []   # Segments to save as NONE once their data has arrived
203	
204	    def command(self, word):
205	        if word == "p":
206	            self.paused = not self.paused
207	            if not self.paused:
208	                self.phase, self.phase_end = "announce", time.time() + ANNOUNCE_S
209	            self.say("PAUSED (type p to carry on)" if self.paused else "carrying on", ORANGE)
210	        else:
211	            super().command(word)

213	    def next_prompt(self):
214	        left = self.remaining()
215	        for label, _, _ in self.pending:  # prompts still waiting for their data count as asked
216	            left[label] -= 1
217	        bag = [k for k, n in left.items() for _ in range(n)]
218	        return random.choice(bag) if bag else None
219	
220	    def advance(self, now):
221	        if self.phase in ("announce", "go", "free"):
222	            if self.phase == "free":
223	                self.free.append((self.free_start, now))
224	            if self.prompts_done and self.prompts_done % FREE_EVERY == 0 and self.phase == "go":
225	                self.phase, self.phase_end, self.free_start = "free", now + FREE_S, now
226	                beep("FREE")

228	            self.prompt = self.next_prompt()
229	            if self.prompt is None:
230	                self.phase = "done"
231	                self.say("ALL DONE. Train with python punch_train.py", GREEN)
232	                return
233	            self.phase, self.phase_end = "rest", now + REST_S
234	        elif self.phase == "rest":
235	            self.phase, self.phase_end = "go", now + GO_S
236	            self.windows.append((self.prompt, now, now + GO_S))
237	            self.pending.append((self.prompt, now, now + GO_S))
238	            self.prompts_done += 1
239	            beep(self.prompt)

241	    def in_prompt_window(self, t):
242	        return any(start - 0.2 <= t <= end + LATE_S for _, start, end in self.windows)

245	        now = time.time()
246	        while not self.sensors.events.empty():
247	            kind, value = self.sensors.events.get()
248	            if kind == "end" and value.reason != "gap" and not self.in_prompt_window(value.start_t):
249	                self.none_pending.append(value)

251	            self.advance(now)
252	        latest = self.sensors.latest_imu_t() or 0.0
253	        wait = self.sensors.settings.timeout_s + POST_S
254	        for item in [p for p in self.pending if latest >= p[2] + wait]:
255	            self.pending.remove(item)
256	            label, start, end = item
257	            seg = self.save_block(label, start, end, quiet=True)

9	Throw that punch once, then return to guard. The strongest punch in the next 1.6 s gets that label.
10	Anything the punch finder catches while you are NOT being prompted is saved as NONE, a "not a punch"
11	example. Every 15 prompts there is a "MOVE, DON'T PUNCH" round: shuffle, adjust your guard, feint,
12	bob. These NONE examples teach the model to press nothing for movement that is not a punch.
13	Your hands stay as they will be in play, so the training punches match the game.
14	
15	BUTTON MODE (--button). Hold the glove button, throw one punch, release. Collects no NONE examples.

20	  j/h/u   button mode only: switch to JAB / HOOK / UPPERCUT
21	  q       quit (everything saved so far is kept); q in the camera window also works

191	class PromptedCapture(Capture):
192	    MODE = "prompted"
193	    HELP = "type p to pause, x to undo, q to quit"
194	
195	    def __init__(self, *args):
196	        super().__init__(*args)
197	        self.phase, self.phase_end, self.prompt = "announce", time.time() + ANNOUNCE_S, None
198	        self.prompts_done, self.paused = 0, False
199	        self.windows = []        # (label, start, end) of every punch prompt, to tell punches from NONE
200	        self.pending = []        # (label, start, end) prompts waiting for their data
201	        self.free = []           # (start, end) of MOVE, DON'T PUNCH rounds
202	        self.none_pending = []   # Segments to save as NONE once their data has arrived
203	
204	    def command(self, word):
205	        if word == "p":
206	            self.paused = not self.paused
207	            if not self.paused:
208	                self.phase, self.phase_end = "announce", time.time() + ANNOUNCE_S
209	            self.say("PAUSED (type p to carry on)" if self.paused else "carrying on", ORANGE)
210	        else:
211	            super().command(word)
212	
213	    def next_prompt(self):
214	        left = self.remaining()
215	        for label, _, _ in self.pending:  # prompts still waiting for their data count as asked
216	            left[label] -= 1
217	        bag = [k for k, n in left.items() for _ in range(n)]
218	        return random.choice(bag) if bag else None
219	
220	    def advance(self, now):
221	        if self.phase in ("announce", "go", "free"):
222	            if self.phase == "free":
223	                self.free.append((self.free_start, now))
224	            if self.prompts_done and self.prompts_done % FREE_EVERY == 0 and self.phase == "go":
225	                self.phase, self.phase_end, self.free_start = "free", now + FREE_S, now
226	                beep("FREE")
227	                return
228	            self.prompt = self.next_prompt()
229	            if self.prompt is None:
230	                self.phase = "done"
231	                self.say("ALL DONE. Train with python punch_train.py", GREEN)
232	                return
233	            self.phase, self.phase_end = "rest", now + REST_S
234	        elif self.phase == "rest":
235	            self.phase, self.phase_end = "go", now + GO_S
236	            self.windows.append((self.prompt, now, now + GO_S))
237	            self.pending.append((self.prompt, now, now + GO_S))
238	            self.prompts_done += 1
239	            beep(self.prompt)
240	
241	    def in_prompt_window(self, t):
242	        return any(start - 0.2 <= t <= end + LATE_S for _, start, end in self.windows)
243	
244	    def on_frame(self):
245	        now = time.time()
246	        while not self.sensors.events.empty():
247	            kind, value = self.sensors.events.get()
248	            if kind == "end" and value.reason != "gap" and not self.in_prompt_window(value.start_t):
249	                self.none_pending.append(value)
250	        if not self.paused and self.phase != "done" and now >= self.phase_end:
251	            self.advance(now)
252	        latest = self.sensors.latest_imu_t() or 0.0
253	        wait = self.sensors.settings.timeout_s + POST_S
254	        for item in [p for p in self.pending if latest >= p[2] + wait]:
255	            self.pending.remove(item)
256	            label, start, end = item
257	            seg = self.save_block(label, start, end, quiet=True)
258	            if seg is None:
259	                self.say(f"MISSED {label}: no punch in the 1.6 s after the beep. It will come up again.", RED)
260	            else:
261	                self.say(f"saved {label} {self.counts[label]}/{self.target}: {1000 * seg.duration:.0f} ms, "
262	                         f"{seg.peak_g:.1f} g", GREEN)
263	        for seg in [s for s in self.none_pending if latest >= s.end_t + POST_S]:
264	            self.none_pending.remove(seg)
265	            if self.save_block(NONE, seg.start_t - 0.05, seg.start_t + 0.05, quiet=True) is not None:
266	                where = "while moving freely" if any(a <= seg.start_t <= b for a, b in self.free) or self.phase == "free" else "between prompts"
267	                print(f"saved NONE {self.counts[NONE]} (a movement {where})")
268	        return self.quit or self.phase == "done" and not self.pending and not self.none_pending

283	        elif self.phase == "free":

286	        elif self.phase == "done":

292	def draw_common(cap, frame, row, button_held):
293	    h = frame.shape[0]
294	    totals = "  ".join(f"{k} {cap.counts.get(k, 0)}/{cap.target}" for k in ps.LABELS) + f"  NONE {cap.counts.get(NONE, 0)}"

324

"""Play a boxing game: the trained model classifies each left-hand punch and presses its key.

  python punch_live.py                dry run: prints the keys it would press, presses nothing
  python punch_live.py --live         really presses keys in whichever window has focus
  python punch_live.py --simulate     fake glove (no hardware), to try the tool

Punches (glove and camera together, via the model from punch_train.py): JAB = J, HOOK = H, UPPERCUT = U.
Defence (camera only, as in controller.py): BLOCK = W, DUCK = S, SLIP LEFT = A, SLIP RIGHT = D.
Keys come from mappings/browser_boxing.json. Movement the model calls NONE (not a punch), and any punch
it is unsure about, presses nothing.

Hotkeys work from any window: F7 calibrate (5 s countdown to get into guard; needed for duck and slip), F8 key output
on or off (with --live it starts OFF), F9 quit.

Sensitivity, with no retraining:
  F5 / F6           confidence cutoff down / up by 5 points while playing (shown on screen). Lower = presses
                    more keys, including more wrong ones. Higher = fewer wrong keys, more missed punches.
  --confidence 0.7  start at this cutoff (otherwise min_confidence in punch_config.json, default 0.6)
  --start-g 3       how hard a movement must be to count as a punch at all (the model was trained at
                    its own value, usually 2.5 g). Small changes are fine; for big ones, retrain.

The key is pressed when the punch ENDS (it stops, or the timeout runs out), because the model needs
the whole punch. A shorter timeout in punch_tune.py means less delay, then retrain.
"""
import argparse
import os
import time

import punch_segment
import punch_session as ps

VK_F5, VK_F6 = 0x74, 0x75

GREEN, ORANGE, GREY, YELLOW = (0, 220, 0), (0, 150, 255), (190, 190, 190), (0, 255, 255)


class LivePlay:
    def __init__(self, sensors, classifier, game, log=print):
        self.sensors, self.clf, self.game, self.log = sensors, classifier, game, log
        self.waiting = []        # finished punches waiting for their last camera frame
        self.shown, self.shown_t = "", 0.0
        self.count = 0

    def poll(self):
        while not self.sensors.events.empty():
            kind, value = self.sensors.events.get()
            if kind == "end" and value.reason != "gap":
                self.waiting.append((value, time.time()))
        ready = []
        latest_pose = self.sensors.latest_pose_t() or 0.0
        for seg, seen_at in self.waiting:
            # wait for a camera frame from after the punch, or give up on the camera after 0.1 s
            if latest_pose + self.clf.camera_lag_s >= seg.end_t or time.time() - seen_at > 0.1:
                ready.append((seg, seen_at))
        for item in ready:
            self.waiting.remove(item)
            self.decide(*item)

    def decide(self, seg, seen_at):
        pre = self.clf.segment.pre_s
        imu, pose = self.sensors.window(seg.start_t - pre - 0.05, seg.end_t + 0.01)
        label, conf = self.clf.classify(imu, pose, seg)
        self.count += 1
        delay = 1000 * (time.time() - seen_at)
        timing = f"{1000 * seg.duration:.0f} ms punch ({'stopped' if seg.reason == 'decel' else 'timeout'}), +{delay:.0f} ms to decide"
        if label == "NONE":
            self.show(f"not a punch ({100 * conf:.0f}%): no key", GREY)
            self.log(f"movement {self.count}: not a punch {100 * conf:.0f}% | {timing}")
            return
        if label is None or conf < self.clf.min_confidence:
            self.show(f"unsure ({label} {100 * conf:.0f}%): no key", ORANGE)
            self.log(f"punch {self.count}: unsure, best guess {label} {100 * conf:.0f}% | {timing}")
            return
        if not self.game.enabled:
            note = "output OFF, press F8"
        elif self.game.punch(label):
            note = f"key {self.game.mapping.taps[label]}"
        else:
            note = "no key mapped, or key already down"
        self.show(f"{label} {100 * conf:.0f}%  ({note})", GREEN)
        self.log(f"punch {self.count}: {label} {100 * conf:.0f}% -> {note} | {timing}")

    def show(self, text, colour):
        self.shown, self.shown_colour, self.shown_t = text, colour, time.time()

    def on_draw(self, frame):
        top = 150
        if not self.sensors.glove_ok():
            ps.put(frame, "NO GLOVE DATA", top, (0, 0, 255), 0.8)
        elif not self.sensors.segmenter.ready:
            ps.put(frame, "hold the glove still for a moment...", top, ORANGE, 0.7)
        if time.time() - self.shown_t < 1.5:
            ps.put(frame, self.shown, top + 40, self.shown_colour, 1.0, thick=3)
        ps.put(frame, f"key output {'ON' if self.game.enabled else 'OFF (F8)'}  |  F7 calibrate  F9 quit",
               frame.shape[0] - 40, YELLOW if self.game.enabled else GREY, 0.5)
        ps.put(frame, f"confidence cutoff {100 * self.clf.min_confidence:.0f}%  (F5 looser, F6 stricter)"
               f"  |  start {self.sensors.settings.start_g:g} g", frame.shape[0] - 65, GREY, 0.5)

    def adjust_confidence(self, step):
        self.clf.min_confidence = round(min(0.95, max(0.35, self.clf.min_confidence + step)), 2)
        self.show(f"confidence cutoff {100 * self.clf.min_confidence:.0f}%", YELLOW)
        self.log(f"confidence cutoff now {100 * self.clf.min_confidence:.0f}%")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--live", action="store_true", help="really press keys (default: only print them)")
    parser.add_argument("--model", default=ps.MODEL_PATH)
    parser.add_argument("--mapping", default=os.path.join(ps.ROOT, "mappings", "browser_boxing.json"))
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="fake glove (no hardware)")
    parser.add_argument("--camera", type=int, default=0)

        ready = []
        latest_pose = self.sensors.latest_pose_t() or 0.0
        for seg, seen_at in self.waiting:
            # wait for a camera frame from after the punch, or give up on the camera after 0.1 s
            if latest_pose + self.clf.camera_lag_s >= seg.end_t or time.time() - seen_at > 0.1:

        label, conf = self.clf.classify(imu, pose, seg)

        delay = 1000 * (time.time() - seen_at)
        timing = f"{1000 * seg.duration:.0f} ms punch ({'stopped' if seg.reason == 'decel' else 'timeout'}), +{delay:.0f} ms to decide"

            self.log(f"movement {self.count}: not a punch {100 * conf:.0f}% | {timing}")

            self.show(f"unsure ({label} {100 * conf:.0f}%): no key", ORANGE)
            self.log(f"punch {self.count}: unsure, best guess {label} {100 * conf:.0f}% | {timing}")
            return

"""Tests for the punch pipeline, on synthetic data (punch_sim.py). Run: python -m unittest discover tests

Synthetic punches only show the code works. They say nothing about accuracy on real punches.
"""
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

import glove_receiver  # noqa: E402
import punch_features  # noqa: E402
import punch_segment  # noqa: E402
import punch_session  # noqa: E402
import punch_sim  # noqa: E402


def block_segment(rec, settings=None):
    segs = punch_segment.find_segments(rec["t"], rec["accel"], rec["gyro"], settings)
    return punch_segment.pick_block_segment(segs, rec["press_t"], rec["release_t"])


class FrameFormat(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_button_round_trips_and_old_frames_still_parse(self):
        released = glove_receiver.pack_frame(1234, [0, 0, 1], [1, 2, 3])
        pressed = glove_receiver.pack_frame(1236, [0.5, 0, 1], [0, 0, 300], button=True)
        self.assertEqual(released[:2], b"\xA5\x5A")
        self.assertEqual(pressed[:2], b"\xA5\x5B")
        samples = list(glove_receiver.parse_frames(b"junk" + released + pressed))
        self.assertEqual([s.button for s in samples], [False, True])
        self.assertEqual([s.t_us for s in samples], [1234, 1236])
        np.testing.assert_allclose(samples[1].gyro, [0, 0, 300], atol=0.1)

    def test_corrupt_pressed_frame_is_skipped(self):
        bad = bytearray(glove_receiver.pack_frame(1, [0, 0, 1], [0, 0, 0], button=True))
        bad[10] ^= 0xFF
        self.assertEqual(list(glove_receiver.parse_frames(bytes(bad))), [])


class Segmenting(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(3)

    def test_every_block_has_one_punch(self):
        for kind in punch_sim.LABELS:
            for _ in range(20):
                seg, found = block_segment(punch_sim.synthetic_recording(kind, self.rng))
                self.assertIsNotNone(seg, kind)
                self.assertEqual(found, 1, kind)

    def test_jab_ends_when_it_stops_not_at_the_timeout(self):
        reasons = [block_segment(punch_sim.synthetic_recording("JAB", self.rng))[0].reason for _ in range(30)]

class Features(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_glove_features_are_finite_and_pose_is_missing_without_a_camera(self):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(4)
        rec = punch_sim.synthetic_recording("UPPERCUT", rng)
        seg, _ = block_segment(rec)
        imu = {k: rec[k] for k in ("t", "accel", "gyro")}
        feats = punch_features.extract(imu, None, seg, 0.25)
        imu_vals = [v for k, v in feats.items() if k.startswith("imu_")]
        self.assertTrue(np.all(np.isfinite(imu_vals)))
        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(feats["pose_up_min"]))
        # uppercut: the window should see the dip (down) before the drive (up)
        self.assertGreater(feats["imu_dip_before_up"], 1.0)
        jab = punch_sim.synthetic_recording("JAB", rng)
        jab_feats = punch_features.extract({k: jab[k] for k in ("t", "accel", "gyro")}, None, block_segment(jab)[0], 0.25)

        frames = 12

    def test_capture_format_train_and_classify(self):
        import punch_train
        rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            data, model = os.path.join(tmp, "data"), os.path.join(tmp, "model.joblib")
            for session in ("s1", "s2"):
                for kind in punch_sim.LABELS:
                    for _ in range(12):
                        rec = punch_sim.synthetic_recording(kind, rng)

                               "button": (rec["t"] >= rec["press_t"]) & (rec["t"] <= rec["release_t"])}
                        meta = {"label": kind, "press_t": rec["press_t"], "release_t": rec["release_t"], "session": session}
                        punch_session.save_block(kind, imu, punch_session.pose_arrays([]), meta, data)
            self.assertEqual(punch_session.count_blocks(data), {"JAB": 24, "HOOK": 24, "UPPERCUT": 24})
            config = os.path.join(tmp, "config.json")
            punch_session.save_config(punch_session.load_config(os.path.join(tmp, "none.json")), config)
            code = punch_train.main(["--data", data, "--out", model, "--config", config, "--features", "imu"])

            self.assertEqual(punch_session.Classifier(model, 0.8).min_confidence, 0.8)

            for _ in range(5):

            for _ in range(20):
                play.adjust_confidence(-0.05)

class StartAndPause(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_tuner_test_waits_for_calibration_and_pauses(self):
        import punch_tune
        tuner = punch_tune.Tuner(FakeSensors(), punch_session.load_config())
        tuner.classifier = None
        tuner.say = lambda text: None
        tuner.set_up_test(["3", "10", "jab"])
        tuner.toggle_test()                       # not calibrated yet
        self.assertEqual(tuner.test["state"], "waiting")
        tuner.on_calibrated()
        tuner.toggle_test()
        self.assertEqual(tuner.test["state"], "countdown")
        tuner.test["go_wall"] = 0
        tuner.update_test()
        self.assertEqual(tuner.test["state"], "running")
        self.assertTrue(tuner.counts_for_test(100.5))
        tuner.sensors.now_t = 102.0
        tuner.toggle_test()                       # pause
        self.assertEqual(tuner.test["state"], "paused")
        self.assertEqual(tuner.test["intervals"], [(100.0, 102.0)])
        self.assertFalse(tuner.counts_for_test(103.0))  # a punch while paused does not count
        self.assertLess(tuner.test["left"], 10.0)

    def test_capture_waits_then_pause_cancels_the_showing_prompt(self):
        import time
        import punch_capture
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            cap = punch_capture.PromptedCapture(FakeSensors(), punch_session.load_config(), 5, tmp, "test")
            cap.say = lambda *a: None
            punch_capture.beep = lambda kind: None
            cap.toggle()
            self.assertEqual(cap.phase, "waiting")        # not calibrated: nothing starts
            seg = punch_segment.Segment(start_t=99.0, end_t=99.2, reason="decel")
            cap.sensors.events.put(("end", seg))
            cap.on_frame()
            self.assertEqual(cap.none_pending, [])       # movement while waiting is not saved as NONE
            cap.on_calibrated()
            cap.toggle()
            self.assertEqual(cap.phase, "announce")
            cap.phase_end = 0
            cap.on_frame()                                # announce -> rest
            cap.phase_end = 0
            cap.on_frame()                                # rest -> go: a prompt is showing
            self.assertEqual((cap.phase, cap.prompts_done, len(cap.pending)), ("go", 1, 1))
            cap.toggle()                                  # pause during the prompt
            self.assertTrue(cap.paused)
            self.assertEqual((cap.prompts_done, len(cap.pending), len(cap.windows)), (0, 0, 0))
            before = cap.phase_end
            cap.on_frame()
            self.assertEqual(cap.phase_end, before)       # nothing moves on while paused
            cap.toggle()
            self.assertFalse(cap.paused)
            self.assertEqual(cap.phase, "announce")

# hack_trent_submission
Hack Trent Boxing Submission

A left-hand boxing controller. A motion sensor on the glove and a webcam watch each punch, a random forest decides whether it was a jab, hook or uppercut, and the laptop presses that punch's key in a boxing game. The team's plan and decisions are in [PROJECT.md](PROJECT.md).

## Main pipeline: glove and camera with a trained model

| Step | Command | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Check the glove | `python glove_check.py`, then `python glove_receiver.py` | Confirms data arrives. The receiver also shows whether the button reads `HELD` |
| 2. Pick the timeout | `python punch_tune.py` | Type a timeout in ms in the terminal and watch each punch's start and end on the camera window. `test 10 60 jab` runs a timed test and compares timeouts. Type `save` to keep the settings |
| 3. Record | `python punch_capture.py --person <name>` | The screen calls JAB, HOOK or UPPERCUT with a beep, in random order. Throw that punch. Records 100 of each, plus NONE (not a punch) examples from movement between prompts. `--target 20` makes a smaller set. `--button` uses the glove button instead. Data stays in `punch_data/` |
| 4. Train | `python punch_train.py` | Trains the random forest and reports glove-only, camera-only and combined accuracy. Saves `models/punch_rf.joblib` |
| 5. Play | `python punch_live.py --live` | J jab, H hook, U uppercut, plus W/S/A/D defence keys from the camera. F7 calibrate, F8 key output, F9 quit. **F5/F6** lower or raise the confidence cutoff while playing, with no retraining. `--confidence 0.7` and `--start-g 3` set the cutoff and the punch threshold at startup |

To change a setting without opening a tool, run `python punch_settings.py timeout 300` (any value from 100 to 1500 ms), `python punch_settings.py confidence 0.7`, or `python punch_settings.py` to show them all. Retrain after changing the timeout.

Every tool except training takes `--simulate`, which uses a fake glove so you can try it without hardware. Run the tests with `python -m unittest discover tests`. The supporting modules are `punch_segment.py` (finds where punches start and end), `punch_features.py` (turns a punch into model inputs), `punch_session.py` (shared buffers, settings and data files) and `punch_sim.py` (fake glove data, for testing only). Shared settings live in `punch_config.json`.

The other scripts below came earlier and still work: Kadir's rule-based camera controller, and the wired Uno tracker.

## How the pieces connect

| Input | Runs on the board | Link | Runs on the laptop |
|---|---|---|---|
| Glove sensor, wired | `punch_stream.ino` on an Arduino Uno | USB serial at 500000 baud | `punch_tracker.py` |
| Glove sensor, wireless | `glove_imu.ino` on an ESP32-CAM | WiFi UDP on port 5005 | `glove_receiver.py` |
| Webcam | None | Camera 0 | `pose_tracker.py` |

The wired and wireless firmware send the same 19-byte frame, at 500 Hz:

```
A5 5A | timestamp in µs (uint32, little-endian) | ax ay az gx gy gz (int16, big-endian) | XOR of the timestamp and sensor bytes
```

Accelerometer range is ±16 g and gyro range is ±2000 deg/s. If you change these in the firmware, also change the matching constants in the Python script that reads it.

## Setup

Requires Python. These commands are for Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

If you see `ModuleNotFoundError`, the virtual environment isn't active. In VS Code, run **Python: Select Interpreter** and choose `.venv`.

## Python scripts

### `punch_tracker.py`

Reads the wired glove over USB serial, finds punches and estimates their paths. Replace `COM7` with your port.

```powershell
python punch_tracker.py capture --port COM7 --seconds 30 --out punches.csv
python punch_tracker.py analyze punches.csv
python punch_tracker.py analyze punches.csv --save punches.png
python punch_tracker.py live --port COM7 --dry-run
python punch_tracker.py live --port COM7
```

- **`capture`** records the raw sensor data to a CSV file.
- **`analyze`** finds punches in a recording, prints a table of each punch's speed and reach, and plots the 3D paths.
- **`live`** classifies each punch as it happens and presses a key: `w` for a straight punch, or `s` for one that travels up or down. This is Windows only.

Hold still for the first 2 seconds, and rest briefly between punches, because the script uses those rests to limit drift. Back-to-back combinations can't be reconstructed. Treat paths as rough estimates: compare shape and direction rather than exact distances.

> **Warning:** without `--dry-run`, `live` sends real keystrokes to whichever window has focus.

### `pose_tracker.py`

Tracks your body through the webcam with MediaPipe and shows a skeleton overlay plus a rotatable 3D view. It detects jabs, crosses, hooks and uppercuts, plus duck, slip, block and guard-down. On first run, it downloads its pose model to `models/`, so it needs internet access once.

```powershell
python pose_tracker.py
```

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `c` | Calibrate: a 5-second countdown starts, so you can get into guard, then it records your stance. Needed for duck and slip detection |
| `a` / `d` | Rotate the 3D view |
| `q` | Quit |

The lead hand defaults to left (orthodox). To change it, set `LEAD` at the top of the file.

### `glove_receiver.py`

Receives the wireless glove's data over UDP, and puts each sample on the laptop's clock. Run directly, it prints the sample rate, peak acceleration and gyro readings. Other code can use its `GloveReceiver` class to read samples, but no script in this repo does that yet.

```powershell
python glove_receiver.py             # listen for a real glove
python glove_receiver.py --simulate  # fake a glove, with no hardware needed
```

To tell two gloves apart, add their IP addresses to `GLOVE_BY_IP`. Any glove not listed is treated as `L`. If the sensor is mounted at an angle, set `AXIS_MAP` and `AXIS_SIGN`.

## Firmware

The Uno sketches use only the built-in `Wire` library. `glove_imu.ino` needs the ESP32 board package (core 3.x). Each sketch lists its wiring at the top of the file.

| File | Board | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `firmware/punch_stream/punch_stream.ino` | Arduino Uno | Streams sensor data over USB to `punch_tracker.py`. Close the Serial Monitor first, because only one program can use the port. |
| `firmware/glove_imu/glove_imu.ino` | AI Thinker ESP32-CAM | Sends sensor data over WiFi to `glove_receiver.py`, with the training button's state in every frame. The camera isn't used. Wire the button between GPIO12 and GND, and never to 3V3, or the board won't boot. |
| `firmware/glove_imu/config.example.h` | ESP32-CAM | Template for your WiFi details. Copy it to `config.h` in the same folder and fill it in, or `glove_imu.ino` won't compile. Git ignores `config.h`, so your password stays on your computer. |
| `firmware/sketch_nov6a/sketch_nov6a.ino` | Arduino Uno | Sensor test that shows roll, pitch and yaw on the Serial Plotter at 115200 baud. Its output doesn't work with the Python scripts. Yaw drifts over time. |

## Project files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `requirements.txt` | Python packages for all three scripts. |
| `.gitignore` | Keeps `.venv/`, `models/`, `__pycache__/`, `config.h` and local Claude settings out of git. |
| `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` | Point coding agents to the Entire guide below. |
| `.entire/agent-guide.md` | Tells coding agents how to use Entire's Graph and Brain tools in this repo. |
| `.entire/settings.json` | Turns on Entire and sets where it stores session checkpoints. |
| `.entire/.gitignore` | Keeps Entire's local logs, metadata and temporary files out of git. |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Claude Code hooks that connect sessions and edits to Entire. |
| `.brainignore` | Keeps local Claude settings out of Entire's Brain index. |

[ShAkEuP134] Project plan: left-hand boxing controller. ESP32-CAM streams raw MPU6050 data over UDP on a phone hotspot to a laptop, which syncs it with webcam pose estimation, finds punches, classifies jab/hook/uppercut with a random forest (neural network only if needed), and presses keys for a boxing game. The full agreed plan is in PROJECT.md; read it before changing anything.
[ShAkEuP134] Webcam sits straight in front of the boxer by team choice. Front cameras barely see straight punches (Kadir measured about 0.1 shoulder-widths), so jabs rely mostly on the glove; training reports glove-only, camera-only and combined accuracy.
[ShAkEuP134] Design rule: calibration always waits 5 seconds after it is requested (C key or F7 hotkey), with an on-screen countdown, so the boxer can get into guard or click back into the game first. It is CALIBRATE_DELAY_S in pose_tracker.py and applies to every tool built on pose_tracker.main; on_calibrated fires when calibration actually happens, after the countdown. Do not make calibration instant.

Then Kadir needs to share it first: it's only on Kadir's laptop, and I can't reach that from here. The quickest route is for Kadir to push it to a branch. Here's a message you can send:

> Can you push your boxing game to a branch, e.g. `git switch -c kadir/game`, `git add` the game files, commit, then `git push -u origin kadir/game`? Also tell us how to start it (a Python file, an HTML page, an exe…) and which keys it uses for jab, hook, uppercut, and block/duck/slip if it has them.

**Once it's pushed, tell me.** The sync check will also flag the new branch on your next message. Then I'll:
1. **Read the game** to see how it starts and which keys it reads.
2. **Make a key mapping for it** in `mappings/` if its keys differ from J/H/U and W/S/A/D. The live pipeline already takes any mapping, so the recognition code won't change.
3. **Write one launcher** that starts the game and `punch_live.py --live` together, with the glove, camera and your trained model.
4. **Test it in dry-run first,** then you play. F8 turns key output on, F5/F6 adjust the confidence cutoff, and F9 quits.

If the game isn't a Windows-window game, for example if it runs on a phone or reads input in an unusual way, the key-press approach may not work, and I'll tell you once I've seen it.

input.content:
Kadir, this needs your approval to merge into `main`. It brings in the trained model, so your game can be driven by real punch recognition.

## The trained model

- **`models/punch_rf.joblib`:** a random forest on glove and camera features, at a 350 ms timeout.
  - Cross-validated accuracy is 98% for both together, 95% for the glove only and 97% for the camera only, on 59 punches: 20 hooks, 19 jabs and 20 uppercuts.
  - Andre's live test classified almost perfectly.
- **`punch_data/`:** the 59 raw recordings it was trained on, so anyone can retrain with `python punch_train.py`. Rejected recordings stay out.
- **`requirements.txt`:** scikit-learn is pinned to 1.9.1, the version the model was saved with. A different version may not load it. Run `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
- **Known gap:** there are no NONE (not a punch) examples yet. The recordings were made before prompted capture existed, so any movement the punch finder catches will be classified as a punch. More data from `punch_capture.py` would fix that.

## Tool changes

- **`punch_live.py`:** sensitivity changes without retraining. F5/F6 lower or raise the confidence cutoff while playing, and `--confidence` and `--start-g` set it at startup.
- **`punch_settings.py`:** sets settings from the terminal, for example `python punch_settings.py timeout 300`.
- **Timed sessions:** the tuner's test and prompted capture wait for calibration and the glove, then **.** (a global key) starts, pauses and resumes them.
- **Full screen:** the camera window opens full screen, F11 switches it, and `--windowed` opts out. Tool text sits above the bottom strip where `pose_tracker` shows calibration messages.
- **`punch_config.json`:** the default timeout is now 350 ms.

## Heads-up: conflict with `kadir/front-glove`

This merges cleanly into `main`. But `kadir/front-glove` also changes `pose_tracker.py`, including its own calibration countdown, so whichever branch merges second will conflict in that file. Since `main` already has the 5-second countdown design rule, the fix is to keep one countdown. Andre's Claude session can resolve it once this is merged.

## Testing

- 15 unit tests pass.
- Retraining from the committed data reproduces 98%.
- The tools ran with `--simulate`, and the new tuner and capture screens were checked for layout. Full screen ran without errors.

content.text:
Fixed and pushed. The confidence keys are now `[` and `]`, and all 15 tests still pass.

## Play Kadir's game with your punches

The game page is already open in your browser at **http://localhost:8000**, served from the `kadir-game` folder. If you close the browser, open that address again.

1. **Leave the game page as it is.** Don't click **Start camera** on it. Our pipeline needs the webcam, and the game will take your punches as key presses instead.
2. **Check the glove** in the VS Code terminal:
   ```powershell
   .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe glove_check.py --until 2
   ```
3. **Start the live pipeline in a window, not full screen,** so the game stays visible:
   ```powershell
   .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe punch_live.py --live --windowed
   ```
   Put the camera window to one side and the browser game on the other.
4. **Hold the glove still** until "hold the glove still" disappears.
5. **Calibrate:** click the camera window, press **C**, then get into guard during the 5-second countdown. Use C, not F7, because F7 opens a dialog in Chrome and Edge.
6. **Click into the game page** so it has focus, because keys go to whichever window is focused. Press **Space** to start the round.
7. **Press F8** to turn key output on. It starts off for safety.
8. **Punch.** Jab presses J, hook H, uppercut U, and your guard and duck/slip press W/S/A/D.

**While playing:** `[` and `]` lower or raise the confidence cutoff, and **F9** quits. Don't press F5, F6, F7 or F11 while the game has focus: they're browser keys.

**What hasn't been tested:**
- **Not yet played end to end:** I've confirmed the game page loads and listens for J/K/H/U and W/S/A/D, and that our pipeline presses those keys.
- **Holding guard presses W (block).** If that stops your punches from landing in the game, tell me and I'll turn the defence keys off.
- **No "not a punch" training yet,** so guard adjustments may throw punches.

Your branch is `andre/live-sensitivity` again, with the model restored.

"""Receive glove IMU frames over UDP.

Frame (19 bytes): A5 5A | uint32 us (little-endian) | ax ay az gx gy gz int16 (big-endian) | XOR of bytes 2-17
The second byte is 5B instead of 5A while the glove's training button is held (Sample.button).
Run directly to print incoming data, or with --simulate to fake a glove for testing.
"""
import argparse
import socket
import struct
import threading
import time
from collections import deque
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

PORT = 5005
SYNC = b"\xA5\x5A"          # button released (and all firmware without a button)
SYNC_PRESSED = b"\xA5\x5B"  # training button held
FRAME_LEN = 19

# Must match the ranges the firmware sets on the MPU.
ACCEL_LSB_PER_G = 2048.0   # +-16 g; 16384 = +-2 g, 8192 = +-4 g, 4096 = +-8 g
GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS = 16.4    # +-2000 deg/s; 131 = +-250, 65.5 = +-500, 32.8 = +-1000

# How the sensor sits on the glove: glove axis i = AXIS_SIGN[i] * sensor axis AXIS_MAP[i]
AXIS_MAP = [0, 1, 2]
AXIS_SIGN = np.array([1, 1, 1])

# Frames carry no glove id, so identify the glove by its sender IP.
GLOVE_BY_IP = {}        # e.g. {"192.168.137.20": "L", "192.168.137.21": "R"}
DEFAULT_GLOVE = "L"


@dataclass
class Sample:
    t_us: int            # ESP32 clock (wraps every ~71 min)
    accel: np.ndarray    # g, in glove axes
    gyro: np.ndarray     # deg/s, in glove axes
    t: float = 0.0       # when it was measured, on the laptop clock (time.time()); set by Clock
    dt: float = 0.0      # seconds since the previous sample, from t_us; a dropped packet shows as a big dt
    button: bool = False  # the training button was held when this sample was taken


def checksum(body):
    out = 0
    for b in body:
        out ^= b
    return out


def parse_frames(data):
    """Yield a Sample for every valid frame in data; junk or corrupt bytes are skipped."""
    i = 0
    while i + FRAME_LEN <= len(data):
        head = data[i:i + 2]
        if head in (SYNC, SYNC_PRESSED) and checksum(data[i + 2:i + 18]) == data[i + 18]:
            (t_us,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, i + 2)
            raw = np.array(struct.unpack_from(">6h", data, i + 6), dtype=float)
            accel = raw[:3][AXIS_MAP] / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G * AXIS_SIGN
            gyro = raw[3:][AXIS_MAP] / GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS * AXIS_SIGN
            yield Sample(t_us, accel, gyro, button=head == SYNC_PRESSED)
            i += FRAME_LEN
        else:
            i += 1  # resync


def pack_frame(t_us, accel, gyro, button=False):
    """Build a frame from accel (g) and gyro (deg/s); used by the simulator and tests."""
    counts = np.concatenate([np.asarray(accel) * ACCEL_LSB_PER_G, np.asarray(gyro) * GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS])
    body = struct.pack("<I", t_us & 0xFFFFFFFF) + struct.pack(">6h", *np.clip(np.round(counts), -32768, 32767).astype(int))
    return (SYNC_PRESSED if button else SYNC) + body + bytes([checksum(body)])
