"""Receive glove IMU frames over UDP.

Frame (19 bytes): A5 5A | uint32 us (little-endian) | ax ay az gx gy gz int16 (big-endian) | XOR of bytes 2-17
The second byte is 5B instead of 5A while the glove's training button is held (Sample.button).
Run directly to print incoming data, or with --simulate to fake a glove for testing.
"""
import argparse
import socket
import struct
import threading
import time
from collections import deque
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

PORT = 5005
SYNC = b"\xA5\x5A"          # button released (and all firmware without a button)
SYNC_PRESSED = b"\xA5\x5B"  # training button held
FRAME_LEN = 19

# Must match the ranges the firmware sets on the MPU.
ACCEL_LSB_PER_G = 2048.0   # +-16 g; 16384 = +-2 g, 8192 = +-4 g, 4096 = +-8 g
GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS = 16.4    # +-2000 deg/s; 131 = +-250, 65.5 = +-500, 32.8 = +-1000

# How the sensor sits on the glove: glove axis i = AXIS_SIGN[i] * sensor axis AXIS_MAP[i]
AXIS_MAP = [0, 1, 2]
AXIS_SIGN = np.array([1, 1, 1])

# Frames carry no glove id, so identify the glove by its sender IP.
GLOVE_BY_IP = {}        # e.g. {"192.168.137.20": "L", "192.168.137.21": "R"}
DEFAULT_GLOVE = "L"


@dataclass
class Sample:
    t_us: int            # ESP32 clock (wraps every ~71 min)
    accel: np.ndarray    # g, in glove axes
    gyro: np.ndarray     # deg/s, in glove axes
    t: float = 0.0       # when it was measured, on the laptop clock (time.time()); set by Clock
    dt: float = 0.0      # seconds since the previous sample, from t_us; a dropped packet shows as a big dt
    button: bool = False  # the training button was held when this sample was taken


def checksum(body):
    out = 0
    for b in body:
        out ^= b
    return out


def parse_frames(data):
    """Yield a Sample for every valid frame in data; junk or corrupt bytes are skipped."""
    i = 0
    while i + FRAME_LEN <= len(data):
        head = data[i:i + 2]
        if head in (SYNC, SYNC_PRESSED) and checksum(data[i + 2:i + 18]) == data[i + 18]:
            (t_us,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, i + 2)
            raw = np.array(struct.unpack_from(">6h", data, i + 6), dtype=float)
            accel = raw[:3][AXIS_MAP] / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G * AXIS_SIGN
            gyro = raw[3:][AXIS_MAP] / GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS * AXIS_SIGN
            yield Sample(t_us, accel, gyro, button=head == SYNC_PRESSED)
            i += FRAME_LEN
        else:
            i += 1  # resync


def pack_frame(t_us, accel, gyro, button=False):
    """Build a frame from accel (g) and gyro (deg/s); used by the simulator and tests."""
    counts = np.concatenate([np.asarray(accel) * ACCEL_LSB_PER_G, np.asarray(gyro) * GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS])
    body = struct.pack("<I", t_us & 0xFFFFFFFF) + struct.pack(">6h", *np.clip(np.round(counts), -32768, 32767).astype(int))
    return (SYNC_PRESSED if button else SYNC) + body + bytes([checksum(body)])


class Clock:
    """Puts one glove's ESP32 microsecond counter on the laptop clock.

    Packets arrive late and in bursts, so arrival time is too jittery to use directly. Instead the
    ESP32 time is unwrapped and shifted by the smallest (arrival - ESP32 time) seen recently, which
    is the packet that suffered the least delay. The result is smooth and off by only that minimum
    WiFi latency (a few ms).
    """
    MASK = 0xFFFFFFFF
    RESET_US = 5_000_000   # a step bigger than this means a reboot or long outage

    def __init__(self, window=500):
        self.last_us, self.elapsed_us = None, 0
        self.offsets = deque(maxlen=window)

    def stamp(self, sample, arrival):
        step = (sample.t_us - self.last_us) & self.MASK if self.last_us is not None else 0
        if self.last_us is None or step > self.RESET_US:  # first sample, reboot, or long outage
            self.elapsed_us, step = sample.t_us, 0
            self.offsets.clear()
        else:
            self.elapsed_us += step  # modular difference, so the 32-bit rollover is harmless
        self.last_us = sample.t_us
        t_esp = self.elapsed_us / 1e6
        self.offsets.append(arrival - t_esp)
        sample.dt, sample.t = step / 1e6, t_esp + min(self.offsets)


class GloveReceiver:
    """Background UDP listener. samples[glove_id] holds the most recent readings.

    on_sample(glove, sample), if given, is called for every sample in arrival order, on the listener
    thread. Use it when you must see every sample exactly once (the deque can drop old ones).
    """

    def __init__(self, port=PORT, history=1000, on_sample=None):
        self.sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        self.sock.bind(("0.0.0.0", port))
        self.samples, self.clocks, self.history = {}, {}, history
        self.on_sample = on_sample
        threading.Thread(target=self._listen, daemon=True).start()

    def _listen(self):
        while True:
            data, addr = self.sock.recvfrom(2048)
            arrival = time.time()
            glove = GLOVE_BY_IP.get(addr[0], DEFAULT_GLOVE)
            clock = self.clocks.setdefault(glove, Clock())
            for sample in parse_frames(data):
                clock.stamp(sample, arrival)
                self.samples.setdefault(glove, deque(maxlen=self.history)).append(sample)
                if self.on_sample:
                    self.on_sample(glove, sample)

    def latest(self, glove):
        buf = self.samples.get(glove)
        return buf[-1] if buf else None

    def recent(self, glove, seconds):
        cutoff = time.time() - seconds
        return [s for s in list(self.samples.get(glove, [])) if s.t >= cutoff]


def simulate(port=PORT, hz=200):
    """Send fake frames: a resting glove with an 80 ms punch every 1.5 s."""
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    t0 = time.time()
    while True:
        t = time.time() - t0
        phase = t % 1.5
        bump = np.sin(np.pi * phase / 0.08) if phase < 0.08 else 0.0
        accel = np.array([8 * bump, 0, 1]) + np.random.normal(0, 0.02, 3)
        gyro = np.array([0, 0, 300 * bump]) + np.random.normal(0, 1, 3)
        sock.sendto(pack_frame(int(t * 1e6), accel, gyro), ("127.0.0.1", port))
        time.sleep(1 / hz)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="send fake glove data to ourselves")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    receiver = GloveReceiver()
    if args.simulate:
        threading.Thread(target=simulate, daemon=True).start()
    while True:
        time.sleep(0.5)
        for glove in list(receiver.samples):
            recent = receiver.recent(glove, 0.5)
            peak = max((np.linalg.norm(s.accel) for s in recent), default=0)
            button = "HELD" if receiver.latest(glove).button else "up"
            print(f"glove {glove}: {len(recent) * 2} Hz, peak accel {peak:.1f} g, gyro {receiver.latest(glove).gyro.round(0)}, button {button}")

  A5 5C (5D while the button is held) | uint32 us | ax ay az gx gy gz | mx my mz (int16, big-endian,
  AK8963 axes, 0.15 uT per count) | status (bit 0 magnetometer working, bit 1 new reading) | XOR of 2-24

import argparse
import socket
import struct
import threading
import time
from collections import deque
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

PORT = 5005
SYNC = b"\xA5\x5A"          # button released (and all firmware without a button)
SYNC_PRESSED = b"\xA5\x5B"  # training button held
FRAME_LEN = 19

# Must match the ranges the firmware sets on the MPU.
ACCEL_LSB_PER_G = 2048.0   # +-16 g; 16384 = +-2 g, 8192 = +-4 g, 4096 = +-8 g
GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS = 16.4    # +-2000 deg/s; 131 = +-250, 65.5 = +-500, 32.8 = +-1000

AXIS_MAP = [0, 1, 2]
AXIS_SIGN = np.array([1, 1, 1])

# Frames carry no glove id, so identify the glove by its sender IP.
GLOVE_BY_IP = {}        # e.g. {"192.168.137.20": "L", "192.168.137.21": "R"}
DEFAULT_GLOVE = "L"

class Sample:
    t_us: int            # ESP32 clock (wraps every ~71 min)
    accel: np.ndarray    # g, in glove axes
    gyro: np.ndarray     # deg/s, in glove axes
    t: float = 0.0       # when it was measured, on the laptop clock (time.time()); set by Clock
    dt: float = 0.0      # seconds since the previous sample, from t_us; a dropped packet shows as a big dt
    button: bool = False  # the training button was held when this sample was taken


def checksum(body):
    out = 0
    for b in body:
        out ^= b
    return out


def parse_frames(data):
    """Yield a Sample for every valid frame in data; junk or corrupt bytes are skipped."""
    i = 0
    while i + FRAME_LEN <= len(data):
        head = data[i:i + 2]
        if head in (SYNC, SYNC_PRESSED) and checksum(data[i + 2:i + 18]) == data[i + 18]:
            (t_us,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, i + 2)
            raw = np.array(struct.unpack_from(">6h", data, i + 6), dtype=float)
            accel = raw[:3][AXIS_MAP] / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G * AXIS_SIGN
            gyro = raw[3:][AXIS_MAP] / GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS * AXIS_SIGN
            yield Sample(t_us, accel, gyro, button=head == SYNC_PRESSED)
            i += FRAME_LEN
        else:
            i += 1  # resync

    """Build a frame from accel (g) and gyro (deg/s); used by the simulator and tests."""
    counts = np.concatenate([np.asarray(accel) * ACCEL_LSB_PER_G, np.asarray(gyro) * GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS])

"""Receive glove IMU frames over UDP.

Frame (19 bytes): A5 5A | uint32 us (little-endian) | ax ay az gx gy gz int16 (big-endian) | XOR of bytes 2-17
The second byte is 5B instead of 5A while the glove's training button is held (Sample.button).

Frame with a magnetometer (26 bytes, the right glove: ESP32-S3 + MPU-9250, firmware/glove_imu_right):
  A5 5C (5D while the button is held) | uint32 us | ax ay az gx gy gz | mx my mz (int16, big-endian,
  AK8963 axes, 0.15 uT per count) | status (bit 0 magnetometer working, bit 1 new reading) | XOR of 2-24
Both kinds can arrive on any port. The gloves are told apart by port: left 5005, right 5006.

Run directly to print incoming data, or with --simulate to fake a glove for testing.
"""
import argparse
import socket
import struct
import threading
import time
from collections import deque
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

PORT = 5005
SYNC = b"\xA5\x5A"          # button released (and all firmware without a button)
SYNC_PRESSED = b"\xA5\x5B"  # training button held
FRAME_LEN = 19
SYNC_MAG = b"\xA5\x5C"          # a frame with magnetometer readings, button released
SYNC_MAG_PRESSED = b"\xA5\x5D"  # ...button held
MAG_FRAME_LEN = 26
MAG_UT_PER_LSB = 0.15           # AK8963 in 16-bit mode
# The AK8963's axes differ from the accelerometer's: x and y swap and z flips (MPU-9250 datasheet).
MAG_TO_ACCEL_AXES, MAG_TO_ACCEL_SIGN = [1, 0, 2], np.array([1, 1, -1])

# Must match the ranges the firmware sets on the MPU.
ACCEL_LSB_PER_G = 2048.0   # +-16 g; 16384 = +-2 g, 8192 = +-4 g, 4096 = +-8 g
GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS = 16.4    # +-2000 deg/s; 131 = +-250, 65.5 = +-500, 32.8 = +-1000

# How the sensor sits on the glove: glove axis i = AXIS_SIGN[i] * sensor axis AXIS_MAP[i]
AXIS_MAP = [0, 1, 2]
AXIS_SIGN = np.array([1, 1, 1])

# Frames carry no glove id, so identify the glove by its sender IP.
GLOVE_BY_IP = {}        # e.g. {"192.168.137.20": "L", "192.168.137.21": "R"}
DEFAULT_GLOVE = "L"


@dataclass
class Sample:
    t_us: int            # ESP32 clock (wraps every ~71 min)
    accel: np.ndarray    # g, in glove axes
    gyro: np.ndarray     # deg/s, in glove axes
    t: float = 0.0       # when it was measured, on the laptop clock (time.time()); set by Clock
    dt: float = 0.0      # seconds since the previous sample, from t_us; a dropped packet shows as a big dt
    button: bool = False  # the training button was held when this sample was taken
    mag: np.ndarray = None  # magnetic field in uT, glove axes (same as accel); None if the glove has none
    mag_ok: bool = False    # the magnetometer is present and working
    size: int = FRAME_LEN   # bytes this frame took, for counting junk


def checksum(body):
    out = 0
    for b in body:
        out ^= b
    return out


def parse_frames(data):
    """Yield a Sample for every valid frame in data; junk or corrupt bytes are skipped."""
    i = 0
    while i + FRAME_LEN <= len(data):
        head = data[i:i + 2]
        if head in (SYNC, SYNC_PRESSED) and checksum(data[i + 2:i + 18]) == data[i + 18]:
            (t_us,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, i + 2)
            raw = np.array(struct.unpack_from(">6h", data, i + 6), dtype=float)
            accel = raw[:3][AXIS_MAP] / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G * AXIS_SIGN
            gyro = raw[3:][AXIS_MAP] / GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS * AXIS_SIGN
            yield Sample(t_us, accel, gyro, button=head == SYNC_PRESSED)
            i += FRAME_LEN
        else:
            i += 1  # resync


def pack_frame(t_us, accel, gyro, button=False):
    """Build a frame from accel (g) and gyro (deg/s); used by the simulator and tests."""
    counts = np.concatenate([np.asarray(accel) * ACCEL_LSB_PER_G, np.asarray(gyro) * GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS])
    body = struct.pack("<I", t_us & 0xFFFFFFFF) + struct.pack(">6h", *np.clip(np.round(counts), -32768, 32767).astype(int))
    return (SYNC_PRESSED if button else SYNC) + body + bytes([checksum(body)])


class Clock:
    """Puts one glove's ESP32 microsecond counter on the laptop clock.

    Packets arrive late and in bursts, so arrival time is too jittery to use directly. Instead the
    ESP32 time is unwrapped and shifted by the smallest (arrival - ESP32 time) seen recently, which
    is the packet that suffered the least delay. The result is smooth and off by only that minimum
    WiFi latency (a few ms).
    """
    MASK = 0xFFFFFFFF
    RESET_US = 5_000_000   # a step bigger than this means a reboot or long outage

    def __init__(self, window=500):
        self.last_us, self.elapsed_us = None, 0
        self.offsets = deque(maxlen=window)

    def stamp(self, sample, arrival):
        step = (sample.t_us - self.last_us) & self.MASK if self.last_us is not None else 0
        if self.last_us is None or step > self.RESET_US:  # first sample, reboot, or long outage
            self.elapsed_us, step = sample.t_us, 0
            self.offsets.clear()
        else:
            self.elapsed_us += step  # modular difference, so the 32-bit rollover is harmless
        self.last_us = sample.t_us
        t_esp = self.elapsed_us / 1e6
        self.offsets.append(arrival - t_esp)
        sample.dt, sample.t = step / 1e6, t_esp + min(self.offsets)


class GloveReceiver:
    """Background UDP listener. samples[glove_id] holds the most recent readings.

    on_sample(glove, sample), if given, is called for every sample in arrival order, on the listener
    thread. Use it when you must see every sample exactly once (the deque can drop old ones).
    """

    def __init__(self, port=PORT, history=1000, on_sample=None):
        self.sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        self.sock.bind(("0.0.0.0", port))
        self.samples, self.clocks, self.history = {}, {}, history
        self.on_sample = on_sample
        threading.Thread(target=self._listen, daemon=True).start()

    def _listen(self):
        while True:
            data, addr = self.sock.recvfrom(2048)
            arrival = time.time()
            glove = GLOVE_BY_IP.get(addr[0], DEFAULT_GLOVE)
            clock = self.clocks.setdefault(glove, Clock())
            for sample in parse_frames(data):
                clock.stamp(sample, arrival)
                self.samples.setdefault(glove, deque(maxlen=self.history)).append(sample)
                if self.on_sample:
                    self.on_sample(glove, sample)

    def latest(self, glove):
        buf = self.samples.get(glove)
        return buf[-1] if buf else None

    def recent(self, glove, seconds):
        cutoff = time.time() - seconds
        return [s for s in list(self.samples.get(glove, [])) if s.t >= cutoff]


def simulate(port=PORT, hz=200):
    """Send fake frames: a resting glove with an 80 ms punch every 1.5 s."""
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    t0 = time.time()
    while True:
        t = time.time() - t0
        phase = t % 1.5
        bump = np.sin(np.pi * phase / 0.08) if phase < 0.08 else 0.0
        accel = np.array([8 * bump, 0, 1]) + np.random.normal(0, 0.02, 3)
        gyro = np.array([0, 0, 300 * bump]) + np.random.normal(0, 1, 3)
        sock.sendto(pack_frame(int(t * 1e6), accel, gyro), ("127.0.0.1", port))
        time.sleep(1 / hz)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="send fake glove data to ourselves")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    receiver = GloveReceiver()
    if args.simulate:
        threading.Thread(target=simulate, daemon=True).start()

"""Receive glove IMU frames over UDP.

Frame (19 bytes): A5 5A | uint32 us (little-endian) | ax ay az gx gy gz int16 (big-endian) | XOR of bytes 2-17
The second byte is 5B instead of 5A while the glove's training button is held (Sample.button).

Frame with a magnetometer (26 bytes, the right glove: ESP32-S3 + MPU-9250, firmware/glove_imu_right):
  A5 5C (5D while the button is held) | uint32 us | ax ay az gx gy gz | mx my mz (int16, big-endian,
  AK8963 axes, 0.15 uT per count) | status (bit 0 magnetometer working, bit 1 new reading) | XOR of 2-24
Both kinds can arrive on any port. The gloves are told apart by port: left 5005, right 5006.

Run directly to print incoming data, or with --simulate to fake a glove for testing.
"""
import argparse
import socket
import struct
import threading
import time
from collections import deque
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

PORT = 5005
SYNC = b"\xA5\x5A"          # button released (and all firmware without a button)
SYNC_PRESSED = b"\xA5\x5B"  # training button held
FRAME_LEN = 19
SYNC_MAG = b"\xA5\x5C"          # a frame with magnetometer readings, button released
SYNC_MAG_PRESSED = b"\xA5\x5D"  # ...button held
MAG_FRAME_LEN = 26
MAG_UT_PER_LSB = 0.15           # AK8963 in 16-bit mode
# The AK8963's axes differ from the accelerometer's: x and y swap and z flips (MPU-9250 datasheet).
MAG_TO_ACCEL_AXES, MAG_TO_ACCEL_SIGN = [1, 0, 2], np.array([1, 1, -1])

# Must match the ranges the firmware sets on the MPU.
ACCEL_LSB_PER_G = 2048.0   # +-16 g; 16384 = +-2 g, 8192 = +-4 g, 4096 = +-8 g
GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS = 16.4    # +-2000 deg/s; 131 = +-250, 65.5 = +-500, 32.8 = +-1000

# How the sensor sits on the glove: glove axis i = AXIS_SIGN[i] * sensor axis AXIS_MAP[i]
AXIS_MAP = [0, 1, 2]
AXIS_SIGN = np.array([1, 1, 1])

# Frames carry no glove id, so identify the glove by its sender IP.
GLOVE_BY_IP = {}        # e.g. {"192.168.137.20": "L", "192.168.137.21": "R"}
DEFAULT_GLOVE = "L"


@dataclass
class Sample:
    t_us: int            # ESP32 clock (wraps every ~71 min)
    accel: np.ndarray    # g, in glove axes
    gyro: np.ndarray     # deg/s, in glove axes
    t: float = 0.0       # when it was measured, on the laptop clock (time.time()); set by Clock
    dt: float = 0.0      # seconds since the previous sample, from t_us; a dropped packet shows as a big dt
    button: bool = False  # the training button was held when this sample was taken
    mag: np.ndarray = None  # magnetic field in uT, glove axes (same as accel); None if the glove has none
    mag_ok: bool = False    # the magnetometer is present and working
    size: int = FRAME_LEN   # bytes this frame took, for counting junk


def checksum(body):
    out = 0
    for b in body:
        out ^= b
    return out


def parse_frames(data):
    """Yield a Sample for every valid frame in data; junk or corrupt bytes are skipped."""
    i = 0
    while i + FRAME_LEN <= len(data):
        head = data[i:i + 2]
        if head in (SYNC, SYNC_PRESSED) and checksum(data[i + 2:i + 18]) == data[i + 18]:
            (t_us,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, i + 2)
            raw = np.array(struct.unpack_from(">6h", data, i + 6), dtype=float)
            accel = raw[:3][AXIS_MAP] / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G * AXIS_SIGN
            gyro = raw[3:][AXIS_MAP] / GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS * AXIS_SIGN
            yield Sample(t_us, accel, gyro, button=head == SYNC_PRESSED)
            i += FRAME_LEN
        elif (head in (SYNC_MAG, SYNC_MAG_PRESSED) and i + MAG_FRAME_LEN <= len(data)
              and checksum(data[i + 2:i + 25]) == data[i + 25]):
            (t_us,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, i + 2)
            raw = np.array(struct.unpack_from(">9h", data, i + 6), dtype=float)
            accel = raw[:3][AXIS_MAP] / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G * AXIS_SIGN
            gyro = raw[3:6][AXIS_MAP] / GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS * AXIS_SIGN
            mag_sensor = raw[6:][MAG_TO_ACCEL_AXES] * MAG_TO_ACCEL_SIGN * MAG_UT_PER_LSB
            mag = mag_sensor[AXIS_MAP] * AXIS_SIGN
            yield Sample(t_us, accel, gyro, button=head == SYNC_MAG_PRESSED, mag=mag,
                         mag_ok=bool(data[i + 24] & 0x01), size=MAG_FRAME_LEN)
            i += MAG_FRAME_LEN
        else:
            i += 1  # resync


def pack_frame(t_us, accel, gyro, button=False):
    """Build a frame from accel (g) and gyro (deg/s); used by the simulator and tests."""
    counts = np.concatenate([np.asarray(accel) * ACCEL_LSB_PER_G, np.asarray(gyro) * GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS])
    body = struct.pack("<I", t_us & 0xFFFFFFFF) + struct.pack(">6h", *np.clip(np.round(counts), -32768, 32767).astype(int))
    return (SYNC_PRESSED if button else SYNC) + body + bytes([checksum(body)])


class Clock:
    """Puts one glove's ESP32 microsecond counter on the laptop clock.

    Packets arrive late and in bursts, so arrival time is too jittery to use directly. Instead the
    ESP32 time is unwrapped and shifted by the smallest (arrival - ESP32 time) seen recently, which
    is the packet that suffered the least delay. The result is smooth and off by only that minimum
    WiFi latency (a few ms).
    """
    MASK = 0xFFFFFFFF
    RESET_US = 5_000_000   # a step bigger than this means a reboot or long outage

    def __init__(self, window=500):
        self.last_us, self.elapsed_us = None, 0
        self.offsets = deque(maxlen=window)

    def stamp(self, sample, arrival):
        step = (sample.t_us - self.last_us) & self.MASK if self.last_us is not None else 0
        if self.last_us is None or step > self.RESET_US:  # first sample, reboot, or long outage
            self.elapsed_us, step = sample.t_us, 0
            self.offsets.clear()
        else:
            self.elapsed_us += step  # modular difference, so the 32-bit rollover is harmless
        self.last_us = sample.t_us
        t_esp = self.elapsed_us / 1e6
        self.offsets.append(arrival - t_esp)
        sample.dt, sample.t = step / 1e6, t_esp + min(self.offsets)


class GloveReceiver:
    """Background UDP listener. samples[glove_id] holds the most recent readings.

    on_sample(glove, sample), if given, is called for every sample in arrival order, on the listener
    thread. Use it when you must see every sample exactly once (the deque can drop old ones).
    """

    def __init__(self, port=PORT, history=1000, on_sample=None):
        self.sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        self.sock.bind(("0.0.0.0", port))
        self.samples, self.clocks, self.history = {}, {}, history
        self.on_sample = on_sample
        threading.Thread(target=self._listen, daemon=True).start()

    def _listen(self):
        while True:
            data, addr = self.sock.recvfrom(2048)
            arrival = time.time()
            glove = GLOVE_BY_IP.get(addr[0], DEFAULT_GLOVE)
            clock = self.clocks.setdefault(glove, Clock())
            for sample in parse_frames(data):
                clock.stamp(sample, arrival)
                self.samples.setdefault(glove, deque(maxlen=self.history)).append(sample)
                if self.on_sample:
                    self.on_sample(glove, sample)

    def latest(self, glove):
        buf = self.samples.get(glove)
        return buf[-1] if buf else None

    def recent(self, glove, seconds):
        cutoff = time.time() - seconds
        return [s for s in list(self.samples.get(glove, [])) if s.t >= cutoff]


def simulate(port=PORT, hz=200):
    """Send fake frames: a resting glove with an 80 ms punch every 1.5 s."""
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    t0 = time.time()
    while True:
        t = time.time() - t0
        phase = t % 1.5
        bump = np.sin(np.pi * phase / 0.08) if phase < 0.08 else 0.0
        accel = np.array([8 * bump, 0, 1]) + np.random.normal(0, 0.02, 3)
        gyro = np.array([0, 0, 300 * bump]) + np.random.normal(0, 1, 3)
        sock.sendto(pack_frame(int(t * 1e6), accel, gyro), ("127.0.0.1", port))
        time.sleep(1 / hz)

    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="send fake glove data to ourselves")

            print(f"glove {glove}: {len(recent) * 2} Hz, peak accel {peak:.1f} g, gyro {receiver.latest(glove).gyro.round(0)}, button {button}")

import socket, time, numpy as np, glove_receiver as gr
for name, port in (("left", 5005), ("right", 5006)):
    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    try:
        s.bind(("0.0.0.0", port))
    except OSError:
        print(f"{name} (port {port}): another program is already listening on this port"); continue
    s.settimeout(0.3); end = time.time() + 4; samples, senders = [], set()
    while time.time() < end:
        try:
            data, addr = s.recvfrom(4096)
        except socket.timeout:
            continue
        senders.add(addr[0]); samples += list(gr.parse_frames(data))
    s.close()
    if not samples:
        print(f"{name} (port {port}): nothing received"); continue
    a = np.array([np.linalg.norm(x.accel) for x in samples])
    mag = [x for x in samples if x.mag is not None]

          + (f" | magnetometer {'working' if mag[-1].mag_ok else 'NOT working'}, {np.linalg.norm(mag[-1].mag):.0f} uT" if mag else " | no magnetometer"))

1	"""Shared plumbing for the punch pipeline: live glove and camera buffers, settings, and training blocks.
2	
3	Synchronising the glove and the camera: both are put on the laptop clock (time.time()).
4	  - glove samples: glove_receiver.Clock maps the ESP32's microsecond counter onto it.
5	  - camera frames: pose_tracker stamps each frame when it is read, before pose estimation; that stamp
6	    reaches us through on_features(now, ...), right after on_pose(world, visibility) for the same frame.
7	Any remaining camera delay can be set as camera_lag_s in punch_config.json.
8	"""

24	DATA_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "punch_data")

30	def load_config(path=CONFIG_PATH):
31	    data = {}
32	    if os.path.exists(path):
33	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
34	            data = json.load(f)
35	    return {
36	        "segment": punch_segment.SegmentSettings.from_dict(data.get("segment", {})),
37	        "min_confidence": float(data.get("min_confidence", 0.6)),
38	        "camera_lag_s": float(data.get("camera_lag_s", 0.0)),
39	    }
40	
41	
42	def save_config(config, path=CONFIG_PATH):
43	    data = {"_note": "Shared punch settings. punch_tune.py saves the segment settings here.",
44	            "segment": config["segment"].to_dict(), "min_confidence": config["min_confidence"],
45	            "camera_lag_s": config["camera_lag_s"]}
46	    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
47	        json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
48	        f.write("\n")
49

51	# --- live data ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
52	class LiveSensors:
53	    """Listens to the glove, runs the segmenter on every sample, and keeps recent glove and pose data.
54	
55	    events is a queue of (kind, value): ("start", Segment), ("end", Segment), ("press", t), ("release", t).
56	    Wire the camera in with pose_callbacks().
57	    """
58	
59	    def __init__(self, settings, seconds=30, simulate=False, port=glove_receiver.PORT):
60	        self.lock = threading.Lock()
61	        self.imu = deque(maxlen=int(seconds * 600))  # (t, t_us, ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz, button)
62	        self.pose = deque(maxlen=int(seconds * 40))   # (t, world 33x3, visibility 33)
63	        self.events = queue.Queue()
64	        self.segmenter = punch_segment.Segmenter(settings)
65	        self.button = False
66	        self.last_sample_wall = 0.0
67	        self.samples_seen = 0
68	        self._pending_pose = None
69	        try:
70	            self.receiver = glove_receiver.GloveReceiver(port=port, on_sample=self._on_sample)
71	        except OSError:
72	            raise SystemExit(f"Cannot listen for the glove on UDP port {port}: another program already is. Close the "
73	                             "other punch tool (punch_tune, punch_capture, punch_live, glove_check or controller) first.")
74	        self.sim_stop = None
75	        if simulate:
76	            import punch_sim
77	            self.sim_stop = punch_sim.start_simulator(port=port)
78	
79	    def set_settings(self, settings):
80	        with self.lock:
81	            self.segmenter = punch_segment.Segmenter(settings)
82	
83	    @property
84	    def settings(self):
85	        return self.segmenter.s
86	
87	    def _on_sample(self, glove, s):
88	        with self.lock:
89	            self.imu.append((s.t, s.t_us, *s.accel, *s.gyro, s.button))
90	            self.samples_seen += 1
91	            self.last_sample_wall = time.time()
92	            if s.button != self.button:
93	                self.button = s.button
94	                self.events.put(("press" if s.button else "release", s.t))
95	            event = self.segmenter.feed(s.t, s.accel, s.gyro)
96	        if event:
97	            self.events.put(event)
98	
99	    def glove_ok(self, within=0.5):
100	        return time.time() - self.last_sample_wall < within
101	
102	    def latest_imu_t(self):
103	        with self.lock:
104	            return self.imu[-1][0] if self.imu else None
105	
106	    # camera side
107	    def pose_callbacks(self):
108	        def on_pose(world, visibility):
109	            self._pending_pose = (np.array(world, dtype=float), np.array(visibility, dtype=float))
110	
111	        def on_features(now, speeds, travel, from_low):
112	            if self._pending_pose is not None:
113	                with self.lock:
114	                    self.pose.append((now, *self._pending_pose))
115	                self._pending_pose = None
116	            return None  # we decide punches ourselves
117	
118	        return {"on_pose": on_pose, "on_features": on_features, "builtin_punches": False}
119	
120	    def latest_pose_t(self):
121	        with self.lock:
122	            return self.pose[-1][0] if self.pose else None
123	
124	    def window(self, t0, t1):
125	        """Glove and pose data between t0 and t1, as arrays (see block format below)."""
126	        with self.lock:
127	            imu = [r for r in self.imu if t0 <= r[0] <= t1]
128	            pose = [r for r in self.pose if t0 <= r[0] <= t1]
129	        return imu_arrays(imu), pose_arrays(pose)
130	
131	    def recent_linear_g(self, seconds):
132	        """(t, |acceleration - 1 g|) for the last few seconds, for drawing a trace."""
133	        with self.lock:
134	            rows = list(itertools.islice(reversed(self.imu), int(seconds * 520)))[::-1]
135	        if not rows:
136	            return np.zeros(0), np.zeros(0)
137	        a = np.array(rows, dtype=float)
138	        return a[:, 0], np.abs(np.linalg.norm(a[:, 2:5], axis=1) - 1.0)
139	
140	    def close(self):
141	        if self.sim_stop:
142	            self.sim_stop.set()
143	
144	
145	def imu_arrays(rows):
146	    a = np.array(rows, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 9)
147	    return {"t": a[:, 0], "t_us": a[:, 1].astype(np.int64), "accel": a[:, 2:5], "gyro": a[:, 5:8],
148	            "button": a[:, 8].astype(bool)}
149	
150	
151	def pose_arrays(rows):
152	    if not rows:
153	        return {"t": np.zeros(0), "world": np.zeros((0, 33, 3)), "vis": np.zeros((0, 33))}
154	    return {"t": np.array([r[0] for r in rows]), "world": np.stack([r[1] for r in rows]),
155	            "vis": np.stack([r[2] for r in rows])}

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Arm:
    """Everything that differs between the left and right glove. Each arm has its own port, recordings,
    model and punch names, so the two are recorded, trained and run separately."""
    name: str            # "left" or "right"
    side: str            # "L" or "R": which arm the camera features look at
    port: int            # UDP port its glove sends to
    data_dir: str        # its training recordings
    model_path: str      # its trained random forest
    labels: tuple        # its punches; NONE (not a punch) is added by training when recorded
    how: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # how to throw each punch, shown when recording
    mirror: bool = False  # the simulator mirrors left-right for this arm
    magnetometer: bool = False  # its glove has one (the simulator fakes it)


ARMS = {
    "left": Arm("left", "L", 5005, os.path.join(ROOT, "punch_data"), os.path.join(ROOT, "models", "punch_rf.joblib"),
                ("JAB", "HOOK", "UPPERCUT"),
                {"JAB": "straight forward", "HOOK": "left, then forward, then right",
                 "UPPERCUT": "arm drops down, then drives up"}),
    "right": Arm("right", "R", 5006, os.path.join(ROOT, "punch_data_right"),
                 os.path.join(ROOT, "models", "punch_rf_right.joblib"),
                 ("CROSS", "HOOK", "UPPERCUT"),
                 {"CROSS": "straight forward", "HOOK": "right, then forward, then left",
                  "UPPERCUT": "arm drops down, then drives up"}, mirror=True, magnetometer=True),
}

# The left arm's paths, kept under their old names so existing code and data work unchanged.
DATA_DIR = ARMS["left"].data_dir
MODEL_PATH = ARMS["left"].model_path
LABELS = ARMS["left"].labels


def add_arm_argument(parser):
    parser.add_argument("--arm", choices=sorted(ARMS), default="left",
                        help="which glove: left (ESP32-CAM, port 5005) or right (ESP32-S3, port 5006)")

"""Turn one punch (a Segment plus the glove and camera data around it) into numbers for the random forest.

Used identically by punch_train.py and punch_live.py. Only data up to the end of the punch is used, so
live classification never waits for anything training had but play does not.

The window is [start - pre_s, end]. The part before the start is the wind-up, such as an uppercut's dip.

Glove features (prefix imu_) are in the glove's own axes, so the sensor must be mounted the same way for
training and play. "Vertical" means along gravity as measured just before the punch.
Camera features (prefix pose_) are for the LEFT arm, in a body frame: right = toward the boxer's right
shoulder, up, and forward, all in shoulder-widths. They are NaN when no body was seen; the random forest
handles missing values.

The motions they are built to tell apart (PROJECT.md):
  jab       straight forward
  hook      left, then forward, then right   -> wrist "right" goes down first, then up past the start
  uppercut  down, then up                    -> wrist "up" dips first, then rises; vertical accel - then +
"""
import numpy as np

NOSE, L_SH, R_SH, L_EL, L_WR, L_HIP = 0, 11, 12, 13, 15, 23
CLIP_G, CLIP_DPS = 15.9, 1990.0


def _stats(prefix, values, out):
    """mean, std, min, max, and the time (0 to 1 through the window) of the min and the max."""
    n = len(values)
    out[prefix + "_mean"] = float(np.mean(values))
    out[prefix + "_std"] = float(np.std(values))
    out[prefix + "_min"] = float(np.min(values))

training and play. "Vertical" means along gravity as measured just before the punch.
Magnetometer features (prefix imu_mag_) are only made for a glove that has one (the right glove). They

  uppercut  down, then up                    -> wrist "up" dips first, then rises; vertical accel - then +

ARM_POINTS = {"L": (L_SH, L_EL, L_WR, L_HIP), "R": (R_SH, R_EL, R_WR, R_HIP)}  # shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip

"""Turn one punch (a Segment plus the glove and camera data around it) into numbers for the random forest.

Used identically by punch_train.py and punch_live.py. Only data up to the end of the punch is used, so
live classification never waits for anything training had but play does not.

The window is [start - pre_s, end]. The part before the start is the wind-up, such as an uppercut's dip.

Glove features (prefix imu_) are in the glove's own axes, so the sensor must be mounted the same way for
training and play. "Vertical" means along gravity as measured just before the punch.
Camera features (prefix pose_) are for the LEFT arm, in a body frame: right = toward the boxer's right
shoulder, up, and forward, all in shoulder-widths. They are NaN when no body was seen; the random forest
handles missing values.

The motions they are built to tell apart (PROJECT.md):
  jab       straight forward
  hook      left, then forward, then right   -> wrist "right" goes down first, then up past the start
  uppercut  down, then up                    -> wrist "up" dips first, then rises; vertical accel - then +
"""
import numpy as np

NOSE, L_SH, R_SH, L_EL, L_WR, L_HIP = 0, 11, 12, 13, 15, 23
CLIP_G, CLIP_DPS = 15.9, 1990.0


def _stats(prefix, values, out):
    """mean, std, min, max, and the time (0 to 1 through the window) of the min and the max."""
    n = len(values)
    out[prefix + "_mean"] = float(np.mean(values))
    out[prefix + "_std"] = float(np.std(values))
    out[prefix + "_min"] = float(np.min(values))
    out[prefix + "_max"] = float(np.max(values))
    out[prefix + "_tmin"] = float(np.argmin(values) / max(n - 1, 1))
    out[prefix + "_tmax"] = float(np.argmax(values) / max(n - 1, 1))


def _thirds(prefix, values, out):
    for i, part in enumerate(np.array_split(values, 3)):
        out[f"{prefix}_p{i + 1}"] = float(np.mean(part)) if len(part) else 0.0


def imu_features(imu, seg, pre_s):
    t, accel, gyro = imu["t"], imu["accel"], imu["gyro"]
    out = {}
    main = (t >= seg.start_t) & (t <= seg.end_t)
    pre = (t >= seg.start_t - pre_s) & (t < seg.start_t)
    if main.sum() < 5:
        return None
    up = seg.gravity / np.linalg.norm(seg.gravity)

    # Linear acceleration: subtract gravity, turning it with the glove during the punch.
    idx = np.flatnonzero(main)
    g = up.copy()
    linear = np.empty((len(idx), 3))
    for k, i in enumerate(idx):
        if k:
            dt = t[i] - t[idx[k - 1]]
            g = g - np.cross(np.radians(gyro[i]), g) * dt
            g /= np.linalg.norm(g)
        linear[k] = accel[i] - g
    rot = gyro[main]
    pre_linear = accel[pre] - up if pre.any() else np.zeros((1, 3))
    pre_rot = gyro[pre] if pre.any() else np.zeros((1, 3))

    out["imu_duration"] = float(seg.end_t - seg.start_t)
    out["imu_ended_by_decel"] = float(seg.reason == "decel")
    out["imu_peak_g"] = float(seg.peak_g)
    out["imu_peak_speed"] = float(seg.peak_speed)
    for j, axis in enumerate("xyz"):
        _stats(f"imu_a{axis}", linear[:, j], out)
        _thirds(f"imu_a{axis}", linear[:, j], out)
        _stats(f"imu_g{axis}", rot[:, j], out)
        _thirds(f"imu_g{axis}", rot[:, j], out)
        out[f"imu_a{axis}_pre"] = float(np.mean(pre_linear[:, j]))
        out[f"imu_g{axis}_pre"] = float(np.mean(pre_rot[:, j]))
        out[f"imu_turn_{axis}"] = float(np.sum(rot[:, j]) * np.median(np.diff(t[main])))  # degrees turned
        out[f"imu_tilt_{axis}"] = float(up[j])  # how the glove was held before the punch

    # Along gravity: an uppercut is down (negative) then up (positive).
    vertical = np.concatenate([pre_linear @ up, linear @ up])
    horizontal = np.linalg.norm(linear - np.outer(linear @ up, up), axis=1)
    _stats("imu_vert", vertical, out)
    _thirds("imu_vert", linear @ up, out)
    out["imu_vert_pre"] = float(np.mean(pre_linear @ up))
    # uppercut: how far it went DOWN before its strongest push UP (the brake at the top comes after)
    top = int(np.argmax(vertical))
    out["imu_dip_before_up"] = float(max(0.0, -np.min(vertical[:top + 1])))
    out["imu_up_after_dip"] = float(vertical[top] - np.min(vertical[:top + 1]))
    out["imu_horiz_max"] = float(np.max(horizontal))
    out["imu_horiz_mean"] = float(np.mean(horizontal))
    out["imu_vert_share"] = float(np.mean(np.abs(linear @ up)) / (np.mean(np.linalg.norm(linear, axis=1)) + 1e-6))
    size = np.linalg.norm(linear, axis=1)
    out["imu_lin_mean"] = float(np.mean(size))
    out["imu_rot_max"] = float(np.max(np.linalg.norm(rot, axis=1)))
    out["imu_rot_mean"] = float(np.mean(np.linalg.norm(rot, axis=1)))
    out["imu_clipped"] = float(np.mean((np.abs(accel[main]) >= CLIP_G).any(axis=1) | (np.abs(rot) >= CLIP_DPS).any(axis=1)))
    return out


def _angle(a, b, c):
    """Angle at b, in degrees, for each frame."""
    u, v = a - b, c - b
    cos = np.sum(u * v, axis=1) / (np.linalg.norm(u, axis=1) * np.linalg.norm(v, axis=1) + 1e-9)
    return np.degrees(np.arccos(np.clip(cos, -1, 1)))


POSE_SERIES = ("right", "up", "fwd", "elbow", "shoulder")
POSE_STATS = ("first", "last", "min", "max", "change", "tmin", "tmax")


def pose_feature_names():
    names = [f"pose_{s}_{k}" for s in POSE_SERIES for k in POSE_STATS]
    return names + ["pose_out_left", "pose_back_right", "pose_dip", "pose_rise",
                    "pose_speed_max", "pose_low_start", "pose_wrist_vis", "pose_frames"]


def pose_features(pose, seg, pre_s, camera_lag_s=0.0):
    names = pose_feature_names()
    out = dict.fromkeys(names, float("nan"))
    if pose is None or len(pose["t"]) == 0:
        out["pose_frames"] = 0.0
        return out
    t = pose["t"] - camera_lag_s
    keep = (t >= seg.start_t - pre_s) & (t <= seg.end_t)
    out["pose_frames"] = float(keep.sum())
    if keep.sum() < 3:
        return out
    w, vis, t = pose["world"][keep], pose["vis"][keep], t[keep]

    sw = np.linalg.norm(w[:, R_SH] - w[:, L_SH], axis=1).mean() + 1e-6
    right = (w[:, R_SH] - w[:, L_SH]).mean(axis=0)
    right[1] = 0.0
    right /= np.linalg.norm(right) + 1e-9
    up = np.array([0.0, -1.0, 0.0])  # MediaPipe world y points down
    fwd = np.cross(up, right)
    rel = (w[:, L_WR] - w[:, L_SH]) / sw
    series = {
        "right": rel @ right, "up": rel @ up, "fwd": rel @ fwd,
        "elbow": _angle(w[:, L_SH], w[:, L_EL], w[:, L_WR]),
        "shoulder": _angle(w[:, L_HIP], w[:, L_SH], w[:, L_EL]),
    }
    n = keep.sum()
    for name, v in series.items():
        out[f"pose_{name}_first"], out[f"pose_{name}_last"] = float(v[0]), float(v[-1])
        out[f"pose_{name}_min"], out[f"pose_{name}_max"] = float(v.min()), float(v.max())
        out[f"pose_{name}_change"] = float(v[-1] - v[0])
        out[f"pose_{name}_tmin"] = float(np.argmin(v) / (n - 1))
        out[f"pose_{name}_tmax"] = float(np.argmax(v) / (n - 1))
    r, u = series["right"], series["up"]
    out["pose_out_left"] = float(r[0] - r.min())             # hook: swings out to the left first...
    out["pose_back_right"] = float(r[-1] - r.min())          # ...then comes back across to the right
    out["pose_dip"] = float(u[0] - u.min())                  # uppercut: drops first...
    out["pose_rise"] = float(u.max() - u.min())              # ...then rises
    steps = np.linalg.norm(np.diff(rel, axis=0), axis=1) / np.maximum(np.diff(t), 1e-3)
    out["pose_speed_max"] = float(steps.max()) if len(steps) else float("nan")
    out["pose_low_start"] = float(w[0, L_WR, 1] > w[0, L_EL, 1])  # wrist below elbow at the start
    out["pose_wrist_vis"] = float(vis[:, L_WR].mean())
    return out


def extract(imu, pose, seg, pre_s, camera_lag_s=0.0):
    """All features for one punch, as {name: value}, or None if there is too little glove data."""
    imu_part = imu_features(imu, seg, pre_s)
    if imu_part is None:
        return None
    return {**imu_part, **pose_features(pose, seg, pre_s, camera_lag_s)}


def select(names, feature_set):
    """Names to use for 'imu', 'pose' or 'both'."""
    if feature_set == "both":
        return list(names)
    return [n for n in names if n.startswith(feature_set + "_")]

                    "pose_speed_max", "pose_low_start", "pose_wrist_vis", "pose_frames"]


def pose_features(pose, seg, pre_s, camera_lag_s=0.0):
    names = pose_feature_names()
    out = dict.fromkeys(names, float("nan"))
    if pose is None or len(pose["t"]) == 0:
        out["pose_frames"] = 0.0
        return out
    t = pose["t"] - camera_lag_s
    keep = (t >= seg.start_t - pre_s) & (t <= seg.end_t)
    out["pose_frames"] = float(keep.sum())
    if keep.sum() < 3:
        return out
    w, vis, t = pose["world"][keep], pose["vis"][keep], t[keep]

    sw = np.linalg.norm(w[:, R_SH] - w[:, L_SH], axis=1).mean() + 1e-6
    right = (w[:, R_SH] - w[:, L_SH]).mean(axis=0)
    right[1] = 0.0
    right /= np.linalg.norm(right) + 1e-9
    up = np.array([0.0, -1.0, 0.0])  # MediaPipe world y points down
    fwd = np.cross(up, right)
    rel = (w[:, L_WR] - w[:, L_SH]) / sw
    series = {
        "right": rel @ right, "up": rel @ up, "fwd": rel @ fwd,
        "elbow": _angle(w[:, L_SH], w[:, L_EL], w[:, L_WR]),
        "shoulder": _angle(w[:, L_HIP], w[:, L_SH], w[:, L_EL]),
    }
    n = keep.sum()
    for name, v in series.items():
        out[f"pose_{name}_first"], out[f"pose_{name}_last"] = float(v[0]), float(v[-1])
        out[f"pose_{name}_min"], out[f"pose_{name}_max"] = float(v.min()), float(v.max())
        out[f"pose_{name}_change"] = float(v[-1] - v[0])
        out[f"pose_{name}_tmin"] = float(np.argmin(v) / (n - 1))
        out[f"pose_{name}_tmax"] = float(np.argmax(v) / (n - 1))
    r, u = series["right"], series["up"]
    out["pose_out_left"] = float(r[0] - r.min())             # hook: swings out to the left first...
    out["pose_back_right"] = float(r[-1] - r.min())          # ...then comes back across to the right
    out["pose_dip"] = float(u[0] - u.min())                  # uppercut: drops first...
    out["pose_rise"] = float(u.max() - u.min())              # ...then rises
    steps = np.linalg.norm(np.diff(rel, axis=0), axis=1) / np.maximum(np.diff(t), 1e-3)
    out["pose_speed_max"] = float(steps.max()) if len(steps) else float("nan")
    out["pose_low_start"] = float(w[0, L_WR, 1] > w[0, L_EL, 1])  # wrist below elbow at the start
    out["pose_wrist_vis"] = float(vis[:, L_WR].mean())
    return out


def extract(imu, pose, seg, pre_s, camera_lag_s=0.0):
    """All features for one punch, as {name: value}, or None if there is too little glove data."""
    imu_part = imu_features(imu, seg, pre_s)
    if imu_part is None:
        return None
    return {**imu_part, **pose_features(pose, seg, pre_s, camera_lag_s)}


def select(names, feature_set):
    """Names to use for 'imu', 'pose' or 'both'."""
    if feature_set == "both":
        return list(names)
    return [n for n in names if n.startswith(feature_set + "_")]

"""Turn one punch (a Segment plus the glove and camera data around it) into numbers for the random forest.

Used identically by punch_train.py and punch_live.py. Only data up to the end of the punch is used, so
live classification never waits for anything training had but play does not.

The window is [start - pre_s, end]. The part before the start is the wind-up, such as an uppercut's dip.

Glove features (prefix imu_) are in the glove's own axes, so the sensor must be mounted the same way for
training and play. "Vertical" means along gravity as measured just before the punch.
Magnetometer features (prefix imu_mag_) are only made for a glove that has one (the right glove). They
describe how the glove turned relative to the Earth's magnetic field, which the gyro cannot drift on.
Camera features (prefix pose_) are for the glove's arm (side "L" or "R"), in a body frame: "right" =
toward the middle of the body (for the right arm this is mirrored, so it means toward the left), up,
and forward, all in shoulder-widths. Mirroring keeps "a hook swings out, then in" the same numbers for
both arms. They are NaN when no body was seen; the random forest handles missing values.

The motions they are built to tell apart (PROJECT.md):
  jab/cross straight forward
  hook      out, then forward, then across   -> wrist "right" goes down first, then up past the start
            (left: left, forward, right. right: right, forward, left)
  uppercut  down, then up                    -> wrist "up" dips first, then rises; vertical accel - then +
"""
import numpy as np

NOSE, L_SH, R_SH, L_EL, L_WR, L_HIP = 0, 11, 12, 13, 15, 23
R_EL, R_WR, R_HIP = 14, 16, 24
ARM_POINTS = {"L": (L_SH, L_EL, L_WR, L_HIP), "R": (R_SH, R_EL, R_WR, R_HIP)}  # shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip
CLIP_G, CLIP_DPS = 15.9, 1990.0
MAG_NAMES = ["imu_mag_turn", "imu_mag_spread"] + [f"imu_mag_{k}_{a}" for k in ("start", "change") for a in "xyz"]


def _stats(prefix, values, out):
    """mean, std, min, max, and the time (0 to 1 through the window) of the min and the max."""
    n = len(values)
    out[prefix + "_mean"] = float(np.mean(values))
    out[prefix + "_std"] = float(np.std(values))
    out[prefix + "_min"] = float(np.min(values))
    out[prefix + "_max"] = float(np.max(values))
    out[prefix + "_tmin"] = float(np.argmin(values) / max(n - 1, 1))
    out[prefix + "_tmax"] = float(np.argmax(values) / max(n - 1, 1))


def _thirds(prefix, values, out):
    for i, part in enumerate(np.array_split(values, 3)):
        out[f"{prefix}_p{i + 1}"] = float(np.mean(part)) if len(part) else 0.0


def imu_features(imu, seg, pre_s):
    t, accel, gyro = imu["t"], imu["accel"], imu["gyro"]
    out = {}
    main = (t >= seg.start_t) & (t <= seg.end_t)
    pre = (t >= seg.start_t - pre_s) & (t < seg.start_t)
    if main.sum() < 5:
        return None
    up = seg.gravity / np.linalg.norm(seg.gravity)

    # Linear acceleration: subtract gravity, turning it with the glove during the punch.
    idx = np.flatnonzero(main)
    g = up.copy()
    linear = np.empty((len(idx), 3))
    for k, i in enumerate(idx):
        if k:
            dt = t[i] - t[idx[k - 1]]
            g = g - np.cross(np.radians(gyro[i]), g) * dt
            g /= np.linalg.norm(g)
        linear[k] = accel[i] - g
    rot = gyro[main]
    pre_linear = accel[pre] - up if pre.any() else np.zeros((1, 3))
    pre_rot = gyro[pre] if pre.any() else np.zeros((1, 3))

    out["imu_duration"] = float(seg.end_t - seg.start_t)
    out["imu_ended_by_decel"] = float(seg.reason == "decel")
    out["imu_peak_g"] = float(seg.peak_g)
    out["imu_peak_speed"] = float(seg.peak_speed)
    for j, axis in enumerate("xyz"):
        _stats(f"imu_a{axis}", linear[:, j], out)
        _thirds(f"imu_a{axis}", linear[:, j], out)
        _stats(f"imu_g{axis}", rot[:, j], out)
        _thirds(f"imu_g{axis}", rot[:, j], out)
        out[f"imu_a{axis}_pre"] = float(np.mean(pre_linear[:, j]))
        out[f"imu_g{axis}_pre"] = float(np.mean(pre_rot[:, j]))
        out[f"imu_turn_{axis}"] = float(np.sum(rot[:, j]) * np.median(np.diff(t[main])))  # degrees turned
        out[f"imu_tilt_{axis}"] = float(up[j])  # how the glove was held before the punch

    # Along gravity: an uppercut is down (negative) then up (positive).
    vertical = np.concatenate([pre_linear @ up, linear @ up])
    horizontal = np.linalg.norm(linear - np.outer(linear @ up, up), axis=1)

    out["imu_horiz_mean"] = float(np.mean(horizontal))
    out["imu_vert_share"] = float(np.mean(np.abs(linear @ up)) / (np.mean(np.linalg.norm(linear, axis=1)) + 1e-6))

"""Synthetic glove data, for testing the pipeline without hardware. NOT real punches.

The shapes follow the team's punch definitions, in the glove's axes, with x forward, y to the boxer's
left and z up (gravity reads +1 g on z at rest):
  JAB       straight forward: speed up along +x, then brake
  HOOK      left, then forward, then right: +y, then +x, then -y, then brake
  UPPERCUT  down, then up: a small dip along -z, then a hard drive along +z, then brake

A model trained on this data is only a test that the code runs. Its accuracy says nothing about real
punches. Real training data comes from punch_capture.py.
"""
import socket
import threading
import time

import numpy as np

import glove_receiver

RATE_HZ = 500
LABELS = ("JAB", "HOOK", "UPPERCUT")
X, Y, Z = np.eye(3)


def _pulse(n, peak):
    """A smooth half-sine burst of n samples."""
    return peak * np.sin(np.pi * (np.arange(n) + 0.5) / n)


def _phases(phases, rng, rate=RATE_HZ):
    """phases = [(axis, g, seconds, gyro axis, deg/s)]. Returns (linear accel, gyro) arrays."""
    accel, gyro = [], []
    for axis, g, seconds, gyro_axis, dps in phases:
        n = max(3, int(round(seconds * rng.uniform(0.85, 1.15) * rate)))
        shape = _pulse(n, 1.0)
        accel.append(np.outer(shape * g, axis))
        gyro.append(np.outer(shape * dps, gyro_axis))
    return np.vstack(accel), np.vstack(gyro)


def punch_motion(kind, rng, strength=1.0):
    """Linear acceleration (g) and rotation (deg/s) for one synthetic punch, glove axes."""
    k = strength * rng.uniform(0.8, 1.2)
    if kind == "JAB":
        # equal areas, so the glove ends at rest: 6 g x 80 ms forward, then 7.2 g x 67 ms back
        phases = [(X, 6 * k, 0.080, X, 80), (X, -7.2 * k, 0.067, X, -80)]
    elif kind == "HOOK":
        phases = [(Y, 4 * k, 0.070, Z, -150), (X, 5 * k, 0.080, Z, -400), (Y, -6 * k, 0.090, Z, -450),
                  (X, -5 * k, 0.080, Z, 200), (Y, 2.9 * k, 0.090, Z, 150)]
    elif kind == "UPPERCUT":
        # dip down (2 g x 80 ms), then up (6 g x 120 ms stops the dip and drives up), then brake
        phases = [(Z, -2 * k, 0.080, Y, 60), (Z, 6 * k, 0.120, Y, -350), (Z, -7 * k, 0.080, Y, 200)]
    else:
        raise ValueError(kind)
    return _phases(phases, rng)


def synthetic_recording(kind, rng, rest_before=1.0, rest_after=0.6, rate=RATE_HZ, t0=0.0):
    """A training block's worth of data: rest, one punch, rest. Returns dict of arrays plus press/release."""
    lin, rot = punch_motion(kind, rng)
    n_before, n_after = int(rest_before * rate), int(rest_after * rate)
    gravity = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
    accel = np.vstack([np.tile(gravity, (n_before, 1)), gravity + lin, np.tile(gravity, (n_after, 1))])
    gyro = np.vstack([np.zeros((n_before, 3)), rot, np.zeros((n_after, 3))])
    accel += rng.normal(0, 0.02, accel.shape)
    gyro += rng.normal(0, 1.0, gyro.shape)
    n = len(accel)
    t = t0 + np.arange(n) / rate
    start = t0 + rest_before
    return {"t": t, "t_us": (np.arange(n) * 1_000_000 // rate).astype(np.int64), "accel": accel, "gyro": gyro,
            "press_t": start - 0.4, "release_t": start + len(lin) / rate + 0.3, "punch_t": start}


def simulate_glove(port=glove_receiver.PORT, kinds=LABELS, hold_button=True, seed=0, stop=None):
    """Stream synthetic punches over UDP like the real glove, button included. Runs until stop is set."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    started, sent, n = time.time(), 0, 0
    while stop is None or not stop.is_set():
        rec = synthetic_recording(kinds[n % len(kinds)], rng, t0=sent / RATE_HZ)
        n += 1
        packet = b""
        for i in range(len(rec["t"])):
            ti = rec["t"][i]
            pressed = hold_button and rec["press_t"] <= ti <= rec["release_t"]
            packet += glove_receiver.pack_frame(int(sent * 1e6 / RATE_HZ), rec["accel"][i], rec["gyro"][i], pressed)
            sent += 1
            if len(packet) >= 10 * glove_receiver.FRAME_LEN:
                sock.sendto(packet, ("127.0.0.1", port))
                packet = b""
                wait = started + sent / RATE_HZ - time.time()
                if wait > 0:
                    time.sleep(wait)


def start_simulator(**kwargs):
    stop = threading.Event()
    threading.Thread(target=simulate_glove, kwargs={**kwargs, "stop": stop}, daemon=True).start()
    return stop

"""Synthetic glove data, for testing the pipeline without hardware. NOT real punches.

The shapes follow the team's punch definitions, in the glove's axes, with x forward, y to the boxer's
left and z up (gravity reads +1 g on z at rest):
  JAB       straight forward: speed up along +x, then brake
  HOOK      left, then forward, then right: +y, then +x, then -y, then brake
  UPPERCUT  down, then up: a small dip along -z, then a hard drive along +z, then brake
  CROSS     the right arm's straight punch: the same motion as JAB
mirror=True makes it a right-arm glove (left and right swapped, so a hook goes right, forward, left).
magnetometer=True adds a magnetic field that turns with the glove, as the right glove's MPU-9250 sends.

A model trained on this data is only a test that the code runs. Its accuracy says nothing about real
punches. Real training data comes from punch_capture.py.
"""
import socket
import threading
import time

import numpy as np

import glove_receiver

RATE_HZ = 500
LABELS = ("JAB", "HOOK", "UPPERCUT")
X, Y, Z = np.eye(3)


def _pulse(n, peak):
    """A smooth half-sine burst of n samples."""
    return peak * np.sin(np.pi * (np.arange(n) + 0.5) / n)


def _phases(phases, rng, rate=RATE_HZ):
    """phases = [(axis, g, seconds, gyro axis, deg/s)]. Returns (linear accel, gyro) arrays."""
    accel, gyro = [], []
    for axis, g, seconds, gyro_axis, dps in phases:
        n = max(3, int(round(seconds * rng.uniform(0.85, 1.15) * rate)))
        shape = _pulse(n, 1.0)
        accel.append(np.outer(shape * g, axis))
        gyro.append(np.outer(shape * dps, gyro_axis))
    return np.vstack(accel), np.vstack(gyro)


def punch_motion(kind, rng, strength=1.0):
    """Linear acceleration (g) and rotation (deg/s) for one synthetic punch, glove axes."""
    k = strength * rng.uniform(0.8, 1.2)
    if kind in ("JAB", "CROSS"):
        # equal areas, so the glove ends at rest: 6 g x 80 ms forward, then 7.2 g x 67 ms back
        phases = [(X, 6 * k, 0.080, X, 80), (X, -7.2 * k, 0.067, X, -80)]
    elif kind == "HOOK":
        phases = [(Y, 4 * k, 0.070, Z, -150), (X, 5 * k, 0.080, Z, -400), (Y, -6 * k, 0.090, Z, -450),
                  (X, -5 * k, 0.080, Z, 200), (Y, 2.9 * k, 0.090, Z, 150)]
    elif kind == "UPPERCUT":
        # dip down (2 g x 80 ms), then up (6 g x 120 ms stops the dip and drives up), then brake
        phases = [(Z, -2 * k, 0.080, Y, 60), (Z, 6 * k, 0.120, Y, -350), (Z, -7 * k, 0.080, Y, 200)]
    else:
        raise ValueError(kind)
    return _phases(phases, rng)


EARTH_FIELD_UT = np.array([20.0, 0.0, -40.0])  # a typical field, in glove axes at rest


def field_in_glove(gyro, rate=RATE_HZ, start=EARTH_FIELD_UT):
    """The Earth's field as a glove turning at gyro (deg/s) would measure it, sample by sample."""
    m, out = start.astype(float).copy(), np.empty((len(gyro), 3))
    for i, w in enumerate(np.radians(gyro)):
        m = m - np.cross(w, m) / rate  # a fixed vector, seen from a turning glove
        out[i] = m
    return out


def synthetic_recording(kind, rng, rest_before=1.0, rest_after=0.6, rate=RATE_HZ, t0=0.0, mirror=False,
                        magnetometer=False):
    """A training block's worth of data: rest, one punch, rest. Returns dict of arrays plus press/release."""
    lin, rot = punch_motion(kind, rng)
    if mirror:  # swap left and right: flip y; rotation is a turning axis, so its x and z flip instead
        lin, rot = lin * [1, -1, 1], rot * [-1, 1, -1]
    n_before, n_after = int(rest_before * rate), int(rest_after * rate)
    gravity = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
    accel = np.vstack([np.tile(gravity, (n_before, 1)), gravity + lin, np.tile(gravity, (n_after, 1))])
    gyro = np.vstack([np.zeros((n_before, 3)), rot, np.zeros((n_after, 3))])
    accel += rng.normal(0, 0.02, accel.shape)
    gyro += rng.normal(0, 1.0, gyro.shape)
    n = len(accel)
    t = t0 + np.arange(n) / rate
    start = t0 + rest_before
    return {"t": t, "t_us": (np.arange(n) * 1_000_000 // rate).astype(np.int64), "accel": accel, "gyro": gyro,
            "press_t": start - 0.4, "release_t": start + len(lin) / rate + 0.3, "punch_t": start}


def simulate_glove(port=glove_receiver.PORT, kinds=LABELS, hold_button=True, seed=0, stop=None):
    """Stream synthetic punches over UDP like the real glove, button included. Runs until stop is set."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    started, sent, n = time.time(), 0, 0
    while stop is None or not stop.is_set():
        rec = synthetic_recording(kinds[n % len(kinds)], rng, t0=sent / RATE_HZ)
        n += 1
        packet = b""
        for i in range(len(rec["t"])):
            ti = rec["t"][i]
            pressed = hold_button and rec["press_t"] <= ti <= rec["release_t"]
            packet += glove_receiver.pack_frame(int(sent * 1e6 / RATE_HZ), rec["accel"][i], rec["gyro"][i], pressed)
            sent += 1
            if len(packet) >= 10 * glove_receiver.FRAME_LEN:
                sock.sendto(packet, ("127.0.0.1", port))
                packet = b""
                wait = started + sent / RATE_HZ - time.time()
                if wait > 0:
                    time.sleep(wait)


def start_simulator(**kwargs):
    stop = threading.Event()
    threading.Thread(target=simulate_glove, kwargs={**kwargs, "stop": stop}, daemon=True).start()
    return stop

BOM_ESC = "\\" + "ufeff"   # the six ASCII characters \ufeff, written into the source as an escape
def sub(path, pairs):
    t = open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="").read()
    for a, b in pairs:
        assert t.count(a) == 1, (path, a, t.count(a))
        t = t.replace(a, b)
    open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write(t)

def build_dataset(root, config, quiet=False):
    """Returns (X, y, groups, names, skipped)."""
    rows, labels, groups, skipped = [], [], [], Counter()
    seg_settings, lag = config["segment"], config["camera_lag_s"]
    for path in ps.block_paths(root):
        block = ps.load_block(path)
        meta, imu = block["meta"], block["imu"]
        segments = punch_segment.find_segments(imu["t"], imu["accel"], imu["gyro"], seg_settings)
        seg, _ = punch_segment.pick_block_segment(segments, meta["press_t"], meta["release_t"])
        if seg is None or seg.reason == "gap":
            skipped["no punch found with the current settings"] += 1
            continue
        feats = punch_features.extract(imu, block["pose"], seg, seg_settings.pre_s, lag)
        if feats is None:
            skipped["too little glove data"] += 1
            continue
        rows.append(feats)
        labels.append(meta["label"])
        groups.append(meta.get("session", "?"))
    if not rows:
        return None, None, None, None, skipped
    names = list(rows[0])
    X = np.array([[r.get(n, np.nan) for n in names] for r in rows], dtype=float)

def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--data", default=ps.DATA_DIR)
    parser.add_argument("--out", default=ps.MODEL_PATH)
    parser.add_argument("--features", choices=["both", "imu", "pose"], default="both")
    parser.add_argument("--config", default=ps.CONFIG_PATH)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    config = ps.load_config(args.config)
    X, y, groups, names, skipped = build_dataset(args.data, config)
    if X is None:
        print(f"No usable blocks in {os.path.abspath(args.data)}. Record some with python punch_capture.py.")
        for why, n in skipped.items():
            print(f"  skipped {n}: {why}")
        return 1
    counts = Counter(y)
    print(f"{len(y)} blocks from {len(set(groups))} session(s): " + ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in sorted(counts.items())))
    few = sorted(k for k, n in counts.items() if n < 5)
    if few:
        print(f"  left out of training (fewer than 5 examples): {', '.join(few)}")
        keep = ~np.isin(y, few)
        X, y, groups = X[keep], y[keep], groups[keep]
        counts = Counter(y)
    if "NONE" not in counts:
        print("  no NONE examples yet, so every movement it catches will be called a punch")
    for why, n in skipped.items():
        print(f"  skipped {n} block(s): {why}")
    pose_seen = float(np.mean(X[:, names.index("pose_frames")] >= 3))
    print(f"camera saw the arm in {100 * pose_seen:.0f}% of punches")
    if len(counts) < 2 or min(counts.values()) < 5:
        print("Need at least 5 punches of at least 2 kinds to train.")
        return 1

    print(f"\nTimeout {1000 * config['segment'].timeout_s:.0f} ms. Cross-validated accuracy:")
    summary = {}
    for fs in ("imu", "pose", "both"):
        r = evaluate(X, y, groups, names, fs, config["min_confidence"], show=False)
        summary[fs] = r
        if r is None:
            print(f"  {fs:5}: " + ("no camera data in these blocks" if fs == "pose" else "not enough data"))
            continue
        extra = f", new session {100 * r['new_session_accuracy']:.0f}%" if "new_session_accuracy" in r else ""
        sure = (f"right on {100 * r['sure_accuracy']:.0f}% of those" if r["sure_share"] else "so no keys would be pressed")
        print(f"  {fs:5}: {100 * r['accuracy']:.0f}%{extra}  "
              f"(sure enough to press a key for {100 * r['sure_share']:.0f}% of punches, {sure})")

    if summary.get(args.features) is None:
        print(f"Cannot train with --features {args.features}: not enough usable data.")
        return 1
    print(f"\nDetails for --features {args.features}:")
    evaluate(X, y, groups, names, args.features, config["min_confidence"], show=True)

    import joblib
    cols = usable_columns(X, names, args.features)
    forest = make_forest().fit(X[:, cols], y)
    used = [names[i] for i in cols]
    top = sorted(zip(forest.feature_importances_, used), reverse=True)[:10]
    print("most useful features: " + ", ".join(f"{n} {v:.2f}" for v, n in top))
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(args.out)), exist_ok=True)
    joblib.dump({"model": forest, "features": used, "labels": list(forest.classes_), "feature_set": args.features,
                 "segment": config["segment"].to_dict(), "camera_lag_s": config["camera_lag_s"],
                 "min_confidence": config["min_confidence"], "trained_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
                 "counts": {str(k): int(v) for k, v in counts.items()},
                 "cv_accuracy": summary[args.features]["accuracy"]}, args.out)
    print(f"saved {args.out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

36	GREEN, ORANGE, GREY, YELLOW = (0, 220, 0), (0, 150, 255), (190, 190, 190), (0, 255, 255)
37

39	class LivePlay:
40	    def __init__(self, sensors, classifier, game, log=print):
41	        self.sensors, self.clf, self.game, self.log = sensors, classifier, game, log
42	        self.waiting = []        # finished punches waiting for their last camera frame
43	        self.shown, self.shown_t = "", 0.0
44	        self.count = 0
45	
46	    def poll(self):
47	        while not self.sensors.events.empty():
48	            kind, value = self.sensors.events.get()
49	            if kind == "end" and value.reason != "gap":
50	                self.waiting.append((value, time.time()))
51	        ready = []
52	        latest_pose = self.sensors.latest_pose_t() or 0.0
53	        for seg, seen_at in self.waiting:
54	            # wait for a camera frame from after the punch, or give up on the camera after 0.1 s
55	            if latest_pose + self.clf.camera_lag_s >= seg.end_t or time.time() - seen_at > 0.1:
56	                ready.append((seg, seen_at))
57	        for item in ready:
58	            self.waiting.remove(item)
59	            self.decide(*item)
60	
61	    def decide(self, seg, seen_at):
62	        pre = self.clf.segment.pre_s
63	        imu, pose = self.sensors.window(seg.start_t - pre - 0.05, seg.end_t + 0.01)
64	        label, conf = self.clf.classify(imu, pose, seg)
65	        self.count += 1
66	        delay = 1000 * (time.time() - seen_at)
67	        timing = f"{1000 * seg.duration:.0f} ms punch ({'stopped' if seg.reason == 'decel' else 'timeout'}), +{delay:.0f} ms to decide"
68	        if label == "NONE":
69	            self.show(f"not a punch ({100 * conf:.0f}%): no key", GREY)
70	            self.log(f"movement {self.count}: not a punch {100 * conf:.0f}% | {timing}")
71	            return
72	        if label is None or conf < self.clf.min_confidence:
73	            self.show(f"unsure ({label} {100 * conf:.0f}%): no key", ORANGE)
74	            self.log(f"punch {self.count}: unsure, best guess {label} {100 * conf:.0f}% | {timing}")
75	            return
76	        if not self.game.enabled:
77	            note = "output OFF, press F8"
78	        elif self.game.punch(label):
79	            note = f"key {self.game.mapping.taps[label]}"
80	        else:
81	            note = "no key mapped, or key already down"
82	        self.show(f"{label} {100 * conf:.0f}%  ({note})", GREEN)
83	        self.log(f"punch {self.count}: {label} {100 * conf:.0f}% -> {note} | {timing}")
84	
85	    def show(self, text, colour):
86	        self.shown, self.shown_colour, self.shown_t = text, colour, time.time()
87	
88	    def on_draw(self, frame):
89	        top = 150
90	        if not self.sensors.glove_ok():
91	            ps.put(frame, "NO GLOVE DATA", top, (0, 0, 255), 0.8)
92	        elif not self.sensors.segmenter.ready:
93	            ps.put(frame, "hold the glove still for a moment...", top, ORANGE, 0.7)
94	        if time.time() - self.shown_t < 1.5:
95	            ps.put(frame, self.shown, top + 40, self.shown_colour, 1.0, thick=3)
96	        ps.put(frame, f"key output {'ON' if self.game.enabled else 'OFF (F8)'}  |  F7 calibrate  F9 quit  F11 full screen",
97	               frame.shape[0] - ps.TEXT_BOTTOM, YELLOW if self.game.enabled else GREY, 0.5)
98	        ps.put(frame, f"confidence cutoff {100 * self.clf.min_confidence:.0f}%  ([ looser, ] stricter)"
99	               f"  |  start {self.sensors.settings.start_g:g} g", frame.shape[0] - ps.TEXT_BOTTOM - 25, GREY, 0.5)
100

103	        self.show(f"confidence cutoff {100 * self.clf.min_confidence:.0f}%", YELLOW)

"""Play with BOTH gloves: each arm has its own glove, its own punch finder and its own trained model,
running side by side, with one camera for both.

  python punch_live_both.py                    dry run: prints the keys it would press, presses nothing
  python punch_live_both.py --live --windowed  really presses keys, with the game visible beside it
  python punch_live_both.py --simulate         fake gloves on both arms (no hardware)

Left arm (port 5005, models/punch_rf.joblib):        JAB = J, HOOK = H, UPPERCUT = U
Right arm (port 5006, models/punch_rf_right.joblib): CROSS = K, HOOK = H, UPPERCUT = U
Defence (camera): BLOCK = W, DUCK = S, SLIP LEFT = A, SLIP RIGHT = D. Keys from mappings/browser_boxing.json.
If one arm has no trained model yet, the other still plays on its own.

Hotkeys from any window: F8 key output on or off (with --live it starts OFF), F9 quit, [ and ] confidence
cutoff down or up (both arms). Calibrate by pressing C in the camera window (5 s countdown into guard).
F7 also calibrates, but in a browser game F7 opens a dialog, so use C there.

Each arm still trains on its own: python punch_train.py --arm left, then --arm right.
"""
import argparse
import os
import time

import punch_live
import punch_session as ps


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--live", action="store_true", help="really press keys (default: only print them)")
    parser.add_argument("--mapping", default=os.path.join(ps.ROOT, "mappings", "browser_boxing.json"))
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="fake gloves on both arms (no hardware)")
    parser.add_argument("--windowed", action="store_true", help="start in a normal window, not full screen")
    parser.add_argument("--camera", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--confidence", type=float, help="how sure a model must be to press a key, 0 to 1")
    parser.add_argument("--max-seconds", type=float, help="stop by itself (for testing)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    import controller
    import game_input
    mapping = game_input.Mapping.load(args.mapping)
    keyboard = game_input.SendInputKeyboard() if args.live else game_input.DryRunKeyboard()
    game = game_input.GameInput(mapping, keyboard)
    game.set_enabled(not args.live)  # a dry run is harmless, so it starts on; live starts off

    arms = []  # (arm, LiveSensors, LivePlay)
    for name, x in (("left", 10), ("right", 330)):
        arm = ps.ARMS[name]
        if not ps.Classifier.exists(arm.model_path):
            print(f"{name} arm: no model at {os.path.relpath(arm.model_path)} yet, so it is off. "
                  f"Record with punch_capture.py --arm {name}, then punch_train.py --arm {name}.")
            continue
        clf = ps.Classifier(arm.model_path, args.confidence)
        sensors = ps.LiveSensors(clf.segment, simulate=args.simulate, port=arm.port, arm=arm)
        play = punch_live.LivePlay(sensors, clf, game, name=f"{name.upper()}: ", x=x, scale=0.65, footer=not arms)
        arms.append((arm, sensors, play))
        print(f"{name} arm: model trained {clf.info['trained_at']} on {clf.info['counts']}, "
              f"timeout {1000 * clf.segment.timeout_s:.0f} ms, glove on port {arm.port}")
    if not arms:
        return 1

    # Defence keys, calibration and F7/F8/F9 come from controller.py; punches come from the two models.
    callbacks = controller.make_callbacks(game, controller.Hotkeys(), detector=False)
    callbacks.pop("on_punch")
    hotkey_frame = callbacks["on_frame"]
    sensitivity_keys = controller.Hotkeys()
    screen_keys = ps.ToolKeys(fullscreen=not args.windowed)
    started = time.time()

    def on_frame():
        for _, _, play in arms:
            play.poll()
        for vk, step in ((punch_live.VK_LOWER, -0.05), (punch_live.VK_RAISE, +0.05)):
            if sensitivity_keys.pressed(vk):
                for _, _, play in arms:
                    play.adjust_confidence(step)
        screen_keys.poll_fullscreen()
        return hotkey_frame() or bool(args.max_seconds and time.time() - started > args.max_seconds)

    def on_draw(frame):
        for _, _, play in arms:
            play.on_draw(frame)

    callbacks.update(ps.shared_pose_callbacks(*[s for _, s, _ in arms]))  # one camera feeds both arms
    callbacks.update(on_frame=on_frame, on_draw=on_draw, camera_index=args.camera, fullscreen=not args.windowed)

    print(f"Keys: {mapping.taps}")
    print("LIVE: keys go to the focused window." if args.live else "Dry run: nothing is pressed.")
    print(f"Key output is {'ON' if game.enabled else 'OFF'}. F8 toggles output, F9 quits, C (camera window) calibrates.")
    import pose_tracker
    try:
        pose_tracker.main(**callbacks)
    finally:
        game.close()
        for _, sensors, _ in arms:
            sensors.close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

class RightGlove(unittest.TestCase):
    """The second glove: its own frame (with a magnetometer), port, data folder, labels and model."""

    def test_magnetometer_frame_round_trips_beside_old_frames(self):
        old = glove_receiver.pack_frame(10, [0, 0, 1], [1, 2, 3])
        new = glove_receiver.pack_frame(12, [0.5, 0, 1], [0, 0, 300], button=True, mag=[20.0, -5.0, 40.0])
        self.assertEqual((len(old), len(new)), (19, 26))
        a, b = glove_receiver.parse_frames(b"x" + old + new)
        self.assertIsNone(a.mag)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(b.mag, [20, -5, 40], atol=0.1)
        self.assertTrue(b.mag_ok and b.button)
        self.assertEqual(b.size, 26)
        bad = bytearray(new)
        bad[20] ^= 0xFF
        self.assertEqual(list(glove_receiver.parse_frames(bytes(bad))), [])

    def test_arms_keep_separate_ports_data_and_models(self):
        left, right = punch_session.ARMS["left"], punch_session.ARMS["right"]
        self.assertEqual((left.port, right.port), (5005, 5006))
        self.assertNotEqual(left.data_dir, right.data_dir)
        self.assertNotEqual(left.model_path, right.model_path)
        self.assertEqual(left.data_dir, punch_session.DATA_DIR)  # the left arm's existing recordings stay put
        self.assertEqual(right.labels, ("CROSS", "HOOK", "UPPERCUT"))

    def test_live_rows_with_and_without_magnetometer(self):
        plain = [(0.0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, False, 0, 0, 0, False)] * 3
        withmag = [(0.0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, False, 20, 0, -40, True)] * 3
        self.assertNotIn("mag", punch_session.imu_arrays(plain))
        self.assertEqual(punch_session.imu_arrays(withmag)["mag"].shape, (3, 3))

    def test_right_arm_pose_features_are_mirrored(self):
        # a right hook swings out to the RIGHT first; mirrored, it should look like a left hook does
        frames = 12
        world = np.zeros((frames, 33, 3))
        world[:, 11], world[:, 12] = [0.2, -0.5, 0], [-0.2, -0.5, 0]   # MediaPipe: left shoulder at +x
        world[:, 14], world[:, 24] = [-0.25, -0.3, -0.1], [-0.1, 0.0, 0]
        x = np.concatenate([np.linspace(-0.3, -0.55, 4), np.linspace(-0.55, 0.1, 8)])  # out right, then across
