content.text:
The model is trained and saved to `models/punch_rf.joblib`. Cross-validated, it scores **99%** on all 119 punches (one hook was read as an uppercut).

| Features | Overall | Trained on one session, tested on the other |
|---|---|---|
| Glove only | 98% | **56%** |
| Camera only | 99% | 99% |
| Both (what plays) | 99% | 94% |

The glove-only 56% is expected. The new sensor sits at a different angle from the old one, so a model trained only on the old glove data doesn't carry over. The model you'll play with learned from both sessions, including today's 60 punches with this sensor, so it knows how the new glove reads. The camera carries over perfectly.

**One gap: there are no not-a-punch examples yet.** In play, any hard movement, such as a guard reset or a feint, will be read as a jab, hook or uppercut. Your next session can fix that:
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe punch_capture.py --target 45 --person andre
```
During the "MOVE, DON'T PUNCH" rounds, move sharply: snap your guard, feint, bob and weave. A movement only counts once it's about as hard as a punch. You'd see "saved NONE" lines in the terminal. Then run `punch_train.py` again.

To play now:
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe punch_live.py --live --windowed
```
Calibrate with **C**, then press **F8** to turn keys on. If it presses keys for movements that weren't punches, press **]** to make it stricter.

The old-sensor data is out, and the model trained on just today's 60 punches scores **100%** cross-validated: all 20 jabs, 20 hooks and 20 uppercuts correct. That's with the glove and camera together, and the glove alone also gets 100% now. The model is saved to `models/punch_rf.joblib`, so `punch_live.py` uses it straight away.

The old recordings aren't deleted. All 59 are in `punch_data/_old_mpu6050/`, which training and recording ignore because the folder name starts with `_`. To bring them back, move the JAB/HOOK/UPPERCUT folders back into `punch_data/`. I used `git mv`, so git tracks this as a move, not a deletion. It isn't committed yet.

Take the 100% with some caution. It comes from 60 punches recorded in one session, so it may drop on another day. It still has **no not-a-punch examples**, so hard movements that aren't punches will press keys. Your next recording round can fix both:
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe punch_capture.py --target 40 --person andre
```
Move sharply during the "MOVE, DON'T PUNCH" rounds, then run `punch_train.py` again.

To play now: `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe punch_live.py --live --windowed`. Press C to calibrate, then F8 to turn keys on.

**Button pin: GPIO12, wired to GND.** The firmware already reads it there (debounced) and sends its state in every frame. Never connect GPIO12 to 3V3, or the board won't boot.

A few design choices change what I build:

options.label: Block off, duck/slip on (Recommended)
options.description: Aiming can't trigger a block by accident; ducking and slipping (head and torso movement) still work while you look around.

options.label: All defence stays on
options.description: Everything works while aiming. Risk: raising your right hand to look up may register as a block.

options.label: All defence off
options.description: While the button is held, only aiming and punches (mouse clicks) work.

options.description: The view follows your hand directly: move the hand 10 cm and the view turns a fixed amount, then stops. Running out of reach means release and re-press.

"""Turn boxing events into keyboard input, so existing games can be played with your body.

  tap  - a punch. The key is pressed, then released a few milliseconds later. Games read the key
         state once per frame, so a press that is released instantly can be missed.
  hold - a body state (block, duck, slip). The key stays down while the state lasts.

Keys are sent as hardware scan codes with the Windows SendInput call. Browsers and DirectInput games
accept these; many games ignore the plain virtual-key events that most keyboard libraries send.

The event names are the labels pose_tracker.py already produces: JAB, CROSS, HOOK, UPPERCUT for
punches and BLOCK, DUCK, SLIP LEFT, SLIP RIGHT, GUARD DOWN for body states. A mapping file (see
mappings/) says which key each one presses.

import atexit
import ctypes
import json
import os
import sys
import threading
import time

SCAN_CODES = {
    **dict(zip("qwertyuiop", range(0x10, 0x1A))),
    **dict(zip("asdfghjkl", range(0x1E, 0x27))),
    **dict(zip("zxcvbnm", range(0x2C, 0x33))),
    **dict(zip("1234567890", range(0x02, 0x0C))),
    "space": 0x39, "enter": 0x1C, "esc": 0x01, "tab": 0x0F,
    "shift": 0x2A, "ctrl": 0x1D, "alt": 0x38,
    "comma": 0x33, "period": 0x34, "semicolon": 0x27,
    "up": 0x48, "down": 0x50, "left": 0x4B, "right": 0x4D,
}
EXTENDED_KEYS = {"up", "down", "left", "right"}

KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY, KEYEVENTF_KEYUP, KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE = 0x0001, 0x0002, 0x0008
INPUT_KEYBOARD = 1

    ULONG_PTR = ctypes.c_ulonglong if ctypes.sizeof(ctypes.c_void_p) == 8 else ctypes.c_ulong

    class _KeyBdInput(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [("wVk", wintypes.WORD), ("wScan", wintypes.WORD), ("dwFlags", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("time", wintypes.DWORD), ("dwExtraInfo", ULONG_PTR)]

    class _MouseInput(ctypes.Structure):  # unused, but it sets the size of the INPUT union
        _fields_ = [("dx", wintypes.LONG), ("dy", wintypes.LONG), ("mouseData", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("dwFlags", wintypes.DWORD), ("time", wintypes.DWORD), ("dwExtraInfo", ULONG_PTR)]

    class _HardwareInput(ctypes.Structure):  # unused, same reason
        _fields_ = [("uMsg", wintypes.DWORD), ("wParamL", wintypes.WORD), ("wParamH", wintypes.WORD)]

        _fields_ = [("ki", _KeyBdInput), ("mi", _MouseInput), ("hi", _HardwareInput)]

    class _Input(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [("type", wintypes.DWORD), ("u", _InputUnion)]

        if not is_down:
            flags |= KEYEVENTF_KEYUP

    def load(cls, path):

        timer.daemon = True
        timer.start()
        return True

        """states = the labels active right now, e.g. {"BLOCK", "SLIP LEFT"}. Keys follow the changes."""
        wanted = set()
        if self.enabled:
            wanted = {self.mapping.holds[s.upper()] for s in states if s.upper() in self.mapping.holds}
        for key in self._state_keys - wanted:
            self.keyboard.release(key)
        for key in wanted - self._state_keys:
            self.keyboard.press(key)
        self._state_keys = wanted

    def set_enabled(self, on):
        """Switch key output on or off. Turning it off lets go of every key."""
        self.enabled = on
        if not on:
            self.set_states(())
            self.keyboard.release_all()

    def close(self):
        self.set_enabled(False)

    for kind, key in game_input.mapping.taps.items():
        print(f"  punch {kind} -> tap {key}")
        game_input.punch(kind)
        time.sleep(0.4)
    for state, key in game_input.mapping.holds.items():
        print(f"  state {state} -> hold {key} for 0.6 s")
        game_input.set_states({state})
        time.sleep(0.6)

        time.sleep(0.2)

    parser.add_argument("--mapping", default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "mappings", "browser_boxing.json"))
    parser.add_argument("--live", action="store_true", help="really press keys (default: only print them)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    mapping = Mapping.load(args.mapping)
    print(f"Game: {mapping.game}")
    if args.live:
        print("LIVE: keys will be sent to the window that has focus. Click the game now.")
        for n in range(5, 0, -1):

            time.sleep(1)

def main(on_punch=None, on_states=None, on_frame=None, want_calibrate=None, on_calibrated=None,
         on_features=None, on_draw=None, builtin_punches=True, camera_index=0, on_pose=None,
         fullscreen=False):
    """Run the tracker. Run on its own it only draws; the callbacks let other code react.

    on_punch(kind, side, speed): a punch was recognised. kind is JAB, CROSS, HOOK or UPPERCUT.
    on_states(states): called every frame with the body-state labels active right now (BLOCK, DUCK,
        SLIP LEFT, SLIP RIGHT, GUARD DOWN). It gets an empty list when nobody is in view.
    on_frame(): called every frame; return True to stop the tracker.
    want_calibrate(): called every frame; return True to request a calibration. It happens
        CALIBRATE_DELAY_S (5 s) later, with a countdown on screen, so the boxer can get into guard.
        This lets a hotkey recalibrate while another window (the game) has focus. The c key in the
        camera window always works too.
    on_calibrated(): called when the calibration actually happens, after the countdown.
    on_features(now, speeds, travel, from_low): the raw numbers the punch decision uses, every frame.
        speeds = [left, right] wrist speed; travel = 2x3 array of (extension, right, up) per hand;
        from_low = [left, right] wrist started below the elbow. It may return a list of (side, kind)
        punches it decided; those are shown on screen and passed to on_punch.
    on_draw(frame): draw extra text on the camera image before it is shown.
    builtin_punches: set False to switch off this file's own punch check, so only the punches
        returned by on_features count (see punch_detector.py).
    camera_index: which camera to open (0 is the default webcam).
    on_pose(world, visibility): called every frame a body is found, with the 33 smoothed 3D world
        landmarks (metres, origin at the hips) and how visible each one is.
    fullscreen: show the camera window full screen. set_fullscreen() switches it while running.
    Layout: this function draws its calibration messages in the bottom BOTTOM_RESERVED pixels of the
    camera image; on_draw should keep its own text above that, so nothing covers them.
    """
    ensure_model()
    landmarker = vision.PoseLandmarker.create_from_options(vision.PoseLandmarkerOptions(
        base_options=mp_python.BaseOptions(model_asset_path=MODEL_PATH),
        running_mode=vision.RunningMode.VIDEO,
        min_pose_detection_confidence=0.4,
        min_pose_presence_confidence=0.4,
        min_tracking_confidence=0.4,
    ))
    cap = cv2.VideoCapture(camera_index)
    if not cap.isOpened():
        raise SystemExit("Could not open webcam")

    smooth_img, smooth_world = Smoother(0.6), Smoother(0.7)
    yaw = 0.0  # 3D view rotation
    cv2.namedWindow("Pose", cv2.WINDOW_NORMAL | cv2.WINDOW_KEEPRATIO)  # resizable, so it can go full screen
    if fullscreen:
        set_fullscreen(True)
    cv2.namedWindow("3D skeleton")
    cv2.moveWindow("3D skeleton", 700, 50)  # beside the camera window, not on top of it
    history = deque(maxlen=5)  # (time, wrist-relative-to-shoulder, wrist-below-elbow), ~0.2 s
    baseline = None
    calibrated_at = -10.0  # when the last calibration happened, for the on-screen flash
    calibrate_at = None    # when a requested calibration will happen (it waits CALIBRATE_DELAY_S)
    last_punch = {"L": 0.0, "R": 0.0}
    flash = {"L": ("", 0.0), "R": ("", 0.0)}
    t0 = time.time()

    failed_reads = 0
    while True:
        ok, frame = cap.read()
        if not ok or frame is None:
            # Some webcams return empty frames for the first moment after opening. Wait before giving up.
            failed_reads += 1
            if failed_reads > 150:  # about 3 seconds of nothing
                break
            time.sleep(0.02)
            continue
        failed_reads = 0
        now = time.time()
        rgb = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
        result = landmarker.detect_for_video(
            mp.Image(image_format=mp.ImageFormat.SRGB, data=rgb), int((now - t0) * 1000))
        frame = cv2.flip(frame, 1)  # mirror for display only; image x is flipped to match
        lines = ["no body detected"]

        if result.pose_landmarks:
            lm = result.pose_landmarks[0]
            img = smooth_img(np.array([[1 - p.x, p.y] for p in lm]))
            vis = np.array([p.visibility for p in lm])
            world = smooth_world(np.array([[p.x, p.y, p.z] for p in result.pose_world_landmarks[0]]))
            sw = np.linalg.norm(world[L_SH] - world[R_SH]) + 1e-6
            if on_pose:
                on_pose(world, vis)

            wrist_below_elbow = world[[L_WR, R_WR], 1] > world[[L_EL, R_EL], 1]  # world y points down
            history.append((now, world[[L_WR, R_WR]] - world[[L_SH, R_SH]], wrist_below_elbow))
            dt = now - history[0][0]
            speeds = [0.0, 0.0]
            if dt > 0:
                delta = (history[-1][1] - history[0][1]) / sw
                travel = punch_travel(delta, history[0][1], history[-1][1], world, sw)
                for i, side in enumerate("LR"):
                    speeds[i] = np.linalg.norm(delta[i]) / dt
                    if builtin_punches and speeds[i] > PUNCH_SPEED and now - last_punch[side] > PUNCH_COOLDOWN:
                        kind = classify_punch(side, travel[i], history[0][2][i])
                        ext, right, up = travel[i]
                        print(f"{side} {kind} speed={speeds[i]:.1f} extension={ext:.2f} right={right:.2f} up={up:.2f} low={history[0][2][i]}")
                        if kind:
                            last_punch[side] = now
                            flash[side] = (f"{kind} {speeds[i]:.1f}", now)
                            if on_punch:
                                on_punch(kind, side, speeds[i])
                if on_features:
                    for side, kind in on_features(now, list(speeds), travel, list(history[0][2])) or ():
                        flash[side] = (kind, now)
                        if on_punch:
                            on_punch(kind, side, speeds["LR".index(side)])

            states = body_state(img, world, sw, baseline)
            if on_states:
                on_states(states)
            lines = [" | ".join(states) or "ok",
                     f"speed L {speeds[0]:.1f}  R {speeds[1]:.1f}"]
            draw(frame, img, vis, flash, now)
            cv2.imshow("3D skeleton", draw_3d(world, vis, yaw))
        else:
            cv2.imshow("3D skeleton", np.zeros((480, 480, 3), np.uint8))
            if on_states:
                on_states([])  # nobody in view: let go of any held keys

        for n, text in enumerate(lines):
            cv2.putText(frame, text, (10, 30 + 30 * n), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.8, (255, 255, 255), 2)
        if calibrate_at is not None:
            cv2.putText(frame, f"GET IN GUARD - calibrating in {max(0.0, calibrate_at - now):.0f}",
                        (10, frame.shape[0] - 45), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 1.0, (0, 255, 255), 3)
        if baseline is None:
            cv2.putText(frame, "press C, then get in guard: it calibrates 5 s later", (10, frame.shape[0] - 15),
                        cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.6, (0, 255, 255), 2)
        else:
            if now - calibrated_at < 1.5:
                cv2.putText(frame, "CALIBRATED", (10, frame.shape[0] - 45),
                            cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 1.0, (0, 255, 0), 3)
            cv2.putText(frame, "C = recalibrate", (10, frame.shape[0] - 15),
                        cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5, (200, 200, 200), 1)
        if on_draw:
            on_draw(frame)
        cv2.imshow("Pose", frame)
        if on_frame and on_frame():
            break
        key = cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF
        requested = key == ord("c") or bool(want_calibrate and want_calibrate())
        if requested and calibrate_at is None:
            # Design rule: calibration waits CALIBRATE_DELAY_S after the request, so the boxer can get
            # into guard after pressing the key (or after clicking back to the game for F7).
            calibrate_at = now + CALIBRATE_DELAY_S
            print(f"Calibrating in {CALIBRATE_DELAY_S:g} s: get into your guard")
        if calibrate_at is not None and now >= calibrate_at:

            print(f"Warning: start {args.start_g:g} g is far from the {trained:g} g the model was trained with, so it "
                  "may be less accurate. Retrain with this value for best results.")

    import game_input
    mapping = game_input.Mapping.load(args.mapping)
    keyboard = game_input.SendInputKeyboard() if args.live else game_input.DryRunKeyboard()
    game = game_input.GameInput(mapping, keyboard)
    game.set_enabled(not args.live)  # a dry run is harmless, so it starts on; live starts off

    sensors = ps.LiveSensors(clf.segment, simulate=args.simulate, port=args.port, arm=arm)
    play = LivePlay(sensors, clf, game)

    # Defence keys, calibration and the F7/F8/F9 hotkeys come from controller.py; punches come from the model.
    callbacks = controller.make_callbacks(game, controller.Hotkeys(), detector=False)
    callbacks.pop("on_punch")
    hotkey_frame = callbacks["on_frame"]
    sensitivity_keys = controller.Hotkeys()
    popup = popup_window.Popup(args.popup_size, args.popup_corner) if args.popup else None
    fullscreen = not args.windowed and not popup  # a corner popup is never full screen
    screen_keys = ps.ToolKeys(fullscreen=fullscreen)
    started_confidence, started = clf.min_confidence, time.time()

    def on_frame():
        play.poll()
        if not popup:
            screen_keys.poll_fullscreen()
        if sensitivity_keys.pressed(VK_LOWER):
            play.adjust_confidence(-0.05)
        if sensitivity_keys.pressed(VK_RAISE):
            play.adjust_confidence(+0.05)
        return hotkey_frame() or bool(args.max_seconds and time.time() - started > args.max_seconds)

    callbacks.update(sensors.pose_callbacks())
    def on_draw(frame):
        if popup:
            play.on_draw_popup(frame)
            popup.update(frame)
        else:
            play.on_draw(frame)

    callbacks.update(on_frame=on_frame, on_draw=on_draw, camera_index=args.camera, fullscreen=fullscreen)

    print(f"Model trained {clf.info['trained_at']} on {clf.info['counts']}, "

"""Turn boxing events into keyboard input, so existing games can be played with your body.

Two kinds of key output:
  tap  - a punch. The key is pressed, then released a few milliseconds later. Games read the key
         state once per frame, so a press that is released instantly can be missed.
  hold - a body state (block, duck, slip). The key stays down while the state lasts.

Keys are sent as hardware scan codes with the Windows SendInput call. Browsers and DirectInput games
accept these; many games ignore the plain virtual-key events that most keyboard libraries send.

The event names are the labels pose_tracker.py already produces: JAB, CROSS, HOOK, UPPERCUT for
punches and BLOCK, DUCK, SLIP LEFT, SLIP RIGHT, GUARD DOWN for body states. A mapping file (see
mappings/) says which key each one presses.

Run `python game_input.py` for a dry run that only prints. `--live` really presses keys.
"""
import argparse
import atexit
import ctypes
import json
import os
import sys
import threading
import time

# Hardware scan codes (set 1). Arrow keys are "extended" keys and need the extended flag.
SCAN_CODES = {
    **dict(zip("qwertyuiop", range(0x10, 0x1A))),
    **dict(zip("asdfghjkl", range(0x1E, 0x27))),
    **dict(zip("zxcvbnm", range(0x2C, 0x33))),
    **dict(zip("1234567890", range(0x02, 0x0C))),
    "space": 0x39, "enter": 0x1C, "esc": 0x01, "tab": 0x0F,
    "shift": 0x2A, "ctrl": 0x1D, "alt": 0x38,
    "comma": 0x33, "period": 0x34, "semicolon": 0x27,
    "up": 0x48, "down": 0x50, "left": 0x4B, "right": 0x4D,
}
EXTENDED_KEYS = {"up", "down", "left", "right"}

KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY, KEYEVENTF_KEYUP, KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE = 0x0001, 0x0002, 0x0008
INPUT_KEYBOARD = 1

if sys.platform == "win32":
    from ctypes import wintypes

    ULONG_PTR = ctypes.c_ulonglong if ctypes.sizeof(ctypes.c_void_p) == 8 else ctypes.c_ulong

    class _KeyBdInput(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [("wVk", wintypes.WORD), ("wScan", wintypes.WORD), ("dwFlags", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("time", wintypes.DWORD), ("dwExtraInfo", ULONG_PTR)]

    class _MouseInput(ctypes.Structure):  # unused, but it sets the size of the INPUT union
        _fields_ = [("dx", wintypes.LONG), ("dy", wintypes.LONG), ("mouseData", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("dwFlags", wintypes.DWORD), ("time", wintypes.DWORD), ("dwExtraInfo", ULONG_PTR)]

    class _HardwareInput(ctypes.Structure):  # unused, same reason
        _fields_ = [("uMsg", wintypes.DWORD), ("wParamL", wintypes.WORD), ("wParamH", wintypes.WORD)]

    class _InputUnion(ctypes.Union):
        _fields_ = [("ki", _KeyBdInput), ("mi", _MouseInput), ("hi", _HardwareInput)]

    class _Input(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [("type", wintypes.DWORD), ("u", _InputUnion)]

    _user32 = ctypes.WinDLL("user32", use_last_error=True)
    _user32.SendInput.argtypes = (wintypes.UINT, ctypes.POINTER(_Input), ctypes.c_int)
    _user32.SendInput.restype = wintypes.UINT


def check_key(key):
    """Return the key name in lower case, or raise if there is no scan code for it."""
    key = key.lower()
    if key not in SCAN_CODES:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown key {key!r}; known keys: {', '.join(sorted(SCAN_CODES))}")
    return key


class Keyboard:
    """Remembers which keys are down, so none can be left stuck down."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.down = set()
        self.lock = threading.RLock()  # taps release from a timer thread

    def press(self, key):
        with self.lock:
            if key not in self.down:
                self._send(key, True)
                self.down.add(key)

    def release(self, key):
        with self.lock:
            if key in self.down:
                self._send(key, False)
                self.down.discard(key)

    def release_all(self):
        with self.lock:
            for key in list(self.down):
                self.release(key)

    def _send(self, key, is_down):
        raise NotImplementedError


class DryRunKeyboard(Keyboard):
    """Prints instead of pressing anything."""

    def _send(self, key, is_down):
        print(f"    key {'DOWN' if is_down else 'UP  '} {key}")


def release_keys_when_console_ends(keyboard):
    """Release every held key if the console is closed, Ctrl+C or Ctrl+Break arrives, or Windows shuts down.

    atexit does not run when the console window is closed, and a key left pressed would stay down in
    the operating system until you tapped it again. Windows only.
    """
    if sys.platform != "win32":
        return
    handler_type = ctypes.WINFUNCTYPE(wintypes.BOOL, wintypes.DWORD)

    def handler(event):
        keyboard.release_all()
        return False  # carry on with Windows' normal handling, which ends the program

    keyboard._console_handler = handler_type(handler)  # keep a reference so it is not garbage collected
    kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
    kernel32.SetConsoleCtrlHandler.argtypes = (handler_type, wintypes.BOOL)
    kernel32.SetConsoleCtrlHandler.restype = wintypes.BOOL
    if not kernel32.SetConsoleCtrlHandler(keyboard._console_handler, True):
        raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())


class SendInputKeyboard(Keyboard):
    """Presses real keys on Windows. Input goes to whichever window has focus."""

    def __init__(self):
        if sys.platform != "win32":
            raise OSError("live key presses are only supported on Windows")
        super().__init__()
        release_keys_when_console_ends(self)

    def _send(self, key, is_down):
        flags = KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE
        if key in EXTENDED_KEYS:
            flags |= KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY
        if not is_down:
            flags |= KEYEVENTF_KEYUP
        event = _Input(type=INPUT_KEYBOARD, u=_InputUnion(ki=_KeyBdInput(0, SCAN_CODES[key], flags, 0, 0)))
        if _user32.SendInput(1, ctypes.byref(event), ctypes.sizeof(event)) != 1:
            raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())


class Mapping:
    """Which key each event presses. Loaded from a JSON file in mappings/."""

    def __init__(self, data):
        self.game = data.get("game", "")
        self.tap_hold = data.get("tap_hold_ms", 50) / 1000
        self.taps = {name.upper(): check_key(key) for name, key in data.get("taps", {}).items()}
        self.holds = {name.upper(): check_key(key) for name, key in data.get("holds", {}).items()}

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return cls(json.load(f))


class GameInput:
    """Call punch() when a punch lands and set_states() every frame with the current body states."""

    def __init__(self, mapping, keyboard):
        self.mapping, self.keyboard = mapping, keyboard
        self.enabled = True
        self._state_keys = set()  # keys currently held because of a body state
        atexit.register(self.close)  # normal exit or an uncaught error; a hard kill can still leave keys down

    def punch(self, kind):
        """Tap the key mapped to this punch. Returns True if a key was sent."""
        key = self.mapping.taps.get(kind.upper())
        if key is None or not self.enabled or key in self.keyboard.down:
            return False
        self.keyboard.press(key)
        timer = threading.Timer(self.mapping.tap_hold, self.keyboard.release, (key,))
        timer.daemon = True
        timer.start()
        return True

    def set_states(self, states):
        """states = the labels active right now, e.g. {"BLOCK", "SLIP LEFT"}. Keys follow the changes."""
        wanted = set()
        if self.enabled:
            wanted = {self.mapping.holds[s.upper()] for s in states if s.upper() in self.mapping.holds}
        for key in self._state_keys - wanted:
            self.keyboard.release(key)
        for key in wanted - self._state_keys:
            self.keyboard.press(key)
        self._state_keys = wanted

    def set_enabled(self, on):
        """Switch key output on or off. Turning it off lets go of every key."""
        self.enabled = on
        if not on:
            self.set_states(())
            self.keyboard.release_all()

    def close(self):
        self.set_enabled(False)


def demo(game_input):
    """Walk through every mapped punch and body state once."""
    for kind, key in game_input.mapping.taps.items():
        print(f"  punch {kind} -> tap {key}")
        game_input.punch(kind)
        time.sleep(0.4)
    for state, key in game_input.mapping.holds.items():
        print(f"  state {state} -> hold {key} for 0.6 s")
        game_input.set_states({state})
        time.sleep(0.6)
        game_input.set_states(())
        time.sleep(0.2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--mapping", default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "mappings", "browser_boxing.json"))
    parser.add_argument("--live", action="store_true", help="really press keys (default: only print them)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    mapping = Mapping.load(args.mapping)
    print(f"Game: {mapping.game}")
    if args.live:
        print("LIVE: keys will be sent to the window that has focus. Click the game now.")
        for n in range(5, 0, -1):
            print(f"  starting in {n}...")
            time.sleep(1)
        keyboard = SendInputKeyboard()
    else:
        print("Dry run: printing keys only. Use --live to press them.")
        keyboard = DryRunKeyboard()
    demo(GameInput(mapping, keyboard))
    print("Done.")

input.content:
"""Tracking mode: while the glove button is held, the RIGHT hand steers the mouse like a joystick.

Where the right hand was when the button went down is the centre. From there:
  hand right / left  -> mouse right / left
  hand up / down     -> mouse up / down
Two styles, chosen in controls_editor.py (the "aim" settings in the controls file):
  speed     like a thumbstick: the further the hand is from the centre, the faster the view turns, and
            it keeps turning while the hand stays out. A small dead zone keeps a still hand from drifting.
  position  like a trackpad: the view follows the hand. Move it 10 cm and the view turns a fixed amount.
While the button is held, punches use the "tracking" set of controls (by default jab = left click,
hook = right click, uppercut = middle click), and the camera's BLOCK is off unless the settings say
otherwise, because a steering hand sits up near the face.

The hand position comes from the camera: the right wrist relative to the right shoulder, in shoulder
widths, in the body's own frame. So ducking or slipping moves the whole body and does not move the aim.

"""Tracking mode: while the glove button is held, the RIGHT hand steers the mouse like a joystick.

Where the right hand was when the button went down is the centre. From there:
  hand right / left  -> mouse right / left
  hand up / down     -> mouse up / down
Two styles, chosen in controls_editor.py (the "aim" settings in the controls file):
  speed     like a thumbstick: the further the hand is from the centre, the faster the view turns, and
            it keeps turning while the hand stays out. A small dead zone keeps a still hand from drifting.
  position  like a trackpad: the view follows the hand. Move it 10 cm and the view turns a fixed amount.
While the button is held, punches use the "tracking" set of controls (by default jab = left click,
hook = right click, uppercut = middle click), and the camera's BLOCK is off unless the settings say
otherwise, because a steering hand sits up near the face.

The hand position comes from the camera: the right wrist relative to the right shoulder, in shoulder
widths, in the body's own frame. So ducking or slipping moves the whole body and does not move the aim.
The camera updates about 30 times a second; AimDriver sends the mouse movement 250 times a second, so
it moves smoothly instead of in steps.
"""
import threading
import time

import numpy as np

L_SH, R_SH, R_WR = 11, 12, 16
FULL = 0.5          # shoulder widths from the centre that count as "full stick"
SMOOTH_S = 0.05     # position mode: how quickly the mouse catches up with the hand
MOVE_HZ = 250


def hand_offset(world, vis, min_visibility=0.5):
    """The right wrist relative to the right shoulder as (right, up) in shoulder widths, or None when
    the camera cannot see it well. world is MediaPipe's 33 x 3 world landmarks (y points down)."""
    if world is None or vis is None or vis[R_WR] < min_visibility:
        return None
    across = world[R_SH] - world[L_SH]
    width = np.linalg.norm(across)
    if width < 1e-6:
        return None
    right = np.array([across[0], 0.0, across[2]])
    right /= np.linalg.norm(right) + 1e-9
    rel = (world[R_WR] - world[R_SH]) / width
    return np.array([rel @ right, -rel[1]])


class Aim:
    """Turns hand offsets into mouse movement. Thread-safe: update() from the camera loop, take() from
    the driver thread."""

    def __init__(self, settings):
        self.settings = dict(settings)
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.active = False
        self.centre = None
        self.offset = None        # latest hand position relative to the centre, shoulder widths
        self.velocity = np.zeros(2)   # speed mode, pixels per second (screen: +x right, +y down)
        self.target = np.zeros(2)     # position mode, pixels from where the mouse was at the start
        self.sent = np.zeros(2)       # position mode, pixels already sent
        self.carry = np.zeros(2)      # fractions of a pixel not sent yet

    def start(self, hand):
        with self.lock:
            self.active = hand is not None
            self.centre = None if hand is None else np.array(hand, dtype=float)
            self.offset = np.zeros(2) if self.active else None
            self.velocity[:] = 0
            self.target[:] = 0
            self.sent[:] = 0
            self.carry[:] = 0

    def stop(self):
        with self.lock:
            self.active, self.centre, self.offset = False, None, None
            self.velocity[:] = 0

    def _screen(self, d):
        """Hand offset (right, up) -> screen direction (+x right, +y down), with the settings applied."""
        s = self.settings
        flip = -1.0 if s.get("invert_y") else 1.0
        return np.array([d[0], -d[1] * s.get("vertical_scale", 1.0) * flip])

    def update(self, hand):
        """Call every camera frame with hand_offset(), or None if the hand is not visible."""
        with self.lock:
            if not self.active:
                return
            if self.centre is None:          # the button went down while the hand was out of view
                if hand is not None:
                    self.centre = np.array(hand, dtype=float)
                return
            if hand is None:                 # lost the hand: stop turning, keep the position target
                self.velocity[:] = 0
                return
            d = np.array(hand, dtype=float) - self.centre
            self.offset = d
            s = self.settings
            if s.get("mode", "speed") == "position":
                self.target = self._screen(d) * s.get("position_gain", 1500)
            else:
                size = float(np.linalg.norm(d))
                dz = s.get("dead_zone", 0.06)
                if size <= dz:
                    self.velocity[:] = 0
                else:
                    push = min((size - dz) / FULL, 1.5) ** s.get("curve", 1.5)
                    self.velocity = self._screen(d / size) * push * s.get("speed", 1200)

    def take(self, dt):
        """Whole pixels to move now, after dt seconds. Fractions carry over to the next call."""
        with self.lock:
            if not self.active:
                return 0, 0
            if self.settings.get("mode", "speed") == "position":
                step = (self.target - self.sent) * (1 - np.exp(-dt / SMOOTH_S))
                self.sent += step
            else:
                step = self.velocity * dt
            step = step + self.carry
            whole = np.trunc(step)
            self.carry = step - whole
            return int(whole[0]), int(whole[1])


class AimDriver:
    """Sends the Aim's movement to the game 250 times a second, on its own thread."""

    def __init__(self, aim, game):
        self.aim, self.game = aim, game
        self.stop_flag = threading.Event()
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self._run, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()

    def _run(self):
        last = time.perf_counter()
        while not self.stop_flag.wait(1 / MOVE_HZ):
            now = time.perf_counter()
            dx, dy = self.aim.take(now - last)
            last = now
            if dx or dy:
                self.game.move(dx, dy)

    def close(self):
        self.stop_flag.set()


class Tracking:
    """Glue for punch_live.py: watches the glove button, switches the game to the tracking set, and
    feeds the right hand to the Aim. Call poll() every camera frame."""

    def __init__(self, sensors, game, log=print):
        self.sensors, self.game, self.log = sensors, game, log
        self.aim = Aim(game.mapping.aim)
        self.driver = AimDriver(self.aim, game)
        self.held = False

    def set_settings(self, settings):
        self.aim.settings = dict(settings)

    def poll(self):
        held = bool(self.sensors.button) and self.sensors.glove_ok()
        hand = self._hand()
        if held != self.held:
            self.held = held
            self.game.set_tracking(held)
            if held:
                self.aim.start(hand)
                self.log(f"TRACKING ON ({self.aim.settings.get('mode', 'speed')} steering)"
                         + ("" if hand is not None else ": right hand not in view yet"))
            else:
                self.aim.stop()
                self.log("tracking off")
        if held:
            self.aim.update(hand)

    def _hand(self):
        latest = self.sensors.latest_pose()
        if latest is None or time.time() - latest[0] > 0.3:
            return None
        return hand_offset(latest[1], latest[2])

    def draw(self, frame, put, x=None, y=60, size=110):
        """A small joystick picture in the top-right corner of the camera image while tracking."""
        if not self.held:
            return
        import cv2
        h, w = frame.shape[:2]
        x = w - size - 20 if x is None else x
        c = (x + size // 2, y + size // 2)
        cv2.rectangle(frame, (x, y), (x + size, y + size), (0, 220, 0), 2)
        dz = int(self.aim.settings.get("dead_zone", 0.06) / FULL * size / 2)
        if self.aim.settings.get("mode", "speed") == "speed" and dz > 0:
            cv2.circle(frame, c, dz, (120, 120, 120), 1)
        offset = self.aim.offset
        if offset is not None:
            # the camera image is mirrored for display, so the boxer's right is on the right of the picture
            px = int(np.clip(offset[0] / FULL, -1, 1) * size / 2)
            py = int(np.clip(-offset[1] / FULL, -1, 1) * size / 2)
            cv2.line(frame, c, (c[0] + px, c[1] + py), (0, 220, 0), 2)
            cv2.circle(frame, (c[0] + px, c[1] + py), 6, (0, 255, 0), -1)
        else:
            put(frame, "no hand", y + size // 2, (0, 0, 255), 0.5, x=x + 8)
        put(frame, f"TRACKING ({self.aim.settings.get('mode', 'speed')})", y - 8, (0, 255, 0), 0.5, x=x - 40)

    def close(self):
        self.driver.close()
        self.game.set_tracking(False)

"""Edit the boxing controls like a game's keybind menu.

  python controls_editor.py                          edits mappings/controls.json
  python controls_editor.py --mapping other.json     edits another controls file (made if missing)

Click a bind, then press a key or click a mouse button to bind it. Esc cancels; the x clears a bind.
Three sets:
  Normal    punches while the glove button is up
  Tracking  punches while the glove button is held (the right hand steers the mouse)
  Defence   camera body states (block, duck, slip), held while they last
Hold is how long a punch keeps its key or mouse button down; some games miss very short presses.
Steering: speed (like a thumbstick) or position (like a trackpad), and how fast.

Every change is saved straight away, and a running punch_live.py picks it up within a second, so you
can tune it with the game open. Warnings show binds that clash (two actions on one key while both can
be active) and keys the tools already use as hotkeys.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys

import game_input as gi

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DEFAULT_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "mappings", "controls.json")
HOTKEYS = {"f7": "calibrate", "f8": "key output on/off", "f9": "quit", "f11": "full screen",
           "bracketleft": "confidence down", "bracketright": "confidence up", "period": "start/pause"}
TK_KEYS = {
    "space": "space", "return": "enter", "tab": "tab", "backspace": "backspace", "caps_lock": "capslock",
    "shift_l": "shift", "shift_r": "shift", "control_l": "ctrl", "control_r": "ctrl", "alt_l": "alt", "alt_r": "alt",
    "up": "up", "down": "down", "left": "left", "right": "right", "comma": "comma", "period": "period",
    "semicolon": "semicolon", "minus": "minus", "equal": "equals", "bracketleft": "bracketleft",
    "bracketright": "bracketright", "apostrophe": "quote", "grave": "grave", "backslash": "backslash",
    "slash": "slash", "insert": "insert", "delete": "delete", "home": "home", "end": "end",
    "prior": "pageup", "next": "pagedown",
}
TK_MOUSE = {1: "mouse_left", 2: "mouse_middle", 3: "mouse_right"}  # Tk's button numbers on Windows
NICE = {"mouse_left": "Left click", "mouse_right": "Right click", "mouse_middle": "Middle click",
        "bracketleft": "[", "bracketright": "]", "comma": ",", "period": ".", "semicolon": ";", "minus": "-",
        "equals": "=", "quote": "'", "grave": "`", "backslash": "\\", "slash": "/"}
LABELS = {"JAB": "Jab", "HOOK": "Hook", "UPPERCUT": "Uppercut", "CROSS": "Cross (right glove)",
          "BLOCK": "Block", "DUCK": "Duck", "SLIP LEFT": "Slip left", "SLIP RIGHT": "Slip right"}


def key_from_tk(keysym):
    """A Tk key name (event.keysym) -> our key name, or None if it cannot be sent to a game."""
    k = keysym.lower()
    if len(k) == 1 and k in gi.SCAN_CODES:
        return k
    if k.startswith("f") and k[1:].isdigit() and k in gi.SCAN_CODES:
        return k
    return TK_KEYS.get(k)


def nice(key):
    return "-" if not key else NICE.get(key, key.upper() if len(key) == 1 else key.capitalize())


def problems(mapping):
    """Warnings for the editor: clashing binds, and binds on the tools' own hotkeys."""
    out = []
    groups = [("normal", mapping.taps), ("tracking", mapping.tracking_taps)]
    for name, taps in groups:
        seen = {}
        for action, key in [*taps.items(), *mapping.holds.items()]:  # defence is active in both modes
            if key in seen:
                out.append(f"{nice(key)} is bound to both {LABELS.get(seen[key], seen[key])} and "
                           f"{LABELS.get(action, action)} ({name} + defence can be active together)")
            seen.setdefault(key, action)
    for key in sorted({*mapping.taps.values(), *mapping.tracking_taps.values(), *mapping.holds.values()}):
        if key in HOTKEYS:
            out.append(f"{nice(key)} is also the tools' {HOTKEYS[key]} hotkey")
    return sorted(set(out))


def load_or_default(path):
    if os.path.exists(path):
        return gi.Mapping.load(path)
    return gi.Mapping.load(DEFAULT_PATH) if os.path.exists(DEFAULT_PATH) else gi.Mapping({})


class Editor:
    def __init__(self, root, path):
        import tkinter as tk
        from tkinter import ttk
        self.tk, self.ttk, self.root, self.path = tk, ttk, root, path
        self.mapping = load_or_default(path)
        self.capturing = None   # (set name, action) waiting for a key
        self.buttons = {}       # (set name, action) -> bind button
        self.holds = {}         # (set name, action) -> IntVar of hold ms
        root.title("Boxing controls")
        root.minsize(720, 520)
        self._build()
        root.bind_all("<KeyPress>", self._on_key, add="+")
        root.bind_all("<ButtonPress>", self._on_mouse, add="+")
        self.refresh()

    # --- layout ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _build(self):
        tk, ttk = self.tk, self.ttk
        top = ttk.Frame(self.root, padding=8)

        body.pack(fill="both", expand=True)
        self._bind_group(body, "Normal  (glove button up)", "normal", gi.PUNCHES, True).grid(row=0, column=0, sticky="nsew", padx=4, pady=4)

    def _bind_group(self, parent, title, name, actions, with_hold):
        ttk = self.ttk
        box = ttk.LabelFrame(parent, text=title, padding=8)
        ttk.Label(box, text="Action").grid(row=0, column=0, sticky="w")
        ttk.Label(box, text="Bind").grid(row=0, column=1)

            ttk.Label(box, text="Hold (ms)").grid(row=0, column=3)
        for i, action in enumerate(actions, start=1):
            ttk.Label(box, text=LABELS.get(action, action)).grid(row=i, column=0, sticky="w", pady=2)
            b = ttk.Button(box, width=16, command=lambda n=name, a=action: self.start_capture(n, a))

            if with_hold:
                var = self.tk.IntVar()
                spin = ttk.Spinbox(box, from_=10, to=2000, increment=10, width=6, textvariable=var,
                                   command=lambda n=name, a=action: self.set_hold(n, a))
                spin.bind("<FocusOut>", lambda e, n=name, a=action: self.set_hold(n, a))
                spin.bind("<Return>", lambda e, n=name, a=action: self.set_hold(n, a))
                spin.grid(row=i, column=3, padx=4)
                self.holds[(name, action)] = var
        return box

    def _aim_group(self, parent):
        tk, ttk = self.tk, self.ttk
        box = ttk.LabelFrame(parent, text="Steering  (right hand, while the button is held)", padding=8)
        self.aim_vars = {}
        self.aim_vars["mode"] = tk.StringVar()

                        command=self.aim_changed).pack(side="left", padx=8)
        sliders = [("speed", "Speed (px/s)", 100, 5000, "speed"), ("curve", "Curve", 1.0, 3.0, "speed"),
                   ("dead_zone", "Dead zone", 0.0, 0.25, "speed"),
                   ("position_gain", "Sensitivity (px per shoulder width)", 200, 6000, "position"),
                   ("vertical_scale", "Vertical vs horizontal", 0.25, 2.0, None)]

                              command=lambda _v: self.aim_changed(save=False))
            scale.bind("<ButtonRelease-1>", lambda e: self.aim_changed())
            scale.grid(row=i, column=1, padx=4)

            value.grid(row=i, column=2)

                                         ("block_while_tracking", "Camera BLOCK works while tracking")]):
            var = tk.BooleanVar()
            self.aim_vars[key] = var

    def _set(self, name):
        m = self.mapping
        return {"normal": (m.taps, m.tap_s), "tracking": (m.tracking_taps, m.tracking_s), "defence": (m.holds, None)}[name]

        for (name, action), button in self.buttons.items():
            keys, _ = self._set(name)
            waiting = self.capturing == (name, action)
            button.configure(text="press a key or click..." if waiting else nice(keys.get(action)))

            _, hold = self._set(name)
            var.set(round(1000 * hold.get(action, 0.05 if name == "normal" else 0.15)))

        for key, var in self.aim_vars.items():
            var.set(aim[key])

        self.warnings.configure(text="\n".join("Warning: " + p for p in found))

        mode = self.aim_vars["mode"].get()
        for key, (label, scale, value, only) in self.sliders.items():
            v = self.aim_vars[key].get()
            value.configure(text=f"{v:.0f}" if v >= 100 else f"{v:.2f}")
            state = "!disabled" if only in (None, mode) else "disabled"
            scale.state([state])
            label.state([state])

    def start_capture(self, name, action):
        self.capturing = (name, action)
        self.say(f"Press a key or click a mouse button for {LABELS.get(action, action)} ({name}). Esc cancels.")
        self.refresh()

    def _on_key(self, event):
        if self.capturing is None:
            return
        if event.keysym == "Escape":
            self.capturing = None
            self.say("Cancelled.")
            self.refresh()
            return "break"
        key = key_from_tk(event.keysym)
        if key is None:

            return "break"

        self.set_bind(name, action, key)
        return "break"

    def _on_mouse(self, event):

            return

        self.capturing = None
        self.set_bind(name, action, TK_MOUSE[event.num])
        return "break"

        keys, hold = self._set(name)
        if key:
            keys[action] = key
            if hold is not None:
                hold.setdefault(action, 0.05 if name == "normal" else 0.15)
        else:
            keys.pop(action, None)
        self.capturing = None
        self.save(f"{LABELS.get(action, action)} ({name}) = {nice(key)}")

    def set_hold(self, name, action):
        try:
            ms = int(self.holds[(name, action)].get())
        except (ValueError, self.tk.TclError):
            return
        _, hold = self._set(name)
        ms = max(10, min(2000, ms))
        if round(1000 * hold.get(action, -1)) != ms:
            hold[action] = ms / 1000
            self.save(f"{LABELS.get(action, action)} ({name}) holds {ms} ms")

        aim = self.mapping.aim
        for key, var in self.aim_vars.items():
            v = var.get()
            aim[key] = round(v) if key in ("speed", "position_gain") else (round(v, 2) if isinstance(v, float) else v)
        self._show_aim_values()

            self.save("steering settings")

    def save(self, what=""):
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(self.path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
        tmp = self.path + ".tmp"
        self.mapping.save(tmp)
        os.replace(tmp, self.path)  # so punch_live never reads a half-written file
        self.say(f"Saved {what}. A running punch_live.py picks it up within a second.")
        self.refresh()

    def say(self, text):
        self.status.configure(text=text)

    def open(self):
        from tkinter import filedialog
        path = filedialog.askopenfilename(initialdir=os.path.dirname(self.path), filetypes=[("Controls", "*.json")])
        if path:
            self.path, self.mapping = path, load_or_default(path)
            self.say(f"Opened {os.path.basename(path)}")
            self.refresh()

    def save_as(self):
        from tkinter import filedialog
        path = filedialog.asksaveasfilename(initialdir=os.path.dirname(self.path), defaultextension=".json",
                                            filetypes=[("Controls", "*.json")])
        if path:
            self.path = path
            self.save(f"as {os.path.basename(path)}")

    def reset(self):
        self.mapping = gi.Mapping.load(DEFAULT_PATH) if os.path.abspath(self.path) != os.path.abspath(DEFAULT_PATH) \
            else gi.Mapping(json.loads(json.dumps(DEFAULTS)))
        self.save("the default controls")


DEFAULTS = {
    "game": "Default controls: edit with python controls_editor.py",
    "normal": {"JAB": {"bind": "j", "hold_ms": 50}, "HOOK": {"bind": "h", "hold_ms": 50},
               "UPPERCUT": {"bind": "u", "hold_ms": 50}, "CROSS": {"bind": "k", "hold_ms": 50}},
    "tracking": {"JAB": {"bind": "mouse_left", "hold_ms": 150}, "HOOK": {"bind": "mouse_right", "hold_ms": 150},
                 "UPPERCUT": {"bind": "mouse_middle", "hold_ms": 150}},
    "defence": {"BLOCK": "w", "DUCK": "s", "SLIP LEFT": "a", "SLIP RIGHT": "d"},
    "aim": dict(gi.AIM_DEFAULTS),
}


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--mapping", default=DEFAULT_PATH, help="controls file to edit")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    import tkinter as tk
    root = tk.Tk()
    Editor(root, os.path.abspath(args.mapping))
    root.mainloop()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Edit the boxing controls like a game's keybind menu.

  python controls_editor.py                          edits mappings/controls.json
  python controls_editor.py --mapping other.json     edits another controls file (made if missing)

Click a bind, then press a key or click a mouse button to bind it. Esc cancels; the x clears a bind.
Three sets:
  Normal    punches while the glove button is up
  Tracking  punches while the glove button is held (the right hand steers the mouse)
  Defence   camera body states (block, duck, slip), held while they last
Hold is how long a punch keeps its key or mouse button down; some games miss very short presses.
Steering: speed (like a thumbstick) or position (like a trackpad), and how fast.

Every change is saved straight away, and a running punch_live.py picks it up within a second, so you
can tune it with the game open. Warnings show binds that clash (two actions on one key while both can
be active) and keys the tools already use as hotkeys.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys

import game_input as gi

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DEFAULT_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "mappings", "controls.json")
HOTKEYS = {"f7": "calibrate", "f8": "key output on/off", "f9": "quit", "f11": "full screen",
           "bracketleft": "confidence down", "bracketright": "confidence up", "period": "start/pause"}
TK_KEYS = {
    "space": "space", "return": "enter", "tab": "tab", "backspace": "backspace", "caps_lock": "capslock",
    "shift_l": "shift", "shift_r": "shift", "control_l": "ctrl", "control_r": "ctrl", "alt_l": "alt", "alt_r": "alt",
    "up": "up", "down": "down", "left": "left", "right": "right", "comma": "comma", "period": "period",
    "semicolon": "semicolon", "minus": "minus", "equal": "equals", "bracketleft": "bracketleft",
    "bracketright": "bracketright", "apostrophe": "quote", "grave": "grave", "backslash": "backslash",
    "slash": "slash", "insert": "insert", "delete": "delete", "home": "home", "end": "end",
    "prior": "pageup", "next": "pagedown",
}
TK_MOUSE = {1: "mouse_left", 2: "mouse_middle", 3: "mouse_right"}  # Tk's button numbers on Windows
NICE = {"mouse_left": "Left click", "mouse_right": "Right click", "mouse_middle": "Middle click",
        "bracketleft": "[", "bracketright": "]", "comma": ",", "period": ".", "semicolon": ";", "minus": "-",
        "equals": "=", "quote": "'", "grave": "`", "backslash": "\\", "slash": "/"}
LABELS = {"JAB": "Jab", "HOOK": "Hook", "UPPERCUT": "Uppercut", "CROSS": "Cross (right glove)",
          "BLOCK": "Block", "DUCK": "Duck", "SLIP LEFT": "Slip left", "SLIP RIGHT": "Slip right"}


def key_from_tk(keysym):
    """A Tk key name (event.keysym) -> our key name, or None if it cannot be sent to a game."""
    k = keysym.lower()
    if len(k) == 1 and k in gi.SCAN_CODES:
        return k
    if k.startswith("f") and k[1:].isdigit() and k in gi.SCAN_CODES:
        return k
    return TK_KEYS.get(k)


def nice(key):
    return "-" if not key else NICE.get(key, key.upper() if len(key) == 1 else key.capitalize())


def problems(mapping):
    """Warnings for the editor: clashing binds, and binds on the tools' own hotkeys."""
    out = []
    groups = [("normal", mapping.taps), ("tracking", mapping.tracking_taps)]
    for name, taps in groups:
        seen = {}
        for action, key in [*taps.items(), *mapping.holds.items()]:  # defence is active in both modes
            if key in seen:
                out.append(f"{nice(key)} is bound to both {LABELS.get(seen[key], seen[key])} and "
                           f"{LABELS.get(action, action)} ({name} + defence can be active together)")
            seen.setdefault(key, action)
    for key in sorted({*mapping.taps.values(), *mapping.tracking_taps.values(), *mapping.holds.values()}):
        if key in HOTKEYS:
            out.append(f"{nice(key)} is also the tools' {HOTKEYS[key]} hotkey")
    return sorted(set(out))


def load_or_default(path):
    if os.path.exists(path):

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys

import game_input as gi

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DEFAULT_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "mappings", "controls.json")
HOTKEYS = {"f7": "calibrate", "f8": "key output on/off", "f9": "quit", "f11": "full screen",
           "bracketleft": "confidence down", "bracketright": "confidence up", "period": "start/pause"}
TK_KEYS = {
    "space": "space", "return": "enter", "tab": "tab", "backspace": "backspace", "caps_lock": "capslock",
    "shift_l": "shift", "shift_r": "shift", "control_l": "ctrl", "control_r": "ctrl", "alt_l": "alt", "alt_r": "alt",
    "up": "up", "down": "down", "left": "left", "right": "right", "comma": "comma", "period": "period",
    "semicolon": "semicolon", "minus": "minus", "equal": "equals", "bracketleft": "bracketleft",
    "bracketright": "bracketright", "apostrophe": "quote", "grave": "grave", "backslash": "backslash",
    "slash": "slash", "insert": "insert", "delete": "delete", "home": "home", "end": "end",
    "prior": "pageup", "next": "pagedown",
}
TK_MOUSE = {1: "mouse_left", 2: "mouse_middle", 3: "mouse_right"}  # Tk's button numbers on Windows
NICE = {"mouse_left": "Left click", "mouse_right": "Right click", "mouse_middle": "Middle click",
        "bracketleft": "[", "bracketright": "]", "comma": ",", "period": ".", "semicolon": ";", "minus": "-",
        "equals": "=", "quote": "'", "grave": "`", "backslash": "\\", "slash": "/"}
LABELS = {"JAB": "Jab", "HOOK": "Hook", "UPPERCUT": "Uppercut", "CROSS": "Cross (right glove)",
          "BLOCK": "Block", "DUCK": "Duck", "SLIP LEFT": "Slip left", "SLIP RIGHT": "Slip right"}


def key_from_tk(keysym):
    """A Tk key name (event.keysym) -> our key name, or None if it cannot be sent to a game."""
    k = keysym.lower()
    if len(k) == 1 and k in gi.SCAN_CODES:
        return k
    if k.startswith("f") and k[1:].isdigit() and k in gi.SCAN_CODES:
        return k
    return TK_KEYS.get(k)


def nice(key):
    return "-" if not key else NICE.get(key, key.upper() if len(key) == 1 else key.capitalize())


def problems(mapping):
    """Warnings for the editor: clashing binds, and binds on the tools' own hotkeys."""
    out = []
    groups = [("normal", mapping.taps), ("tracking", mapping.tracking_taps)]
    for name, taps in groups:
        seen = {}
        for action, key in [*taps.items(), *mapping.holds.items()]:  # defence is active in both modes
            if key in seen:
                out.append(f"{nice(key)} is bound to both {LABELS.get(seen[key], seen[key])} and "
                           f"{LABELS.get(action, action)} ({name} + defence can be active together)")
            seen.setdefault(key, action)
    for key in sorted({*mapping.taps.values(), *mapping.tracking_taps.values(), *mapping.holds.values()}):
        if key in HOTKEYS:
            out.append(f"{nice(key)} is also the tools' {HOTKEYS[key]} hotkey")
    return sorted(set(out))


def load_or_default(path):
    if os.path.exists(path):
        return gi.Mapping.load(path)
    return gi.Mapping.load(DEFAULT_PATH) if os.path.exists(DEFAULT_PATH) else gi.Mapping({})


class Editor:
    def __init__(self, root, path):
        import tkinter as tk
        from tkinter import ttk
        self.tk, self.ttk, self.root, self.path = tk, ttk, root, path
        self.mapping = load_or_default(path)
        self.capturing = None   # (set name, action) waiting for a key
        self.buttons = {}       # (set name, action) -> bind button
        self.holds = {}         # (set name, action) -> IntVar of hold ms
        root.title("Boxing controls")
        root.minsize(720, 520)
        self._build()
        root.bind_all("<KeyPress>", self._on_key, add="+")
        root.bind_all("<ButtonPress>", self._on_mouse, add="+")
        self.refresh()

    # --- layout ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _build(self):
        tk, ttk = self.tk, self.ttk
        top = ttk.Frame(self.root, padding=8)
        top.pack(fill="x")
        self.path_label = ttk.Label(top, text="")
        self.path_label.pack(side="left")
        ttk.Button(top, text="Save as...", command=self.save_as).pack(side="right")
        ttk.Button(top, text="Open...", command=self.open).pack(side="right", padx=4)
        ttk.Button(top, text="Reset to defaults", command=self.reset).pack(side="right")

        body = ttk.Frame(self.root, padding=(8, 0))
        body.pack(fill="both", expand=True)
        self._bind_group(body, "Normal  (glove button up)", "normal", gi.PUNCHES, True).grid(row=0, column=0, sticky="nsew", padx=4, pady=4)
        self._bind_group(body, "Tracking  (glove button held)", "tracking", gi.PUNCHES, True).grid(row=0, column=1, sticky="nsew", padx=4, pady=4)
        self._bind_group(body, "Defence  (camera)", "defence", gi.DEFENCE, False).grid(row=1, column=0, sticky="nsew", padx=4, pady=4)
        self._aim_group(body).grid(row=1, column=1, sticky="nsew", padx=4, pady=4)
        body.columnconfigure((0, 1), weight=1)

        self.status = ttk.Label(self.root, text="", padding=8, foreground="#555")
        self.status.pack(fill="x")
        self.warnings = tk.Label(self.root, text="", padx=8, pady=4, fg="#b00", justify="left", anchor="w")
        self.warnings.pack(fill="x")

    def _bind_group(self, parent, title, name, actions, with_hold):
        ttk = self.ttk
        box = ttk.LabelFrame(parent, text=title, padding=8)
        ttk.Label(box, text="Action").grid(row=0, column=0, sticky="w")
        ttk.Label(box, text="Bind").grid(row=0, column=1)
        if with_hold:
            ttk.Label(box, text="Hold (ms)").grid(row=0, column=3)
        for i, action in enumerate(actions, start=1):
            ttk.Label(box, text=LABELS.get(action, action)).grid(row=i, column=0, sticky="w", pady=2)
            b = ttk.Button(box, width=16, command=lambda n=name, a=action: self.start_capture(n, a))
            b.grid(row=i, column=1, padx=4)
            self.buttons[(name, action)] = b
            ttk.Button(box, text="x", width=2, command=lambda n=name, a=action: self.set_bind(n, a, None)).grid(row=i, column=2)
            if with_hold:
                var = self.tk.IntVar()
                spin = ttk.Spinbox(box, from_=10, to=2000, increment=10, width=6, textvariable=var,
                                   command=lambda n=name, a=action: self.set_hold(n, a))
                spin.bind("<FocusOut>", lambda e, n=name, a=action: self.set_hold(n, a))
                spin.bind("<Return>", lambda e, n=name, a=action: self.set_hold(n, a))
                spin.grid(row=i, column=3, padx=4)
                self.holds[(name, action)] = var
        return box

    def _aim_group(self, parent):
        tk, ttk = self.tk, self.ttk
        box = ttk.LabelFrame(parent, text="Steering  (right hand, while the button is held)", padding=8)
        self.aim_vars = {}
        self.aim_vars["mode"] = tk.StringVar()
        row = ttk.Frame(box)
        row.grid(row=0, column=0, columnspan=3, sticky="w")
        ttk.Radiobutton(row, text="Speed (thumbstick)", value="speed", variable=self.aim_vars["mode"],
                        command=self.aim_changed).pack(side="left")
        ttk.Radiobutton(row, text="Position (trackpad)", value="position", variable=self.aim_vars["mode"],
                        command=self.aim_changed).pack(side="left", padx=8)
        sliders = [("speed", "Speed (px/s)", 100, 5000, "speed"), ("curve", "Curve", 1.0, 3.0, "speed"),
                   ("dead_zone", "Dead zone", 0.0, 0.25, "speed"),
                   ("position_gain", "Sensitivity (px per shoulder width)", 200, 6000, "position"),
                   ("vertical_scale", "Vertical vs horizontal", 0.25, 2.0, None)]
        self.sliders = {}
        for i, (key, text, lo, hi, mode) in enumerate(sliders, start=1):
            var = tk.DoubleVar()
            self.aim_vars[key] = var
            label = ttk.Label(box, text=text)
            label.grid(row=i, column=0, sticky="w")
            scale = ttk.Scale(box, from_=lo, to=hi, variable=var, length=200,
                              command=lambda _v: self.aim_changed(save=False))
            scale.bind("<ButtonRelease-1>", lambda e: self.aim_changed())
            scale.grid(row=i, column=1, padx=4)
            value = ttk.Label(box, width=6)
            value.grid(row=i, column=2)
            self.sliders[key] = (label, scale, value, mode)
        for j, (key, text) in enumerate([("invert_y", "Invert up/down"),
                                         ("block_while_tracking", "Camera BLOCK works while tracking")]):
            var = tk.BooleanVar()
            self.aim_vars[key] = var
            ttk.Checkbutton(box, text=text, variable=var, command=self.aim_changed).grid(
                row=len(sliders) + 1 + j, column=0, columnspan=3, sticky="w")
        return box

    # --- state -> screen ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _set(self, name):
        m = self.mapping
        return {"normal": (m.taps, m.tap_s), "tracking": (m.tracking_taps, m.tracking_s), "defence": (m.holds, None)}[name]

    def refresh(self):
        for (name, action), button in self.buttons.items():
            keys, _ = self._set(name)
            waiting = self.capturing == (name, action)
            button.configure(text="press a key or click..." if waiting else nice(keys.get(action)))
        for (name, action), var in self.holds.items():
            _, hold = self._set(name)
            var.set(round(1000 * hold.get(action, 0.05 if name == "normal" else 0.15)))
        aim = self.mapping.aim
        for key, var in self.aim_vars.items():
            var.set(aim[key])
        self._show_aim_values()
        self.path_label.configure(text=f"Editing {os.path.relpath(self.path, ROOT)}")
        found = problems(self.mapping)
        self.warnings.configure(text="\n".join("Warning: " + p for p in found))

    def _show_aim_values(self):
        mode = self.aim_vars["mode"].get()
        for key, (label, scale, value, only) in self.sliders.items():
            v = self.aim_vars[key].get()
            value.configure(text=f"{v:.0f}" if v >= 100 else f"{v:.2f}")
            state = "!disabled" if only in (None, mode) else "disabled"
            scale.state([state])
            label.state([state])

    # --- editing --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def start_capture(self, name, action):
        self.capturing = (name, action)
        self.say(f"Press a key or click a mouse button for {LABELS.get(action, action)} ({name}). Esc cancels.")
        self.refresh()

    def _on_key(self, event):
        if self.capturing is None:
            return
        if event.keysym == "Escape":
            self.capturing = None
            self.say("Cancelled.")
            self.refresh()
            return "break"
        key = key_from_tk(event.keysym)
        if key is None:
            self.say(f"{event.keysym} cannot be sent to a game. Try another key.")
            return "break"
        name, action = self.capturing
        self.capturing = None
        self.set_bind(name, action, key)
        return "break"

    def _on_mouse(self, event):
        if self.capturing is None or event.num not in TK_MOUSE:
            return
        name, action = self.capturing
        self.capturing = None
        self.set_bind(name, action, TK_MOUSE[event.num])
        return "break"

    def set_bind(self, name, action, key):
        keys, hold = self._set(name)
        if key:
            keys[action] = key
            if hold is not None:
                hold.setdefault(action, 0.05 if name == "normal" else 0.15)
        else:
            keys.pop(action, None)
        self.capturing = None
        self.save(f"{LABELS.get(action, action)} ({name}) = {nice(key)}")

    def set_hold(self, name, action):
        try:
            ms = int(self.holds[(name, action)].get())
        except (ValueError, self.tk.TclError):
            return
        _, hold = self._set(name)
        ms = max(10, min(2000, ms))
        if round(1000 * hold.get(action, -1)) != ms:
            hold[action] = ms / 1000
            self.save(f"{LABELS.get(action, action)} ({name}) holds {ms} ms")

    def aim_changed(self, save=True):
        aim = self.mapping.aim
        for key, var in self.aim_vars.items():
            v = var.get()
            aim[key] = round(v) if key in ("speed", "position_gain") else (round(v, 2) if isinstance(v, float) else v)
        self._show_aim_values()
        if save:
            self.save("steering settings")

    # --- files ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def save(self, what=""):
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(self.path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
        tmp = self.path + ".tmp"
        self.mapping.save(tmp)
        os.replace(tmp, self.path)  # so punch_live never reads a half-written file
        self.say(f"Saved {what}. A running punch_live.py picks it up within a second.")
        self.refresh()

    def say(self, text):
        self.status.configure(text=text)

    def open(self):
        from tkinter import filedialog
        path = filedialog.askopenfilename(initialdir=os.path.dirname(self.path), filetypes=[("Controls", "*.json")])
        if path:
            self.path, self.mapping = path, load_or_default(path)
            self.say(f"Opened {os.path.basename(path)}")
            self.refresh()

    def save_as(self):
        from tkinter import filedialog
        path = filedialog.asksaveasfilename(initialdir=os.path.dirname(self.path), defaultextension=".json",
                                            filetypes=[("Controls", "*.json")])
        if path:
            self.path = path
            self.save(f"as {os.path.basename(path)}")

    def reset(self):
        self.mapping = gi.Mapping.load(DEFAULT_PATH) if os.path.abspath(self.path) != os.path.abspath(DEFAULT_PATH) \
            else gi.Mapping(json.loads(json.dumps(DEFAULTS)))
        self.save("the default controls")


DEFAULTS = {
    "game": "Default controls: edit with python controls_editor.py",
    "normal": {"JAB": {"bind": "j", "hold_ms": 50}, "HOOK": {"bind": "h", "hold_ms": 50},
               "UPPERCUT": {"bind": "u", "hold_ms": 50}, "CROSS": {"bind": "k", "hold_ms": 50}},
    "tracking": {"JAB": {"bind": "mouse_left", "hold_ms": 150}, "HOOK": {"bind": "mouse_right", "hold_ms": 150},
                 "UPPERCUT": {"bind": "mouse_middle", "hold_ms": 150}},
    "defence": {"BLOCK": "w", "DUCK": "s", "SLIP LEFT": "a", "SLIP RIGHT": "d"},
    "aim": dict(gi.AIM_DEFAULTS),
}


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--mapping", default=DEFAULT_PATH, help="controls file to edit")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    import tkinter as tk
    root = tk.Tk()
    Editor(root, os.path.abspath(args.mapping))
    root.mainloop()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Tracking mode (glove button + right-hand steering), the three-set controls file and its editor.

Run with: python -m unittest discover tests
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import unittest

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

import controls_editor  # noqa: E402
import game_input as gi  # noqa: E402
import hand_aim  # noqa: E402
import punch_live  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


class RecordingKeyboard(gi.Keyboard):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.log, self.moved = [], np.zeros(2)

    def _send(self, key, is_down):
        self.log.append((key, is_down, time.time()))

    def _move(self, dx, dy):
        self.moved += (dx, dy)


def game(data=None):
    mapping = gi.Mapping(data or gi.Mapping.load(os.path.join(ROOT, "mappings", "controls.json")).to_dict())
    return gi.GameInput(mapping, RecordingKeyboard())


def body(wrist_right=0.0, wrist_up=0.0):
    """MediaPipe-style world landmarks for a boxer facing the camera (left shoulder at +x, y down),
    with the right wrist moved by (right, up) shoulder widths from the right shoulder."""
    world = np.zeros((33, 3))
    world[11], world[12] = [0.2, -0.5, 0.0], [-0.2, -0.5, 0.0]   # shoulder width 0.4 m
    world[16] = world[12] + 0.4 * np.array([-wrist_right, -wrist_up, 0.0])  # boxer's right = -x, up = -y
    return world, np.ones(33)


class ControlsFile(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_old_format_still_loads(self):
        m = gi.Mapping.load(os.path.join(ROOT, "mappings", "browser_boxing.json"))
        self.assertEqual(m.taps["JAB"], "j")
        self.assertEqual(m.holds["BLOCK"], "w")
        self.assertEqual(m.tracking_taps, {})

    def test_default_controls_have_three_sets(self):
        m = gi.Mapping.load(os.path.join(ROOT, "mappings", "controls.json"))
        self.assertEqual(m.tracking_taps, {"JAB": "mouse_left", "HOOK": "mouse_right", "UPPERCUT": "mouse_middle"})
        self.assertAlmostEqual(m.tracking_s["JAB"], 0.15)
        self.assertEqual(m.aim["mode"], "speed")
        self.assertFalse(m.aim["block_while_tracking"])

    def test_save_and_load_round_trip_and_unbound(self):
        m = gi.Mapping({"normal": {"JAB": "j", "HOOK": ""}, "tracking": {"JAB": {"bind": "mouse_left", "hold_ms": 200}}})
        self.assertNotIn("HOOK", m.taps)  # an empty bind is unbound
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            path = os.path.join(tmp, "c.json")
            m.save(path)
            back = gi.Mapping.load(path)
        self.assertEqual(back.tracking_taps["JAB"], "mouse_left")
        self.assertAlmostEqual(back.tracking_s["JAB"], 0.2)

    def test_mouse_buttons_are_bindable_and_unknown_keys_are_not(self):
        self.assertEqual(gi.check_key("Mouse_Left"), "mouse_left")
